articles.title: The predictive rule of the urn
articles.statement:
`P(X₀ ∈ A₀, …, X_n ∈ A_n)` is the integral over
`A₀ × ⋯ × A_{n-1}` of the predictive probability `(α H(A_n) + #{i < n | xᵢ ∈ A_n}) / (α + n)`.

articles.title: The ties of the Blackwell–MacQueen urn follow the Chinese restaurant process
articles.statement:
**The ties of the Blackwell–MacQueen urn follow the Chinese restaurant process** (Pitman
2006, §3.1): for an atomless base measure, the partition of the first `n` draws into groups of
equal values has the law `α^{|π|} ∏_{B ∈ π} (|B| - 1)! / α^{(n)}`.

articles.title: Blackwell–MacQueen urn
articles.statement:
The **Blackwell–MacQueen urn** with parameter `α` and base measure `H`: the joint law of the
first `n` draws, where draw `n` has law `polyaUrnPredictive α H xs` given the previous draws
`xs` (Blackwell–MacQueen 1973).

articles.title: Tie partition after forgetting the last draw
articles.statement: Forgetting the last draw restricts the tie partition to the earlier draws.

articles.title: Blackwell–MacQueen urn law is a probability measure
articles.statement: The urn law is a probability measure.

articles.title: Moments of the Dirichlet process for at most two draws
articles.statement:
For `n ≤ 2`,
`E[∏_{i<n} G(Aᵢ)] = P(X₀ ∈ A₀, …, X_{n-1} ∈ A_{n-1})` for the Blackwell–MacQueen urn. The case
`n ≥ 3` is the wanted `lintegral_dirichletProcess_prod`.

articles.title: Exchangeability of the Blackwell–MacQueen urn
articles.statement:
**Exchangeability of the Blackwell–MacQueen urn** (Blackwell–MacQueen 1973): relabeling the
draws by a permutation does not change their joint law.

articles.title: Measurability of the Pólya urn predictive law
articles.statement: The predictive law depends measurably on the previous draws.

articles.title: Measurability of the tie partition event
articles.statement: The event that the draws have a given tie partition is measurable.

articles.title: Blocks of the tie partition are classes of equal entries
articles.statement: Two indices lie in the same block of `tiePartition xs` iff the entries agree.

articles.title: Pólya urn predictive law is invariant under reordering
articles.statement: The predictive law does not depend on the order of the previous draws.

articles.title: Characterization of the tie partition
articles.statement: `tiePartition xs = π` iff equal entries are exactly the pairs in a common block of `π`.

articles.title: Last draw opens a new block iff it is new
articles.statement: Where the last draw sits: a new table iff it differs from all earlier draws.

articles.title: Last draw joins a block iff it matches that block
articles.statement: Where the last draw sits: at the table `B` iff it equals the earlier draws in `B`.

articles.title: Tie partition of a sequence of draws
articles.statement: The partition of the indices `{0, …, n-1}` into groups of equal entries of `xs`.

articles.title: Stick-breaking proportions lie in the unit interval almost surely
articles.statement: Almost surely every proportion is in `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: The Dirichlet-process weights sum to `1` almost surely
articles.statement:
**The Dirichlet-process weights sum to `1` almost surely** (Sethuraman 1994): the leftover
stick tends to `0`.

articles.title: Random stick-breaking weights sum to one almost surely
articles.statement:
If the expected leftover stick `∏_{j<k} (1 - E[βⱼ])` tends to `0`, the pieces sum to `1`
almost surely.

articles.title: Stick-breaking random measure is almost surely a probability measure
articles.statement: When the pieces sum to `1` almost surely, `G` is almost surely a probability measure.

articles.title: Dirichlet process is almost surely a probability measure
articles.statement: A Dirichlet process is almost surely a probability measure.

articles.title: Beta law is concentrated on the unit interval
articles.statement: The Beta law is concentrated on `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Random stick-breaking weights lie in the unit interval almost surely
articles.statement: Almost surely every piece is in `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Leftover stick is decreasing
articles.statement: The leftover stick shrinks for proportions in `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Dirichlet process
articles.statement:
The **Dirichlet process** `DP(α, H)` as a law on `Measure X`, defined as the law of
Sethuraman's (1994) stick-breaking measure with `Beta(1, α)` proportions and `H` atoms.
Ferguson's (1973) definition by Dirichlet marginals is the wanted statement
`map_dirichletProcess_partition`.

articles.title: Random measure of a stick-breaking process
articles.statement: The random measure `G = ∑ₖ πₖ δ_{θₖ}`.

articles.title: Law of each proportion in Sethuraman's space
articles.statement: Each proportion of the canonical space has law `Beta(1, α)`.

articles.title: Law of each atom in Sethuraman's space
articles.statement: Each atom of the canonical space has law `H`.

articles.title: Stick-breaking weights sum to one iff the leftover stick tends to zero
articles.statement: For proportions in `[0, 1]`, the pieces sum to `1` iff the leftover stick tends to `0`.

articles.title: Second moment of $1 - X$ under $\mathrm{Beta}(1, \alpha)$
articles.statement: `E[(1 - x)²] = α / (α + 2)` under `Beta(1, α)`.

articles.title: Expected leftover stick is the product of expected complements
Mean of a Dirichlet-process weight
articles.statement:
**Mean of a Dirichlet-process weight** (Sethuraman 1994): `E[πₖ] = αᵏ / (1 + α)^(k+1)`
(`α^{k-1} / (1 + α)^k` for Sethuraman's `π_k`, indexed from `1`).

articles.title: Second moment of a stick-breaking weight
articles.statement: `E[πₖ²] = E[βₖ²] ∏_{j<k} E[(1 - βⱼ)²]`.

articles.title: Mean of a stick-breaking weight
Mean proportion of a Dirichlet process
articles.statement: The proportions of a Dirichlet process have mean `1 / (1 + α)`.

articles.title: Sethuraman's canonical model is a Dirichlet process
articles.statement: The canonical model is a Dirichlet process.

articles.title: Sethuraman's stick-breaking representation of the Dirichlet process
articles.statement:
**Sethuraman's stick-breaking representation of the Dirichlet process** `DP(α, H)`
(Sethuraman 1994): the proportions are `Beta(1, α)` with `α > 0`. We take this construction as
the definition of `DP(α, H)`; Sethuraman's theorem that it has Ferguson's Dirichlet marginals
is recorded in `WantedExt/Probability/DirichletProcessWanted.lean`.

articles.title: Base measure of a stick-breaking process is a probability measure
articles.statement: The base measure is a probability measure.

articles.title: Blackwell–MacQueen predictive law is a probability measure
articles.statement: The predictive law is a probability measure for `α > 0` and a probability measure `H`.

articles.title: Stick-breaking measure is a probability measure
articles.statement: The stick-breaking measure is a probability measure when the pieces sum to `1`.

articles.title: Mean of the Dirichlet process
articles.statement: **Mean of the Dirichlet process**, law form: `∫ ν(A) dDP(α, H)(ν) = H(A)`.

articles.title: The moments of the Dirichlet process are the Blackwell–MacQueen urn
articles.statement:
**The moments of the Dirichlet process are the Blackwell–MacQueen urn** (Blackwell–MacQueen
1973): `E[∏ᵢ G(Aᵢ)] = P(X₀ ∈ A₀, …, X_{n-1} ∈ A_{n-1})` for the urn's first `n` draws.

articles.title: Mean of the Dirichlet process
articles.statement: **Mean of the Dirichlet process** (Ferguson 1973): `E[G(A)] = H(A)`.

articles.title: Mean of the random measure
articles.statement:
If the pieces sum to `1` almost surely, then
`E[G(A)] = H(A)` for every measurable `A`.

articles.title: Mixed second moment of the Dirichlet process
articles.statement:
**Mixed second moment of the Dirichlet process** (Ferguson 1973):
`E[G(A) G(B)] = (α H(A) H(B) + H(A ∩ B)) / (α + 1)`.

articles.title: The Blackwell–MacQueen urn for two draws
articles.statement:
**The Blackwell–MacQueen urn for two draws** (Blackwell–MacQueen 1973): if `X₁, X₂` are
i.i.d. draws from a Dirichlet process `G`, then `P(X₁ ∈ A, X₂ ∈ B) = E[G(A) G(B)]` equals
`∫_A P(X₂ ∈ B | X₁ = x) dH(x)` with the predictive law
`polyaUrnPredictive α H ![x] = (α H + δₓ) / (α + 1)`.

articles.title: Mixed second moment of the random measure
articles.statement:
If the pieces sum to `1` almost surely, then
`E[G(A) G(B)] = (1 - s) H(A) H(B) + s H(A ∩ B)` with `s = ∑ₖ E[πₖ²]` (`sumSqWeight`, at most
`1` under this hypothesis): two draws from `G` pick the same piece with probability `s`, and
otherwise land on two independent atoms.

articles.title: Finite-dimensional marginals of the Dirichlet process
articles.statement:
**Finite-dimensional marginals of the Dirichlet process** (Ferguson 1973, §3; Sethuraman
1994, Theorem 3.4): on a measurable partition `A₀, …, A_m` of `X` with `H(Aᵢ) > 0`, the vector
`(G(A₀), …, G(A_m))` has the Dirichlet law `Dir(α H(A₀), …, α H(A_m))`.

articles.title: Measurability of the random stick-breaking measure
articles.statement: The random measure depends measurably on `ω`.

articles.title: Measurability of the stick-breaking measure in its parameters
articles.statement:
The stick-breaking measure depends measurably (for the Giry σ-algebra on `Measure X`) on
the proportions and the atoms.

articles.title: Measurability of the random stick-breaking weights
articles.statement: The pieces are measurable.

articles.title: Law of the proportion coordinate of Sethuraman's space
articles.statement: The proportion coordinate of the canonical space has law `⊗ₖ Beta(1, α)`.

articles.title: Law of the atom coordinate of Sethuraman's space
articles.statement: The atom coordinate of the canonical space has law `⊗ₖ H`.

articles.title: Predictive probability of a set in the Blackwell–MacQueen urn
articles.statement: The predictive probability of a measurable set: `(α H(A) + #{i | xᵢ ∈ A}) / (α + n)`.

articles.title: Blackwell–MacQueen urn predictive law
articles.statement:
The predictive law in the **Blackwell–MacQueen urn**: after observations `x₀, …, x_{n-1}`,
the next observation has law `(α H + ∑ᵢ δ_{xᵢ}) / (α + n)`. It is a probability measure for
`α > 0` and a probability measure `H` (`isProbabilityMeasure_polyaUrnPredictive`); outside that
domain the definition is total but meaningless (e.g. `α = n = 0` gives the zero measure).

articles.title: Random leftover stick
articles.statement: The random leftover stick `∏_{j<k} (1 - βⱼ)`.

articles.title: Ferguson's conjugacy
articles.statement:
**Ferguson's conjugacy** (Ferguson 1973, Theorem 1): given `n` observations `xs` from
`G ∼ DP(α, H)`, the posterior of `G` is `DP(α + n, (α H + ∑ᵢ δ_{xsᵢ}) / (α + n))`. Stated as
the disintegration `P(G ∈ S, X₀ ∈ A₀, …) = ∫_{∏ Aᵢ} DP(α + n, posterior base)(S) dP(xs)` over
the urn law of the observations.

articles.title: Sethuraman's canonical probability space
articles.statement:
The product probability space `(ℕ → ℝ) × (ℕ → X)` carrying i.i.d. `Beta(1, α)` proportions
and, independently, i.i.d. `H` atoms.

articles.title: Sethuraman's construction
articles.statement:
**Sethuraman's construction** on the canonical space: the coordinates of the two factors are
the proportions and the atoms.

articles.title: Stick-breaking measure has total mass at most one
articles.statement: The stick-breaking measure has total mass at most `1` for proportions in `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Mass of a set under the stick-breaking measure
articles.statement: The mass of a measurable set under the stick-breaking measure.

articles.title: Stick-breaking measure
articles.statement:
The discrete measure `∑ₖ πₖ δ_{θₖ}` with the stick-breaking weights `πₖ = stickWeight b k`
(negative weights, which do not occur for proportions in `[0, 1]`, are read as `0`).

articles.title: Stick-breaking process
articles.statement:
A **stick-breaking process** on the probability space `(Ω, μ)`: independent proportions
`βₖ ∈ [0, 1]` (almost surely, with arbitrary laws), i.i.d. atoms `atom k` with law `H`, and the
proportion sequence independent of the atom sequence. Ishwaran–James (2001) take
`βₖ ∼ Beta(aₖ, bₖ)`; Sethuraman's Dirichlet process is `IsDirichlet`.

articles.title: Leftover stick lies in the unit interval
articles.statement: The leftover stick is in `[0, 1]` for proportions in `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Leftover stick in stick breaking
articles.statement:
The stick left after breaking off the first `k` pieces at proportions `b`:
`∏_{j<k} (1 - bⱼ)`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of stick-breaking weights
articles.statement: The pieces are nonnegative for proportions in `[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Stick-breaking weights
articles.statement: The `k`-th piece of a stick broken at proportions `b`: `bₖ ∏_{j<k} (1 - bⱼ)`.

articles.title: Stick-breaking pieces and leftover make up the whole stick
articles.statement:
The first `n` pieces and the leftover stick make up the whole stick. Holds for all real
`b`.

articles.title: Probability that two Dirichlet process draws pick the same piece
articles.statement:
Two draws from a Dirichlet process pick the same piece with probability `1 / (1 + α)`:
`∑ₖ E[πₖ²] = 1 / (1 + α)`. This is the probability that the second customer of the Chinese
restaurant process with parameter `α` joins the first one's table.

articles.title: Expected sum of squared stick-breaking weights
articles.statement:
`∑ₖ E[πₖ²]`: given `G`, two independent draws from `G` pick the same piece `k` with
probability `∑ₖ πₖ²`. For an atomless base measure the atoms are almost surely distinct, so this
is also the probability that the two draws coincide (not used here).

articles.title: Variance of the Dirichlet process
articles.statement:
**Variance of the Dirichlet process** (Ferguson 1973):
`Var(G(A)) = H(A) (1 - H(A)) / (α + 1)`.

articles.title: Random stick-breaking weight
articles.statement: The random piece `πₖ = βₖ ∏_{j<k} (1 - βⱼ)`.

articles.title: Galton–Watson extinction criterion
articles.statement:
Extinction is certain iff the mean offspring number is at most `1`, provided the offspring
number is not almost surely `1` (Athreya–Ney 1972, ch. I).

articles.title: Extinction probability of a Galton–Watson process
articles.statement:
The extinction probability `q = sup_n P(Z_n = 0)`, the limit of the probabilities of
extinction by generation `n` (`tendsto_law_real_zero`). On a path space carrying the process the
events `{Z_n = 0}` increase with `n` (`0` is absorbing), so `q` is the probability of eventual
extinction; this file describes the process through its generation laws and does not construct
the path space.

articles.title: Least fixed point equals one iff mean offspring is at most one
articles.statement:
The least fixed point is `1` iff the mean offspring number is at most `1`, provided the
offspring number is not almost surely `1` (Athreya–Ney 1972, ch. I).

articles.title: Extinction probability is the least fixed point
articles.statement:
The extinction probability is the least fixed point of the offspring generating function
in `[0, 1]` (Athreya–Ney 1972, ch. I).

articles.title: Limit of generating-function iterates is the least fixed point
articles.statement:
`sup_n f^[n](0)` is the least fixed point of `f` in `[0, 1]`
(Athreya–Ney 1972, ch. I).

articles.title: Iterates of the offspring generating function stay in (0, 1)
articles.statement:
The iterates `f^[n](s)` of the offspring generating function stay in `[0, 1]` for
`s ∈ [0, 1]`.

articles.title: Probability of extinction by generation n
Generation-size law of a Galton–Watson process
articles.statement:
The law of the generation size `Z_n` of the Galton–Watson process with offspring law `ν`
started from one individual: `Z_0 = 1` and, given `Z_n = z`, `Z_{n+1}` has law `ν^{∗z}`
(`Measure.convPow ν z`).

articles.title: Mean generation size of a Galton–Watson process
articles.statement: The mean generation size is `E Z_n = m ^ n` (Athreya–Ney 1972, ch. I).

articles.title: Mean offspring number
articles.statement: The mean offspring number `m = E ξ = ∑ k ν{k} ∈ [0, ∞]`.

articles.title: Iterates of the generating function at zero are nondecreasing
articles.statement: The iterates `f^[n](0)` of the offspring generating function are non-decreasing.

articles.title: Extinction by generation n is nondecreasing in n
articles.statement: `P(Z_n = 0)` is non-decreasing in `n`.

articles.title: Generating function of the n-th generation size
articles.statement:
The generating function of `Z_n` is the `n`-th iterate of the offspring generating
function on `[0, 1]` (Athreya–Ney 1972, ch. I).

articles.title: Extinction by generation n converges to the extinction probability
articles.statement: `P(Z_n = 0)` converges to the extinction probability.

articles.title: Uniqueness of the extinction probability solving the backward equation
articles.statement:
The extinction probability is the only `[0, 1]`-valued solution `q` on `[0, ∞)` of the
backward equation `q' = d - (b + d) q + b q²` with `q 0 = 0`.

articles.title: Kendall's extinction probability for the birth–death process
articles.statement:
Kendall's extinction probability `α t = P(X t = 0 | X 0 = 1)` of the linear birth–death
process with per-capita birth rate `b` and death rate `d`: `d (E - 1) / (b E - d)` with
`E = exp ((b - d) t)` if `b ≠ d`, and `b t / (1 + b t)` if `b = d`. Meaningful for `0 ≤ b`,
`0 ≤ d`, `0 ≤ t`.

articles.title: Kendall's geometric tail ratio
articles.statement:
Kendall's ratio `β t` of the geometric tail of the law of `X t`: `b (E - 1) / (b E - d)`
with `E = exp ((b - d) t)` if `b ≠ d`, and `b t / (1 + b t)` if `b = d`.

articles.title: Backward Kolmogorov equation for the extinction probability
articles.statement:
Backward Kolmogorov equation for the extinction probability:
`α' = d - (b + d) α + b α²` (Karlin–Taylor 1975, ch. 4).

articles.title: Forward Kolmogorov equation for positive states
articles.statement:
Forward Kolmogorov equation for state `n + 1`:
`p_(n+1)' = b n p_n - (b + d) (n + 1) p_(n+1) + d (n + 2) p_(n+2)`.

articles.title: Forward Kolmogorov equation for the empty state
articles.statement: Forward Kolmogorov equation for state `0`: `p_0' = d p_1`.

articles.title: Mean population size of the linear birth–death process
articles.statement:
The mean population size at time `t` started from one individual is
`E[X t] = exp ((b - d) t)` (Kendall 1948; Bailey 1964, ch. 8).

articles.title: Kendall's probabilities sum to one
articles.statement: Kendall's probabilities sum to `1`: no mass escapes to infinity.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of Kendall's probabilities
articles.statement: Kendall's probabilities are nonnegative.

articles.title: Linear birth–death law at time zero
articles.statement: At time `0` the population is one individual: `prob b d 0 = δ₁`.

articles.title: Kendall's law of the linear birth–death process
articles.statement:
Kendall's law of the linear birth–death process at time `t` started from one individual:
`prob b d t 0 = α t` and `prob b d t (n + 1) = (1 - α t) (1 - β t) (β t) ^ n`.

articles.title: Certain extinction in the critical and subcritical cases
articles.statement: Critical and subcritical cases: if `b ≤ d` and `0 < d`, extinction is certain in the limit.

articles.title: Limiting extinction probability in the supercritical case
articles.statement: Supercritical case: if `d < b`, the extinction probability tends to `d / b`.

articles.title: Cycle lemma
articles.statement:
**Cycle lemma** (Dvoretzky–Motzkin 1947). If `x : Fin n → ℕ` satisfies `∑ x_i + k = n` with
`1 ≤ k`, then exactly `k` of the `n` cyclic shifts of `x` (counted by shift `r < n`) are
first-passage sequences.

articles.title: Borel law
articles.statement:
For Poisson(`r`) offspring and one ancestor, the total progeny satisfies
`P(T = n) = e^{-rn} (rn)^{n-1} / n!` for `n ≥ 1` (Borel 1942).

articles.title: Hitting weight of first-passage step sequences
articles.statement:
The weight `H_p(k, n) = ∑ ∏_i p(x_i)` over the step sequences with `∑ x_i + k = n` along
which the walk from `k` first hits `0` at time `n`. For `p(j) = P(ξ = j)` this is the
probability `P(T = n)` that the total progeny of `k` ancestors is `n`.

articles.title: First passage of the exploration walk
articles.statement:
The exploration walk started at `k` with steps `x_i - 1` stays positive at every time
`j < n`: `j < k + ∑_{i < j} x_i`. Together with `∑ x_i + k = n` this says that the walk first
hits `0` at time `n`.

articles.title: Mean total progeny equals $1/(1-m)$
articles.statement:
The mean total progeny is `(1 - m)⁻¹` in `[0, ∞]`: it is `1 / (1 - m)` for `m < 1` and `∞`
for `m ≥ 1` (`m` the mean offspring number).

articles.title: Mean total progeny of a Galton–Watson process
articles.statement:
The mean total progeny `∑_n E Z_n` of the Galton–Watson process started from one individual.
By Tonelli this is `E ∑_n Z_n` for any process with the generation laws `law ν n`.

articles.title: Probability of first passage at time n
articles.statement:
Under `ν^{⊗n}`, the event that the walk from `k` first hits `0` at time `n` has
measure `H_p(k, n)` with `p(j) = ν{j}`. When `ν` is a probability measure this is the
probability `P(T = n)`.

articles.title: Probability of the offspring walk event as a walk weight
articles.statement:
Under `ν^{⊗n}`, the event `ξ_1 + ⋯ + ξ_n + k = n` has measure `W_p(k, n)` with
`p(j) = ν{j}`. When `ν` is a probability measure this is the probability
`P(ξ_1 + ⋯ + ξ_n = n - k)`.

articles.title: Borel–Tanner law
articles.statement:
For Poisson(`r`) offspring and `k ≤ n` ancestors,
`n · P(T = n) = k e^{-rn} (rn)^{n-k} / (n-k)!` (Tanner 1961; Haight–Breuer 1960).

articles.title: Hitting-time theorem
articles.statement:
**Hitting-time theorem**, weighted form: `n · H_p(k, n) = k · W_p(k, n)` for every weight
`p` with values in a commutative semiring and all `k, n`. For probability weights this is the
hitting-time theorem of van der Hofstad–Keane (2008); the proof double counts cyclic shifts
with the cycle lemma.

articles.title: Otter–Dwass formula
articles.statement:
For i.i.d. offspring numbers with law `ν` and `k` ancestors,
the finite-measure identity
`n · P(T = n) = k · P(ξ_1 + ⋯ + ξ_n = n - k)` holds as an identity of event masses
(Otter 1949; Dwass 1969); the two sides are probabilities when `ν` is a probability
measure.

articles.title: Cyclic shift of a tuple
articles.statement: The cyclic shift `i ↦ x_{(i + r) mod n}` of a tuple.

articles.title: Walk weights for Poisson offspring
articles.statement:
For Poisson(`r`) step weights, `W_p(k, n) = e^{-rn} (rn)^{n-k} / (n-k)!` when `k ≤ n`:
the sum of `n` independent Poisson(`r`) variables is Poisson(`rn`).

articles.title: Walk weight of step sequences ending at zero
articles.statement:
The weight `W_p(k, n) = ∑ ∏_i p(x_i)` over the step sequences `x : Fin n → ℕ` with
`∑ x_i + k = n` (the walk from `k` is at `0` at time `n`). For `p(j) = P(ξ = j)` this is
`P(ξ_1 + ⋯ + ξ_n = n - k)` when `k ≤ n`, and `0` when `k > n`.

articles.title: Berry–Esseen theorem with constant 42
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be measurable, mutually
independent real random variables on a probability space, each with the same distribution as
$X_0$, where $X_0$ has a finite third moment, mean $\mathbb{E}[X_0] = 0$ and variance
$\sigma^2 = \operatorname{Var}(X_0) > 0$ with $\sigma > 0$. Write $\rho = \mathbb{E}|X_0|^3$,
$S_n = X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1}$, and $\Phi$ for the distribution function of the standard normal
distribution. Then for every $n \ge 1$ and every real $x$,

$$\left|\mathbb{P}\left(\frac{S_n}{\sqrt{n\sigma^2}} \le x\right) - \Phi(x)\right| \le
\frac{42\rho}{\sigma^3\sqrt{n}}.$$

Integrability of $X_0$ is not assumed separately, since on a probability space it follows from
the finite third moment.

articles.title: Berry–Esseen bound for finite sums
articles.statement:
Let $(\xi_j)_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ be measurable, mutually
independent real random variables on a probability space, and let $s$ be a finite set of indices
such that for each $j \in s$ the variable $\xi_j$ has a finite third moment and mean
$\mathbb{E}[\xi_j] = 0$, and such that $\sum_{j \in s} \mathbb{E}[\xi_j^2] = 1$. Write $\Phi$
for the distribution function of the standard normal distribution. If $\gamma \ge 0$ is a real
number with $\sum_{j \in s} \mathbb{E}|\xi_j|^3 \le \gamma$, then for every real $z$,

$$\left|\mathbb{P}\left(\sum_{j \in s} \xi_j \le z\right) - \Phi(z)\right| \le 42\gamma.$$

articles.title: Berry–Esseen theorem
articles.statement:
There is a constant $C > 0$ with the following property. Let
$X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be measurable, mutually independent real random variables on a probability
space, each with the same distribution as $X_0$, where $X_0$ is integrable and has a finite third
moment, mean $\mathbb{E}[X_0] = 0$ and variance $\sigma^2 = \operatorname{Var}(X_0) > 0$ with
$\sigma > 0$. Write $\rho = \mathbb{E}|X_0|^3$, $S_n = X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1}$, and $\Phi$ for the
distribution function of the standard normal distribution. Then for every $n \ge 1$ and every
real $x$,

$$\left|\mathbb{P}\left(\frac{S_n}{\sqrt{n\sigma^2}} \le x\right) - \Phi(x)\right| \le
\frac{C\rho}{\sigma^3\sqrt{n}}.$$

## Sources

- A. C. Berry, Trans. AMS 49 (1941), 122-136, DOI 10.2307/1990053; and C.-G. Esseen, Arkiv för Matematik, Astronomi och Fysik 28A no. 9 (1942), 1-19.

articles.title: Kolmogorov error bounds are uniform CDF bounds
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathbb{R}$, let
$n$ be a positive integer, let $F$ be the cumulative distribution function of the normalized law
of $\mu$ at $n$, and let $\Phi$ be the standard normal cumulative distribution function. Then for
every real $a$, the Kolmogorov error of $\mu$ at $n$ is at most $a$ if and only if
$|F(x) - \Phi(x)| \le a$ for every real $x$.

articles.title: The CDF errors are bounded above
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathbb{R}$, let $n$ be a
positive integer, let $F$ be the cumulative distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$
at $n$, and let $\Phi$ be the standard normal cumulative distribution function. Then the set
$\{|F(x) - \Phi(x)| : x \in \mathbb{R}\}$ is bounded above.

articles.title: Coordinates of the i.i.d. product are distributed like the original law
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a
standardized law on $\mathbb{R}$ and let $i$ be a natural number. The coordinate map
$\omega \mapsto \omega_i$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ under the i.i.d. product law of $\mu$ and
the identity map of $\mathbb{R}$ under $\mu$ are identically distributed.

articles.title: Coordinates of the i.i.d. product are independent
articles.statement:
If $\mu$ is a standardized law on
$\mathbb{R}$, then the coordinate maps $\omega \mapsto \omega_i$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$, for
$i \in \mathbb{N}$, are mutually independent under the i.i.d. product law of $\mu$.

articles.title: Coordinate laws of the i.i.d. product
articles.statement:
If $\mu$ is a standardized law on $\mathbb{R}$ and
$i$ is a natural number, then the pushforward of the i.i.d. product law of $\mu$ under the
coordinate map $\omega \mapsto \omega_i$ from $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ to $\mathbb{R}$ is $\mu$.

articles.title: The i.i.d. product of a standardized law is a probability measure
articles.statement:
If $\mu$ is a
standardized law on $\mathbb{R}$, then the i.i.d. product law of $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$
is a probability measure.

articles.title: I.i.d. product law
articles.statement:
For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the i.i.d. product law of $\mu$ is
the measure on the sequence space $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ that is the infinite product
$\mu^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$ of countably many copies of $\mu$ when $\mu$ is a probability measure,
and the zero measure otherwise.

articles.title: Standardized i.i.d. models
articles.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a measurable space with a measure $P$, and let
$(X_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be real-valued functions on $\Omega$. They form a standardized i.i.d.
model when $P$ is a probability measure, every $X_i$ is measurable, the $X_i$ are mutually
independent under $P$, every $X_i$ has the same law under $P$ as $X_0$, and $X_0$ has mean
$\int_\Omega X_0 \, dP = 0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment
$\int_\Omega |X_0|^3 \, dP < \infty$.

articles.title: Standardized laws with finite third moment
articles.statement:
A measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is a
standardized law when it is a probability measure with mean $\int x \, d\mu(x) = 0$ and variance
$1$, and has finite third absolute moment $\int |x|^3 \, d\mu(x) < \infty$.

articles.title: The joint law of a standardized i.i.d. model
articles.statement:
If $(X_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ is a
standardized i.i.d. model on a measurable space $\Omega$ with measure $P$, then the law under $P$
of the sequence map $\omega \mapsto (X_i(\omega))_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ from $\Omega$ to
$\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ equals the i.i.d. product law of the law of $X_0$ under $P$.

articles.title: The Kolmogorov error is at most one
articles.statement:
For every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and every
positive integer $n$, the Kolmogorov error of $\mu$ at $n$, that is
$\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_{\mu,n}(x) - \Phi(x)|$ where $F_{\mu,n}$ is Mathlib's cumulative
distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$ and $\Phi$ is the standard normal
cumulative distribution function, is at most $1$.

Here $F_{\mu,n}(x)$ is the mass the normalized law gives to $(-\infty, x]$ when $\mu$ is a
probability measure; otherwise the normalized law is the zero measure and $F_{\mu,n}$ is a
fixed but unspecified cumulative distribution function of some probability measure.

articles.title: The Kolmogorov error is nonnegative
articles.statement:
For every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and every
positive integer $n$, the Kolmogorov error of $\mu$ at $n$, that is
$\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_{\mu,n}(x) - \Phi(x)|$ where $F_{\mu,n}$ is Mathlib's cumulative
distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$ and $\Phi$ is the standard normal
cumulative distribution function, is nonnegative.

Here $F_{\mu,n}(x)$ is the mass the normalized law gives to $(-\infty, x]$ when $\mu$ is a
probability measure; otherwise the normalized law is the zero measure and $F_{\mu,n}$ is a
fixed but unspecified cumulative distribution function of some probability measure.

articles.title: Kolmogorov error
articles.statement:
For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and a positive integer $n$, the
Kolmogorov error of $\mu$ at $n$ is the real supremum
$\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_{\mu,n}(x) - \Phi(x)|$, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal
cumulative distribution function and $F_{\mu,n}$ is Mathlib's cumulative distribution function
of the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$. When $\mu$ is a probability measure, $F_{\mu,n}(x)$ is
the mass the normalized law gives to $(-\infty, x]$; otherwise the normalized law is the zero
measure and $F_{\mu,n}$ is a fixed but unspecified cumulative distribution function of some
probability measure, not the zero function.

The values $|F_{\mu,n}(x) - \Phi(x)|$ lie in $[0, 1]$, so the supremum is finite.

articles.title: Finite third absolute moment as an $L^3$ condition
articles.statement:
For every measure $\mu$ on
$\mathbb{R}$, the identity function $x \mapsto x$ belongs to $L^3(\mu)$ if and only if
the function $x \mapsto |x|^3$ is $\mu$-integrable.

articles.title: Standard normal CDF
articles.statement:
For $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $\Phi(x)$ is the value at $x$ of the
cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$, that
is, the probability that a standard normal random variable is at most $x$.

articles.title: CDF of the normalized sum
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a standardized law on $\mathbb{R}$
(a probability measure with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment), let $n$ be
a positive integer and let $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the cumulative distribution function of the
normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$, evaluated at $x$, equals the probability under the i.i.d. law
$\mu^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ of the event
$\{\omega \in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}} : (\omega_0 + \dots + \omega_{n-1})/\sqrt{n} \le x\}$.

articles.title: Normalized sums of an i.i.d. model have the canonical law
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a probability
measure on a measurable space $\Omega$ and let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random variables on
$\Omega$ that are measurable, independent and identically distributed under $P$, with $X_0$ of
mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment. Then for every positive integer $n$,
the law under $P$ of $(X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1})/\sqrt{n}$ equals the normalized law at $n$ of the
law of $X_0$.

articles.title: The normalized law with one summand
articles.statement:
For every standardized law $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$
(a probability measure with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment), the
normalized law of $\mu$ at $n = 1$ is $\mu$ itself.

articles.title: The normalized law is a probability measure
articles.statement:
For every standardized law $\mu$ on
$\mathbb{R}$ (a probability measure with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute
moment) and every positive integer $n$, the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$ is a probability
measure.

articles.title: Law of the normalized sum
articles.statement:
For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and a positive integer
$n$, the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$ is the pushforward of the i.i.d. law of $\mu$ on
$\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ (the product measure $\mu^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$ when $\mu$ is a
probability measure, and the zero measure otherwise) under the normalized sum
$\omega \mapsto (\omega_0 + \dots + \omega_{n-1})/\sqrt{n}$.

articles.title: Measurability of the normalized sum
articles.statement:
For every positive integer $n$, the map sending a real
sequence $\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$ to $(\omega_0 + \dots + \omega_{n-1})/\sqrt{n}$ is
measurable with respect to the product $\sigma$-algebra on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$.

articles.title: Normalized sum
articles.statement:
For a positive integer $n$ and a real sequence
$\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$, the normalized sum $S_n(\omega)$ is the sum of the first $n$
coordinates divided by $\sqrt{n}$: $S_n(\omega) = (\omega_0 + \dots + \omega_{n-1})/\sqrt{n}$.

articles.title: The CDF error is at most one
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathbb{R}$, $n$ a positive integer
and $x$ a real number. Let $F_{\mu,n}$ be the distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$
at $n$ and $\Phi$ the standard normal distribution function. Then $|F_{\mu,n}(x) - \Phi(x)| \le 1$.

No assumption is made on $\mu$: both distribution functions take values in $[0, 1]$.

articles.title: Each CDF error is at most the Kolmogorov error
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathbb{R}$,
$n$ a positive integer, $F_{\mu,n}$ the distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$ at
$n$ and $\Phi$ the standard normal distribution function. Then for every real $x$,
$|F_{\mu,n}(x) - \Phi(x)| \le \sup_{y \in \mathbb{R}} |F_{\mu,n}(y) - \Phi(y)|$, the right side
being the Kolmogorov error of $\mu$ at $n$.

articles.title: The Kolmogorov error vanishes for one standard Gaussian summand
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be the distribution
function of the normalized law of the standard normal law $N(0,1)$ at $n = 1$, and $\Phi$ the
standard normal distribution function. Then the Kolmogorov error of $N(0,1)$ at $n = 1$,
$\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F(x) - \Phi(x)|$, equals $0$.

articles.title: The standard Gaussian is a standardized law
articles.statement:
The standard normal law $N(0,1)$ on
$\mathbb{R}$ is a standardized law: it is a probability measure with mean $0$, variance $1$ and
finite third absolute moment.

articles.title: The common law of an i.i.d. model is standardized
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a measure on a measurable
space $\Omega$ and $X_0, X_1, \dots$ real-valued functions on $\Omega$ forming an i.i.d. model:
$P$ is a probability measure, the $X_i$ are measurable, independent and identically distributed,
and $X_0$ has mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment. Then the law of $X_0$, the
pushforward of $P$ under $X_0$, is a standardized law.

articles.title: Third absolute moment of the common law
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a measure on a measurable space $\Omega$
and $X_0, X_1, \dots$ real-valued functions on $\Omega$ forming an i.i.d. model: $P$ is a
probability measure, the $X_i$ are measurable, independent and identically distributed, and $X_0$
has mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment. Then the third absolute moment of the
law of $X_0$ equals $\int_\Omega |X_0(\omega)|^3 \, dP(\omega)$.

articles.title: Standardized laws have an integrable third absolute moment
articles.statement:
If $\mu$ is a standardized law
on $\mathbb{R}$, then the function $x \mapsto |x|^3$ is integrable with respect to $\mu$.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the third absolute moment
articles.statement:
For every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the
third absolute moment $\int_{\mathbb{R}} |x|^3 \, d\mu(x)$ is nonnegative.

As a real number, this integral is taken to be $0$ when $|x|^3$ is not $\mu$-integrable.

articles.title: The third absolute moment of a standardized law is positive
articles.statement:
If $\mu$ is a standardized
law on $\mathbb{R}$, that is, a probability measure with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third
absolute moment, then its third absolute moment $\int |x|^3 \, d\mu(x)$ is strictly positive.

The variance condition is what excludes a zero third absolute moment.

articles.title: Third absolute moment
articles.statement:
The third absolute moment of a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is the
real number $\int |x|^3 \, d\mu(x)$, taken to be $0$ when $x \mapsto |x|^3$ is not integrable
with respect to $\mu$.

This integrand is integrable whenever $\mu$ is a standardized law.

articles.title: Characteristic function of the real-valued binomial distribution
articles.statement:
For every natural
number $n$, every $p \in [0, 1]$ and every real $t$, the characteristic function
$\varphi_{\mathrm{Bin}(n, p)}$ of the binomial distribution $\mathrm{Bin}(n, p)$, viewed as a
measure on $\mathbb{R}$, satisfies
$\varphi_{\mathrm{Bin}(n, p)}(t) = \left((1 - p) + p e^{it}\right)^n$.

articles.title: Affine transformation of a characteristic function
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on
$\mathbb{R}$, let $a, s, t \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $\nu$ be the image of $\mu$ under the map
$x \mapsto (x - a)/s$. Then the characteristic functions satisfy
$\varphi_\nu(t) = \varphi_\mu(t s^{-1}) \, e^{-i a t s^{-1}}$. Here $s^{-1}$ and division by $s$
are read as $0$ when $s = 0$, so no hypothesis $s \neq 0$ is needed.

articles.title: Characteristic function of the standardized binomial
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$,
every $p \in [0, 1]$ and every real $t$, put $s = \sqrt{np(1-p)}$, with $s^{-1}$ read as $0$ when
$s = 0$. Let $\psi$ be the characteristic function of the binomial distribution
$\mathrm{Bin}(n, p)$ viewed as a measure on $\mathbb{R}$, and $\varphi$ that of the standardized
binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$. Then
$\varphi(t) = \psi(t s^{-1}) \, e^{-i n p t s^{-1}}$.

articles.title: De Moivre–Laplace limit theorem, interval form
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be independent,
identically distributed real random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, P)$, each almost
surely equal to $0$ or $1$, with mean $p$ for some $0 < p < 1$. Write
$S_n = X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1}$. Then for all real numbers $a \le b$, the probability
$P\left(a \le (S_n - np)/\sqrt{np(1-p)} \le b\right)$ tends, as $n \to \infty$, to the mass that
the standard normal distribution $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ gives to the interval $[a, b]$.

articles.title: Standardized partial sums
articles.statement:
For a sequence $X_0, X_1, \dots$ of real-valued functions on a
set $\Omega$, a real number $p$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the standardized partial sum is the
function $\omega \mapsto (S_n(\omega) - np)/\sqrt{np(1-p)}$ on $\Omega$, where
$S_n = X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1}$.

The square root of a negative number is taken to be $0$ and division by $0$ gives $0$; in
particular the standardized partial sum is $0$ for $n = 0$.

articles.title: De Moivre–Laplace limit theorem, convergence in distribution
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be
independent, identically distributed real random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, P)$,
each almost surely equal to $0$ or $1$, with mean $p$ for some $0 < p < 1$. Write
$S_n = X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1}$. Then the standardized sums $(S_n - np)/\sqrt{np(1-p)}$ converge in
distribution to the standard normal distribution $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Second-order Taylor remainder bound for the exponential
articles.statement:
For every complex number $z$
with $|z| \le 1$, the remainder after the degree-2 Taylor polynomial of the exponential
satisfies $|e^z - 1 - z - z^2/2| \le 2|z|^3$.

articles.title: Almost surely $\{0, 1\}$-valued random variables are integrable
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a probability
measure on $\Omega$ and let $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ be almost everywhere measurable with
$f(\omega) \in \{0, 1\}$ for $P$-almost every $\omega$. Then $f$ is integrable with respect to
$P$.

articles.title: Second moment of a $\{0, 1\}$-valued random variable
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a probability measure on
$\Omega$ and let $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $f(\omega) \in \{0, 1\}$ for $P$-almost every
$\omega$. Then $\int f^2 \, dP = \int f \, dP$.

articles.title: Bernoulli standardization map
articles.statement:
For a real number $p$, the standardization map sends
$x \in \mathbb{R}$ to $(x - p)/\sqrt{p(1-p)}$.

The square root of a negative number is taken to be $0$ and division by $0$ gives $0$, so for
$p \le 0$ or $p \ge 1$ the map is identically $0$.

articles.title: Standardized binomial distribution
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$ and $p \in [0, 1]$, the
standardized binomial distribution is the measure on $\mathbb{R}$ given by the law of
$(S_n - np)/\sqrt{np(1-p)}$, where $S_n$ has the binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and
$p$. When $np(1-p) = 0$ the division by $0$ is read as $0$, so the law is the point mass at $0$.

This is the standardized sum appearing in the De Moivre–Laplace limit theorem.

articles.title: Convergence of characteristic functions in De Moivre–Laplace
articles.statement:
Let $0 < p < 1$ and
$t \in \mathbb{R}$. As $n \to \infty$, the characteristic function of the standardized binomial
distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$, evaluated at $t$, converges to $e^{-t^2/2}$, the
value at $t$ of the characteristic function of the standard normal distribution.

This is the key analytic step in proving the De Moivre–Laplace theorem via Lévy's continuity
theorem.

articles.title: Finite-dimensional distributions determine laws on $C((0,1))$
articles.statement:
Probability measures on `C([0,1], ℝ)` are determined by their finite-dimensional
distributions. Compatibility wrapper around
`MathlibExt.Probability.ContinuousPathConvergence.continuousPath_measure_ext_of_finset_eval`
at `T = 1`; the projective-limit argument lives there, not here.

articles.title: Clamping to the unit interval
articles.statement:
For a real number $x$, its clamp to $[0,1]$ is
$\min(\max(x, 0), 1)$.

articles.title: Donsker's invariance principle
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be independent, identically
distributed, measurable real random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, P)$ such that
$X_0$ is integrable, $\mathbb{E}[X_0^2] < \infty$, $\mathbb{E}[X_0] = 0$ and
$\operatorname{Var}(X_0) = 1$. Let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real Brownian motion on a probability
space $(\Omega', P')$: its finite-dimensional laws are those of Brownian motion and its paths are
$P'$-almost surely continuous. For $n \ge 1$ let $S_n$ be the polygonal partial-sum process of
the $X_i$, the random element of $C([0,1], \mathbb{R})$ that linearly interpolates the values
$(X_0 + \dots + X_{k-1})/\sqrt{n}$ at the times $k/n$ for $0 \le k \le n$. Then there is a random
element $Y$ of $C([0,1], \mathbb{R})$ defined on $\Omega'$ such that $P'$-almost surely
$Y(t) = B_t$ for all $t \in [0,1]$, and $S_n$ converges in distribution to $Y$ as $n \to \infty$.
Here $C([0,1], \mathbb{R})$ carries the topology of uniform convergence and its Borel
$\sigma$-algebra.

Proof: The route combines finite-dimensional convergence from the central limit theorem,
tightness from a maximal inequality and a modulus-of-continuity criterion, Prokhorov's theorem,
and uniqueness of laws on $C([0,1], \mathbb{R})$ from finite-dimensional distributions.

## Sources

- M. D. Donsker, An invariance principle for certain probability limit theorems, Mem. Amer. Math. Soc. 6 (1951); extension Prohorov 1956 to Polish; textbook in Billingsley, Convergence of Probability Measures, 2nd ed., Kallenberg, Foundations of Modern Probability; Lean is `C(Icc 0 1, ℝ)` polygonal process with `MemLp 2`, mean-zero variance-one standardization.

articles.title: Explicit formula for the polygonal partial-sum process
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be
real-valued functions on a set $\Omega$ and let $S_n$ be their polygonal partial-sum process. For
$n \ge 1$, $\omega \in \Omega$ and $t \in [0,1]$, write $m = \lfloor nt \rfloor$. Then

$$S_n(\omega)(t) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \Big( \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} X_i(\omega) + c \Big),$$

where $c = (nt - m) X_m(\omega)$ if $m < n$ and $c = 0$ otherwise.

articles.title: Polygonal partial-sum process
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real-valued functions on a set
$\Omega$. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\omega \in \Omega$, $S_n(\omega)$ is the element of the space
$C([0,1], \mathbb{R})$ of continuous real functions on $[0,1]$ defined by $S_0(\omega) = 0$ and,
for $n \ge 1$ and $t \in [0,1]$,

$$S_n(\omega)(t) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} X_i(\omega) \min(\max(nt - i, 0), 1).$$

Thus for $n \ge 1$, $S_n(\omega)$ linearly interpolates the values
$(X_0(\omega) + \dots + X_{k-1}(\omega))/\sqrt{n}$ at the times $k/n$ for $0 \le k \le n$.

articles.title: Polygonal interpolation weight as a continuous function
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $i$,
this is the function $t \mapsto \min(\max(nt - i, 0), 1)$ on $[0,1]$, regarded as an element of
the space $C([0,1], \mathbb{R})$ of continuous real functions on $[0,1]$.

articles.title: Polygonal interpolation weight
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $i$ and $t \in [0,1]$, the
weight is $w_{n,i}(t) = \min(\max(nt - i, 0), 1)$, the clamp of $nt - i$ to $[0,1]$.

articles.title: Etemadi's maximal inequality
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be independent real random variables
on a probability space $(\Omega, P)$ and write $S_k = X_0 + \dots + X_{k-1}$, so that $S_0 = 0$.
Then for every natural number $n$ and every real number $a$,

$$P\Big(\max_{0 \le k \le n} |S_k| \ge 3a\Big) \le 3 \max_{0 \le k \le n} P(|S_k| \ge a).$$

articles.title: Inclusion of the unit interval into the nonnegative reals
articles.statement:
This map sends $t \in [0,1]$
to $t$ regarded as a nonnegative real number.

articles.title: Kac's Scottish Book Problem 126
articles.statement:
Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a measurable function
that is integrable on $[0, 1]$ and satisfies $\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx = 0$ and
$\int_0^1 f(x)^2\,dx = \infty$. Then the complex numbers
$\left(\int_0^1 \exp\left(i f(x) / \sqrt{n}\right) dx\right)^n$ tend to $0$ as $n \to \infty$
through the natural numbers.

## Sources

- M. Kac, Problem 126 of the Scottish Book; solved affirmatively by A. Khintchine, fourth communique on dependent functions, Studia Mathematicae 6 or 7, as cited in the typescript addendum Ad 126. The typescript parenthetical states the finite-variance case as `e ^ (-1 / 2)` where `e ^ (-A / 2)` for `A = ∫_0^1 f^2` would be expected; that parenthetical is not used here.

articles.title: Kac's lacunary central limit theorem
articles.statement:
Let $(r_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers such
that $r_n - (r_0 + r_1 + \dots + r_{n-1})$ tends to $+\infty$ as $n \to \infty$. Then $(r_n)$
satisfies the central limit theorem for lacunary sine sums. The sequence $r_n = 2^n$ satisfies
it as well.

The sequence $r_n = 2^n$ does not satisfy the gap hypothesis, since
$2^n - (1 + 2 + \dots + 2^{n-1}) = 1$ for every $n$. The sequence $r_n = 2^{n^2}$ is the example
given in the problem that does satisfy it.

## Sources

- M. Kac, Problem 161 of the Scottish Book; the `2ⁿ` case is affirmative by R. Salem and A. Zygmund, "On lacunary trigonometric series", Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 33 (1947), 333-338, who proved the central limit theorem for lacunary trigonometric series with ratio bounded away from `1`.

articles.title: Central limit theorem for lacunary sine sums
articles.statement:
A sequence of integers $(r_k)_{k \ge 0}$
satisfies the central limit theorem for lacunary sine sums if for all real numbers $a < b$, the
Lebesgue measure of the set of $x \in [0, 1]$ with
$a < \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} \sin(2 \pi r_k x) < b$ tends to
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}} \int_a^b e^{-y^2} \, dy$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Analytic core of the Lindeberg–Feller theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on
$\Omega$ and let $X_{n,k}$ ($n \in \mathbb{N}$, $0 \le k < n$) be real random variables on
$\Omega$ such that each $X_{n,k}$ has mean $0$ and each $X_{n,k}^2$ is integrable (expectations
are taken under $\mu$). Suppose that for some $\sigma > 0$ the row variances
$\sum_{k < n} \mathbb{E}[X_{n,k}^2]$ converge to $\sigma^2$ and that the array satisfies the
Lindeberg condition. Then for every real $t$ the product $\prod_{k < n} \varphi_{n,k}(t)$ of the
characteristic functions $\varphi_{n,k}$ of the laws of the $X_{n,k}$ converges to
$e^{-\sigma^2 t^2 / 2}$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Lindeberg condition for a triangular array
articles.statement:
A triangular array of real random variables
$X_{n,k}$ ($n \in \mathbb{N}$, $0 \le k < n$) on a measure space $(\Omega, \mu)$ satisfies the
Lindeberg condition if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ the truncated second moments

$$\sum_{k < n} \int_\Omega X_{n,k}^2 \, \mathbf{1}\{|X_{n,k}| > \varepsilon\} \, d\mu$$

tend to $0$ as $n \to \infty$. This is the key hypothesis of the Lindeberg–Feller central limit
theorem.

articles.title: Lindeberg–Feller central limit theorem
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$
and let $X_{n,k}$ ($n \in \mathbb{N}$, $0 \le k < n$) be a triangular array of real random
variables on $\Omega$ such that for each $n$ the variables $X_{n,0}, \dots, X_{n,n-1}$ are
independent, each $X_{n,k}$ has mean $0$, and each $X_{n,k}^2$ is integrable (expectations are
taken under $\mu$). Suppose that for some $\sigma > 0$ the row variances
$\sum_{k < n} \mathbb{E}[X_{n,k}^2]$ converge to $\sigma^2$ and that the array satisfies the
Lindeberg condition. Then the row sums $S_n = \sum_{k < n} X_{n,k}$ converge in distribution to
the Gaussian law $N(0, \sigma^2)$: for every bounded continuous $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$,
$\mathbb{E}[f(S_n)] \to \int_{\mathbb{R}} f \, dN(0, \sigma^2)$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Second-order Taylor bound for the imaginary exponential
articles.statement:
For every real $x$ with
$|x| \le 1$, $|e^{ix} - 1 - ix| \le x^2$.

articles.title: Comparing a finite product with the exponential of a sum
articles.statement:
Let $s$ be a finite index
set and let $u_i \in \mathbb{C}$ for $i \in s$. If $|u_i| \le 1/2$ for every $i \in s$, then

$$
\Bigl|\prod_{i \in s} (1 + u_i) - \exp\Bigl(\sum_{i \in s} u_i\Bigr)\Bigr| \le
\Bigl(\sum_{i \in s} |u_i|^2\Bigr) \exp\Bigl(\sum_{i \in s} |u_i|\Bigr).
$$

This is the estimate that turns the second-order expansion of each characteristic function
into convergence of the product.

articles.title: Stirling decomposition of the binomial-to-Gaussian ratio
articles.statement:
Algebraic rewriting of the ratio `binomProbHalf n k / gaussianApproxHalf n k` using
Stirling's formula, separating it into a Stirling-sequence factor, a square-root factor,
a power-of-`n` factor, and an exponential correction.

articles.title: Binomial point mass is equivalent to a fixed Gaussian value
articles.statement:
For any binomial success-index sequence whose standardized displacement converges to
`x`, the point mass is equivalent to the Gaussian expression evaluated at the fixed limit `x`.
The number of trials may follow any natural-valued sequence tending to infinity.

articles.title: Binomial point mass is equivalent to its Gaussian approximation
articles.statement:
The binomial point mass and its Gaussian approximation are asymptotically equivalent along
the sequence `k = localDMLIndex x n`:
`binomProbHalf n k ~ gaussianApproxHalf n k` as `n → ∞`. Combines Stirling's formula with the
power-factor and entropy estimates.

articles.title: Binomial point mass with success probability one half
articles.statement: The point mass `P(B_n = k) = C(n,k) / 2ⁿ` for a `Binomial(n, 1/2)` success count `B_n`.

articles.title: The corrected binomial power factor tends to one
articles.statement:
The product of the power factor `nⁿ / (kᵏ (n-k)^{n-k} 2ⁿ)` with the Gaussian correction
`exp((k - n/2)² / (n/2))`, evaluated at `k = localDMLIndex x n`, tends to `1` as `n → ∞`.
This is the key analytic estimate behind the local DeMoivre–Laplace limit theorem.

articles.title: Cubic bound on the symmetric entropy residual
articles.statement:
Third-order Taylor bound for the symmetric entropy expansion:
`|(1+u) log(1+u) + (1-u) log(1-u) - u²| ≤ 6 |u|³` whenever `|u| < 1/2`. Used to control the
deviation of the binomial coefficient from its Gaussian approximation.

articles.title: Factorial in terms of the Stirling sequence
articles.statement:
Rewriting of `m!` in terms of Mathlib's `Stirling.stirlingSeq`:
`m! = stirlingSeq(m) · √(2m) · (m/e)^m`.

articles.title: Gaussian approximation to the symmetric binomial point mass
articles.statement:
The Gaussian (local CLT) approximation to `binomProbHalf n k`,
`√(2/(π n)) · exp(-(k - n/2)² / (n/2))`.

articles.title: Local limit theorem for the simple random walk
articles.statement:
The source's random-walk local limit theorem: every integer displacement sequence with
`2 kₙ / √(2n) → x` has point mass equivalent to `(√(π n))⁻¹ exp(-x²/2)`.
The scaling hypothesis itself implies that `n + kₙ` is a valid success index eventually.

articles.title: Local De Moivre–Laplace theorem for $p = 1/2$
articles.statement:
Canonical rounded-sequence corollary of the local De Moivre–Laplace theorem: for any
`x ∈ ℝ`, the binomial point mass divided by its moving Gaussian approximation along
`localDMLIndex x` tends to `1`. The arbitrary integer-displacement statement with the fixed
Gaussian value at `x` is `local_deMoivreLaplace_half_of_tendsto`.

articles.title: Deviation bound for the De Moivre–Laplace index
articles.statement:
Eventually, the deviation `|2k - n|` for `k = localDMLIndex x n` is at most `|x| √n + 2`,
since `k = ⌊n/2 + x √n / 2⌋`.

articles.title: The De Moivre–Laplace index over n tends to one half
articles.statement:
The ratio `localDMLIndex x n / n` tends to `1/2` as `n → ∞`, because the correction
`x √n / 2` is `o(n)`.

articles.title: Standardized displacement of the rounded index converges
articles.statement: The rounded success index has standardized displacement converging to `x`.

articles.title: The De Moivre–Laplace index tends to infinity
articles.statement: The index `localDMLIndex x n` tends to infinity as `n → ∞`, for any fixed `x : ℝ`.

articles.title: Lattice index in the local De Moivre–Laplace theorem
articles.statement:
The integer index `k = ⌊n/2 + x·√n/2⌋` corresponding to the parameter `x` in the local
DeMoivre–Laplace statement: it picks the lattice point near `n/2 + x √n / 2`, so that
`(2k - n)/√n ≈ x`.

articles.title: Logarithm of the binomial power factor
articles.statement:
Identity rewriting the logarithm of the power factor `nⁿ / (kᵏ (n-k)^{n-k} 2ⁿ)` plus the
Gaussian exponent `(k - n/2)² / (n/2)` as `-(n/2) · ((1+u) log(1+u) + (1-u) log(1-u) - u²)`,
where `u = (2k - n)/n`. This combines the log-binomial expansion with the Gaussian correction.

articles.title: The complementary index over n tends to one half
articles.statement:
Companion to `localDMLIndex_ratio_half`: the ratio `(n - k) / n` for `k = localDMLIndex x n`
also tends to `1/2`.

articles.title: The complementary De Moivre–Laplace index tends to infinity
articles.statement:
The complementary index `n - localDMLIndex x n` also tends to infinity, so both `k` and
`n - k` are eventually arbitrarily large.

articles.title: The admissible Berry–Esseen coefficients are bounded below
articles.statement:
The set of real numbers $C$
that are admissible Berry–Esseen coefficients (common Berry–Esseen coefficients for all
standardized laws and all positive sample sizes) is bounded below.

articles.title: Admissible Berry–Esseen coefficients exist
articles.statement:
The set of real numbers $C$ that are
admissible Berry–Esseen coefficients (common Berry–Esseen coefficients for all standardized laws
and all positive sample sizes) is nonempty.

articles.title: The Bernoulli-admissible coefficients are bounded below
articles.statement:
The set of real numbers $C$ that
are admissible Berry–Esseen coefficients for the Bernoulli subclass (common Berry–Esseen
coefficients for all standardized laws concentrated on two points and all positive sample sizes)
is bounded below.

articles.title: Bernoulli-admissible coefficients exist
articles.statement:
The set of real numbers $C$ that are admissible
Berry–Esseen coefficients for the Bernoulli subclass (common Berry–Esseen coefficients for all
standardized laws concentrated on two points and all positive sample sizes) is nonempty.

The coefficient $42$, admissible for all standardized laws, is one such coefficient.

articles.title: The Bernoulli Berry–Esseen constant is at most the general one
articles.statement:
The infimum of the real
numbers that are admissible Berry–Esseen coefficients for the Bernoulli subclass is at most the
infimum of the real numbers that are admissible Berry–Esseen coefficients for all standardized
laws.

articles.title: The Bernoulli Berry–Esseen constant is nonnegative
articles.statement:
The infimum of the real numbers that
are admissible Berry–Esseen coefficients for the Bernoulli subclass is nonnegative.

articles.title: Bernoulli Berry–Esseen constant
articles.statement:
The Bernoulli Berry–Esseen constant is the infimum, in
$\mathbb{R}$, of the set of real numbers $C$ that are admissible Berry–Esseen coefficients for the
Bernoulli subclass: for every standardized law $\mu$ (a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with
mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment) concentrated on two distinct points, and
every positive integer $n$, the supremum over $x \in \mathbb{R}$ of the distance between the
distribution function of $(X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1})/\sqrt{n}$ at $x$, for independent
$\mu$-distributed $X_0, \dots, X_{n-1}$, and the standard normal distribution function at $x$ is
at most $C \rho(\mu) / \sqrt{n}$, where $\rho(\mu) = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu(x)$.

articles.title: Esseen's lower bound for the Berry–Esseen constant
articles.statement:
For a probability measure
$\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and an integer $n \ge 1$, let $F_n$ be the distribution function of
$(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$ for independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ each with law
$\mu$, let $\Delta_n(\mu) = \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)|$, where $\Phi$ is the
standard normal distribution function, and let $\beta_3(\mu) = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu$. Let $C_0$ be
the optimal i.i.d. Berry–Esseen constant, the infimum of all real $C$ such that
$\Delta_n(\mu) \le C \beta_3(\mu) / \sqrt{n}$ for every integer $n \ge 1$ and every probability
measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment. Then
$(\sqrt{10} + 3)/(6\sqrt{2\pi}) \le C_0$.

## Sources

- catalogue C19a, E1956 lower row; retained 2011 exact benchmark.

articles.title: Statement of Esseen's lower bound for the Berry–Esseen constant
articles.statement:
For a probability measure
$\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and an integer $n \ge 1$, let $F_n$ be the distribution function of
$(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$ for independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ each with law
$\mu$, let $\Delta_n(\mu) = \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)|$, where $\Phi$ is the
standard normal distribution function, and let $\beta_3(\mu) = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu$. Let $C_0$ be
the optimal i.i.d. Berry–Esseen constant, the infimum of all real $C$ such that
$\Delta_n(\mu) \le C \beta_3(\mu) / \sqrt{n}$ for every integer $n \ge 1$ and every probability
measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment. This
is the proposition that $(\sqrt{10} + 3)/(6\sqrt{2\pi}) \le C_0$.

## Sources

- catalogue C19a, lower row E1956, and retained Shevtsova2011 lines 185-194. The symbolic endpoint is not replaced by its decimal approximation.

articles.title: Esseen's asymptotic lower bound for a two-point law
articles.statement:
For a probability measure $\mu$ on
$\mathbb{R}$ and an integer $n \ge 1$, let $F_n$ be the distribution function of
$(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$ for independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ each with law
$\mu$, let $\Delta_n(\mu) = \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)|$, where $\Phi$ is the
standard normal distribution function, let $\beta_3(\mu) = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu$, and let
$C_E = (\sqrt{10} + 3)/(6\sqrt{2\pi})$. There is a probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with
mean $0$ and variance $1$ that is concentrated on two distinct points, such that for every real
$\varepsilon > 0$ and every $N \in \mathbb{N}$ there is a positive integer $n \ge N$ with

$$\Delta_n(\mu) \ge \frac{(C_E - \varepsilon)\,\beta_3(\mu)}{\sqrt{n}}.$$

In other words, $\limsup_{n \to \infty} \sqrt{n}\,\Delta_n(\mu) / \beta_3(\mu) \ge C_E$.

## Sources

- catalogue C19a, the asymptotic normalized Bernoulli lower-row clause.

articles.title: Statement of Esseen's asymptotic lower bound for a two-point law
articles.statement:
For a probability
measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and an integer $n \ge 1$, let $F_n$ be the distribution function of
$(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$ for independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ each with law
$\mu$, let $\Delta_n(\mu) = \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)|$, where $\Phi$ is the
standard normal distribution function, let $\beta_3(\mu) = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu$, and let
$C_E = (\sqrt{10} + 3)/(6\sqrt{2\pi})$. This is the proposition that there is a probability
measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$ and variance $1$ that is concentrated on two distinct
points, such that for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ and every $N \in \mathbb{N}$ there is a positive
integer $n \ge N$ with

$$\Delta_n(\mu) \ge \frac{(C_E - \varepsilon)\,\beta_3(\mu)}{\sqrt{n}}.$$

## Sources

- catalogue C19a, lower-row Bernoulli asymptotic comment. A single actual standardized two-point law is chosen before epsilon and the sample-size threshold. Its normalized sums approach the lower coefficient along arbitrarily large sample sizes; an original Esseen primary comparison remains a source gap.

articles.title: Esseen's lower-bound constant is positive
articles.statement:
The number $(\sqrt{10} + 3)/(6\sqrt{2\pi})$ is
positive.

articles.title: Esseen's lower-bound constant
articles.statement:
Esseen's constant is the real number
$(\sqrt{10} + 3)/(6\sqrt{2\pi})$.

Esseen showed that the Berry–Esseen constant for i.i.d. sums is at least this number; the
definition records the value only, not that lower bound.

articles.title: Admissible coefficients bound every standardized i.i.d. sequence
articles.statement:
Let $C$ be an admissible
Berry–Esseen coefficient. Let $X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be measurable real random variables on a
probability space $(\Omega, P)$ that are independent and identically distributed, with
$\mathbb{E}[X_0] = 0$, $\operatorname{Var}(X_0) = 1$ and $\mathbb{E}|X_0|^3 < \infty$. Then for
every positive integer $n$ and every real $x$,

$$
\left| P\left( \frac{X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1}}{\sqrt{n}} \le x \right) - \Phi(x) \right|
\le \frac{C \, \mathbb{E}|X_0|^3}{\sqrt{n}},
$$

where $\Phi$ is the distribution function of the standard normal law.

articles.title: The Berry–Esseen bound with coefficient 42
articles.statement:
The number $42$ is an admissible
Berry–Esseen coefficient: for every probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$,
variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment $\rho = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu(x)$, and every positive
integer $n$, the Kolmogorov error $\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)|$ is at most
$42 \rho / \sqrt{n}$, where $F_n$ is the distribution function of $(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$
for independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ with law $\mu$, and $\Phi$ is the standard
normal distribution function.

articles.title: Admissible coefficients are exactly those above the optimal one
articles.statement:
A real number $C$ is an
admissible Berry–Esseen coefficient if and only if $C_0 \le C$, where $C_0$ is the optimal
Berry–Esseen coefficient, the infimum of the set of admissible coefficients.

articles.title: Admissibility is upward closed
articles.statement:
If $C \le D$ are real numbers and $C$ is an admissible
Berry–Esseen coefficient, then $D$ is an admissible Berry–Esseen coefficient.

articles.title: Admissible coefficients are nonnegative
articles.statement:
Every admissible Berry–Esseen coefficient
$C \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $C \ge 0$.

articles.title: Admissible Berry–Esseen coefficient
articles.statement:
A real number $C$ is an admissible Berry–Esseen
coefficient when, for every probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$, variance $1$
and finite third absolute moment $\rho = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu(x)$, and every positive integer $n$,
the Kolmogorov error $\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)|$ is at most $C \rho / \sqrt{n}$.
Here $F_n$ is the distribution function of $(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$ for independent random
variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ with law $\mu$, and $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution
function.

articles.title: Bernoulli-admissible coefficients are nonnegative
articles.statement:
Every real number $C$ that is an
admissible Berry–Esseen coefficient for standardized two-point laws satisfies $C \ge 0$.

The class of standardized two-point laws is nonempty: it contains the law with mass $1/2$ at each
of $-1$ and $1$.

articles.title: Admissible Berry–Esseen coefficient for two-point laws
articles.statement:
A real number $C$ is an admissible
Berry–Esseen coefficient for standardized two-point laws when, for every probability measure $\mu$
on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment
$\rho = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu(x)$ that is concentrated on two distinct points, and every positive
integer $n$, the Kolmogorov error $\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)|$ is at most
$C \rho / \sqrt{n}$. Here $F_n$ is the distribution function of $(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$ for
independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ with law $\mu$, and $\Phi$ is the standard normal
distribution function.

articles.title: Standardized two-point law
articles.statement:
A measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is a standardized two-point
law when it is a probability measure with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute
moment, and there are real numbers $a \ne b$ with $\mu(\mathbb{R} \setminus \{a, b\}) = 0$.

articles.title: Korolev–Shevtsova structural Berry–Esseen bound
articles.statement:
For a probability measure $\mu$ on
$\mathbb{R}$ and an integer $n \ge 1$, let $F_n$ be the distribution function of
$(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$ for independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ each with law
$\mu$, let $\Delta_n(\mu) = \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)|$, where $\Phi$ is the
standard normal distribution function, and let $\beta_3(\mu) = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu$. Then for every
probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute
moment and every integer $n \ge 1$,

$$\Delta_n(\mu) \le \frac{0.34445\,(\beta_3(\mu) + 0.489)}{\sqrt{n}}.$$

## Sources

- catalogue C19a, KS2009 structural comment; retained 2011 equation.

articles.title: Statement of the Korolev–Shevtsova structural Berry–Esseen bound
articles.statement:
For a probability
measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and an integer $n \ge 1$, let $F_n$ be the distribution function of
$(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$ for independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ each with law
$\mu$, let $\Delta_n(\mu) = \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)|$, where $\Phi$ is the
standard normal distribution function, and let $\beta_3(\mu) = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu$. This is the
proposition that for every probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$, variance $1$
and finite third absolute moment and every integer $n \ge 1$,

$$\Delta_n(\mu) \le \frac{0.34445\,(\beta_3(\mu) + 0.489)}{\sqrt{n}}.$$

## Sources

- catalogue C19a, KS2009 upper-row comment, and the exact retained Shevtsova2011 quotation at lines 141-148. The additive offset is 0.489, not 0.429.

articles.title: Korolev–Shevtsova upper bound for the Berry–Esseen constant
articles.statement:
For a probability measure
$\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and an integer $n \ge 1$, let $F_n$ be the distribution function of
$(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$ for independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ each with law
$\mu$, let $\Delta_n(\mu) = \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)|$, where $\Phi$ is the
standard normal distribution function, and let $\beta_3(\mu) = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu$. Let $C_0$ be
the optimal i.i.d. Berry–Esseen constant, the infimum of all real $C$ such that
$\Delta_n(\mu) \le C \beta_3(\mu) / \sqrt{n}$ for every integer $n \ge 1$ and every probability
measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment. Then
$C_0 \le 0.5129$.

## Sources

- catalogue C19a, KS2009 upper row; retained Shevtsova2011 quotation.

articles.title: Statement of the Korolev–Shevtsova upper bound
articles.statement:
For a probability measure $\mu$ on
$\mathbb{R}$ and an integer $n \ge 1$, let $F_n$ be the distribution function of
$(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$ for independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ each with law
$\mu$, let $\Delta_n(\mu) = \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)|$, where $\Phi$ is the

the optimal i.i.d. Berry–Esseen constant, the infimum of all real $C$ such that

## Sources

- catalogue C19a, upper row KS2009; retained Shevtsova2011 lines 141-148.

articles.title: Kolmogorov distance via left-continuous distribution functions
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability
measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment, let $n \ge 1$
be an integer, and let $S_n = X_1 + \dots + X_n$ for independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$
each with law $\mu$. Then

$$
\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} \bigl|P(S_n/\sqrt{n} < x) - \Phi(x)\bigr|
= \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} \bigl|P(S_n/\sqrt{n} \le x) - \Phi(x)\bigr|,
$$

where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function.

## Sources

- catalogue C19a right CDF and Shevtsova2011's explicit left convention.

articles.title: Statement of the Kolmogorov distance via left-continuous distribution functions
articles.statement:
This is
the proposition that for every probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$, variance
$1$ and finite third absolute moment and every integer $n \ge 1$, if $S_n = X_1 + \dots + X_n$ for
independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ each with law $\mu$, then

$$
\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} \bigl|P(S_n/\sqrt{n} < x) - \Phi(x)\bigr|
= \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} \bigl|P(S_n/\sqrt{n} \le x) - \Phi(x)\bigr|,
$$

where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function.

## Sources

- the right-CDF catalogue definition and retained Shevtsova2011 lines 104-108, which explicitly use a left-continuous CDF. This probability bridge is requested, not inferred by replacing strict with non-strict events.

articles.title: Lin's 2026 Berry–Esseen bound
articles.statement:
Let $C_0$ be the infimum of all
real $C$ such that for every real probability law $\mu$ with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite
third absolute moment $\rho = \int |x|^3\,d\mu$, and every integer $n \ge 1$, the distribution
function $F_n$ of $(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$, for independent $X_1, \dots, X_n$ with law
$\mu$, satisfies $\sup_x |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)| \le C \rho / \sqrt{n}$, where $\Phi$ is the
standard normal distribution function. Then $C_0 \le 0.423$.

## Sources

- catalogue C19a, explicitly unverified Lin2026 row.

articles.title: Statement of Lin's 2026 Berry–Esseen bound
articles.statement:
Let $C_0$ be the infimum of all
real $C$ such that for every real probability law $\mu$ with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite
third absolute moment $\rho = \int |x|^3\,d\mu$, and every integer $n \ge 1$, the distribution

$\mu$, satisfies $\sup_x |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)| \le C \rho / \sqrt{n}$, where $\Phi$ is the
standard normal distribution function. This is the proposition $C_0 \le 0.423$.

## Sources

- catalogue C19a, upper row Lin2026, explicitly unverified. No external repository certificate or comparator result is asserted here.

articles.title: Schulz's Bernoulli Berry–Esseen optimum
articles.statement:
Let $C_B$ be the infimum of all
real $C$ such that for every real probability law $\mu$ with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite
third absolute moment $\rho = \int |x|^3\,d\mu$ that is concentrated on two points, that is,
$\mu(\mathbb{R} \setminus \{a, b\}) = 0$ for some reals $a \ne b$, and every integer $n \ge 1$,
the distribution function $F_n$ of $(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$, for independent
$X_1, \dots, X_n$ with law $\mu$, satisfies $\sup_x |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)| \le C \rho / \sqrt{n}$,
where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function. Then
$C_B = (\sqrt{10} + 3)/(6\sqrt{2\pi})$.

## Sources

- catalogue C19a, Bernoulli/binomial comment, Schulz2016.

articles.title: Statement of Schulz's Bernoulli Berry–Esseen optimum
articles.statement:
Let $C_B$ be the infimum of all
real $C$ such that for every real probability law $\mu$ with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite
third absolute moment $\rho = \int |x|^3\,d\mu$ that is concentrated on two points, that is,
$\mu(\mathbb{R} \setminus \{a, b\}) = 0$ for some reals $a \ne b$, and every integer $n \ge 1$,
the distribution function $F_n$ of $(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$, for independent

articles.title: Integrals against the symmetric Bernoulli law
articles.statement:
For every function
$f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, the integral of $f$ against the symmetric Bernoulli law
$\frac12 \delta_{-1} + \frac12 \delta_1$ equals $\frac12 f(-1) + \frac12 f(1)$.

articles.title: The symmetric Bernoulli law is a standardized two-point law
articles.statement:
The law
$\frac12 \delta_{-1} + \frac12 \delta_1$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is a probability measure with mean $0$,
variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment, and it is concentrated on the two distinct points
$-1$ and $1$.

articles.title: The symmetric Bernoulli law is standardized
articles.statement:
The symmetric Bernoulli law, which puts mass
$1/2$ at each of the points $-1$ and $1$, is a standardized law: it is a probability measure on
$\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$ and variance $1$, and it has a finite third absolute moment.

articles.title: Symmetric Bernoulli law
articles.statement:
The symmetric Bernoulli law is the measure
$\frac12 \delta_{-1} + \frac12 \delta_1$ on $\mathbb{R}$, where $\delta_a$ denotes the Dirac mass
at $a$; it puts mass $1/2$ at each of the points $-1$ and $1$.

articles.title: The symmetric Bernoulli law has moments of all orders
articles.statement:
For every exponent
$p \in [0, \infty]$, the identity function of $\mathbb{R}$ belongs to $L^p$ of the symmetric
Bernoulli law.

articles.title: Third absolute moment of the symmetric Bernoulli law
articles.statement:
The third absolute moment
$\int |x|^3 \, d\mu(x)$ of the symmetric Bernoulli law $\mu$ equals $1$.

articles.title: The optimal Berry–Esseen coefficient satisfies the Berry–Esseen bound
articles.statement:
Let $C^*$ be the
infimum of all admissible Berry–Esseen coefficients. For every standardized law $\mu$ on
$\mathbb{R}$ and every positive integer $n$, the Kolmogorov error of $\mu$ at sample size $n$ is
at most $C^* \rho(\mu) / \sqrt{n}$, where $\rho(\mu) = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu(x)$ is the third
absolute moment of $\mu$.

articles.title: The optimal Berry–Esseen coefficient is admissible
articles.statement:
The infimum $C^*$ of all admissible
Berry–Esseen coefficients is itself an admissible coefficient.

articles.title: The Berry–Esseen constant is the least admissible coefficient
articles.statement:
The infimum $C^*$ of all
admissible Berry–Esseen coefficients is the least element of the set of admissible
coefficients: $C^*$ is admissible, and $C^* \le C$ for every admissible coefficient $C$.

articles.title: The optimal Berry–Esseen coefficient is at most 42
articles.statement:
The infimum $C^*$ of all admissible
Berry–Esseen coefficients satisfies $C^* \le 42$.

articles.title: The optimal Berry–Esseen coefficient is at most every admissible one
articles.statement:
If $C$ is an
admissible Berry–Esseen coefficient, then the infimum $C^*$ of all admissible coefficients
satisfies $C^* \le C$.

articles.title: The optimal Berry–Esseen coefficient is nonnegative
articles.statement:
The infimum $C^*$ of all admissible
Berry–Esseen coefficients satisfies $0 \le C^*$.

articles.title: The optimal Berry–Esseen constant
articles.statement:
Call a real number $C$ admissible if for every
probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute
moment $\rho = \int |x|^3 \, d\mu$, and every positive integer $n$,

$$\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)| \le \frac{C \rho}{\sqrt{n}},$$

where $F_n$ is the distribution function of $(X_1 + \dots + X_n)/\sqrt{n}$ for independent
random variables $X_1, X_2, \dots$ with law $\mu$, and $\Phi$ is the standard normal
distribution function. The optimal Berry–Esseen constant is the infimum of the admissible $C$.

The set of admissible constants is nonempty (it contains $42$) and bounded below by $0$, so
this is a genuine real infimum.

articles.title: Binomial approximation to the Poisson law
articles.statement: The binomial law `Bin(n, λ / (n + λ))` on `ℝ`.

articles.title: Binomial law as a probability measure
articles.statement: The binomial law `Bin(n, p)` on `ℝ`, bundled as a probability measure.

articles.title: Characteristic function of a binomial law
Characteristic function of a Poisson law
articles.statement: `φ_{Poisson(λ)}(t) = exp(λ * (e^{it} - 1))`.

articles.title: Analytic core of Poisson convergence
articles.statement:
Let $\lambda \ge 0$ be a real number, let
$k : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and for each $n$ let $p_{n,i}$, $0 \le i < k(n)$, be real
numbers. Suppose that $p_{n,i} \ge 0$ for all $n$ and $i$, that for every $\varepsilon > 0$
we have $p_{n,i} < \varepsilon$ for all $i < k(n)$ once $n$ is large enough, and that
$\sum_{i < k(n)} p_{n,i} \to \lambda$ as $n \to \infty$. Then for every natural number $j$,
as $n \to \infty$ the Poisson-binomial mass

$$\sum_{|A| = j} \prod_{i \in A} p_{n,i} \prod_{i \notin A} (1 - p_{n,i})$$

tends to $e^{-\lambda} \lambda^j / j!$, where $A$ runs over the $j$-element subsets of
$\{0, \dots, k(n) - 1\}$ and $i \notin A$ ranges over the elements of that set not in $A$.

Without the hypothesis $p_{n,i} \ge 0$ the conclusion can fail.

articles.title: Success probability of the binomial approximation to Poisson
articles.statement:
The success probability `λ / (n + λ)` used in the binomial approximation to
