articles.title: Inclusion–exclusion for the weighted probability
articles.statement: Inclusion–exclusion for `wprob`.

articles.title: Weighted probability of an event
articles.statement:
The `pweight φ`-mass `∑ ω ∈ S, pweight φ ω` of an event `S`. When `φ ≥ 0` and
`φ x false + φ x true = 1` for all `x`, this is the probability of `S` under the product measure
whose coordinate `x` has law `φ x`.

articles.title: Doubled family of disjoint pairs
articles.statement: The family of `dbl S T` over disjoint pairs `S ∈ 𝒜`, `T ∈ ℬ`.

articles.title: Size of the doubled disjoint-pair family
articles.statement: The size of `boxDoubled 𝒜 ℬ` is the number of disjoint pairs in `𝒜 × ℬ`.

articles.title: Disjoint-union family is no larger than the doubled family
articles.statement: `#(𝒜 ○ ℬ) ≤ #(boxDoubled 𝒜 ℬ)`: distinct disjoint pairs can have the same union.

articles.title: Encoding a pair of finsets in the doubled ground set
articles.statement: The finset `inl '' S ∪ inr '' T` of `α ⊕ α`, encoding the pair `(S, T)`.

articles.title: Double compression at a coordinate
articles.statement: Down-compression at `inl i` followed by up-compression at `inr i`.

articles.title: Doubled coordinate weight
articles.statement: The coordinate weight `w` on both copies of `α`.

articles.title: Down-compression at the left copy of a coordinate
articles.statement: Down-compression at the left copy `inl i`.

articles.title: Family closed under erasing the left copy
articles.statement: `IsDownAtLeft i 𝒜`: `𝒜` is closed under erasing `inl i`.

articles.title: Family closed under inserting the right copy
articles.statement: `IsUpAtRight i 𝒜`: `𝒜` is closed under inserting `inr i`.

articles.title: Left copy in the doubled ground set
articles.statement: The left copy `{inl a}` of `α` in `α ⊕ α`.

articles.title: Restriction of a doubled configuration to the left copy
articles.statement: The restriction of a configuration on `α ⊕ α` to the left copy.

articles.title: Event on the left copy of the doubled ground set
articles.statement: The event on `α ⊕ α` that the left restriction lies in `A`.

articles.title: Reimer equality for a left event and a right event
articles.statement: Reimer's inequality, with equality, for a left event and a right event.

articles.title: Right copy in the doubled ground set
articles.statement: The right copy `{inr a}` of `α` in `α ⊕ α`.

articles.title: Restriction of a doubled configuration to the right copy
articles.statement: The restriction of a configuration on `α ⊕ α` to the right copy.

articles.title: Event on the right copy of the doubled ground set
articles.statement: The event on `α ⊕ α` that the right restriction lies in `B`.

articles.title: Up-compression at a point of the doubled ground set
articles.statement: Up-compression of a family on `α ⊕ α` at the point `a` (`UV.compression {a} ∅`).

articles.title: Up-compression at the right copy of a coordinate
articles.statement: Up-compression at the right copy `inr i`.

articles.title: Weighted disjoint pairs as a doubled-weight probability
articles.statement: `wdpairs w 𝒜 ℬ` is the doubled-weight probability of `familyEvent (boxDoubled 𝒜 ℬ)`.

articles.title: Members of a disjoint-union family avoiding a coordinate
articles.statement:
The members of `𝒜 ○ ℬ` avoiding `i` are exactly the disjoint unions of members of `𝒜` and
`ℬ` avoiding `i`.

articles.title: Configurations on a finite set as finsets
articles.statement: Configurations on a finite set are the same as finsets (their supports).

articles.title: Support of a configuration as a finset
articles.statement: The support `{i | ω i = true}` of a configuration, as a finset.

articles.title: Down-compression map on a single finset
articles.statement: The compression map: erase `i` from `s` when `s` contains `i` and `s.erase i ∉ 𝒜`.

articles.title: Event depending only on a set of coordinates
articles.statement:
`DependsOn A S`: whether a configuration lies in `A` depends only on its values on `S`.
This is Mathlib's `DependsOn` for the membership predicate of `A`.

articles.title: Disjoint occurrence equals intersection for disjoint dependence sets
articles.statement:
If `A` depends only on `S`, `B` only on `T`, and `S, T` are disjoint, then
`A □ B = A ∩ B`.

articles.title: Down-compression of a family of configurations
articles.statement: Down-compression at `i` of a family of configurations, through `cfgEquivFinset`.

articles.title: Down-compression does not decrease the disjoint-pair count
articles.statement: Down-compressing both families at `i` does not decrease the number of disjoint pairs.

articles.title: Recursion for disjoint pairs by membership of a coordinate
articles.statement:
Splitting disjoint pairs by membership of `i`: pairs where neither, only the first, or
only the second set contains `i`.

articles.title: Number of disjoint pairs from two families
articles.statement: The number of disjoint pairs `(S, T) ∈ 𝒜 × ℬ`.

articles.title: Iterated down-compression reaches a lower set
articles.statement: Some iterated down-compression of `𝒜` is a lower set.

articles.title: Family closed under erasing a coordinate
articles.statement: `IsDownAtCoord i 𝒜`: the family `𝒜` is closed under erasing `i`.

articles.title: Iterated down-compression along a list of coordinates
articles.statement: Down-compression at each coordinate of `cs` in turn (the head of `cs` is applied last).

articles.title: Weight kernel of disjoint pairs off a coordinate
articles.statement: `fwt' w i S * fwt' w i T` for disjoint `S, T`, and `0` otherwise.

articles.title: One compression step on the doubled disjoint-pair family
articles.statement:
Bookkeeping for one compression step at coordinate `i` on `boxDoubled 𝒜 ℬ`:
`doubleCompress i` preserves its size and makes it down-closed at `inl i` and up-closed at
`inr i`, and sizes split over `memberSubfamily i` and `nonMemberSubfamily i`.

articles.title: Down-compression can shrink the disjoint-union family
articles.statement:
Down-compressing both families at the same coordinate can strictly decrease the size of
`𝒜 ○ ℬ`.

articles.title: First family in the box-compression counterexample
articles.statement:
The family `{∅, {1}}` on `Fin 2`, the first family of the counterexample
`StatMech.reimerStep_box_compression_false`.

articles.title: Second family in the box-compression counterexample
articles.statement:
The family `{∅, {0, 1}}` on `Fin 2`, the second family of the counterexample
`StatMech.reimerStep_box_compression_false`.

articles.title: Reimer's inequality for events on disjoint coordinate sets
articles.statement: Reimer's inequality, with equality, for events depending on disjoint coordinate sets.

articles.title: Reimer's inequality on one coordinate
articles.statement: Reimer's inequality on one coordinate, for all events.

articles.title: Configuration with a given support
articles.statement: The configuration whose open coordinates are exactly the elements of `s`.

articles.title: Total size of a family of finsets
articles.statement: The total size `∑ S ∈ 𝒜, #S` of a family.

articles.title: Down-compression does not decrease weighted disjoint pairs
articles.statement:
Down-compressing both families at `i` does not decrease the weighted number of disjoint
pairs when `w i true ≤ w i false`.

articles.title: Weighted down-compression monotonicity fails for general weights
articles.statement: Without `w i true ≤ w i false`, `wdpairs_downDown_mono` can fail.

articles.title: Independence of events on complementary coordinate sets
articles.statement:
Events depending on complementary coordinate sets are independent under a product
probability weight.

articles.title: Determined-by and depends-on are the same predicate
articles.statement: `DeterminedBy` and `DependsOn` are the same predicate.

articles.title: Event determined by a set of coordinates
articles.statement:
`DeterminedBy A K`: whether a configuration lies in `A` depends only on its values on `K`.
This is definitionally `StatMech.DependsOn A K`.

articles.title: Reimer equality for events determined by disjoint coordinates
articles.statement:
Reimer's inequality with equality for events determined by disjoint coordinate sets: under
the product Bernoulli(`p`) measure, `P_p(A □ B) = P_p(A) * P_p(B)`.

articles.title: Independence of events determined by disjoint coordinate sets
articles.statement:
Events determined by disjoint coordinate sets are independent under a product probability
weight: `wprob φ (A ∩ B) = wprob φ A * wprob φ B`.

articles.title: Event of a family of finsets
articles.statement: The event that the support of a configuration lies in the family `𝒜`.

articles.title: Lower sets are families closed under erasing an element
articles.statement: A family of finsets is a lower set iff it is closed under erasing any single element.

articles.title: Reimer's inequality for two lower families
articles.statement:
Reimer's inequality for the events of two lower families (the BK inequality for
decreasing events).

articles.title: Reimer's inequality for two upper families
articles.statement: Reimer's inequality for the events of two upper families (the BK inequality).

articles.title: Reimer's inequality
articles.statement:
**Reimer's inequality** (van den Berg–Kesten conjecture). For every `n`, every product
probability weight `φ` on `{0, 1}^n` (`φ i b ≥ 0`, `φ i false + φ i true = 1`) and all events
`A`, `B ⊆ {0, 1}^n`, `P(A □ B) ≤ P(A) P(B)`, where `A □ B` is the event that `A` and `B` occur on
disjoint sets of coordinates.

## Sources

- D. Reimer, *Proof of the van den Berg–Kesten conjecture*, Combin. Probab. Comput. 9 (2000), 27–32.

articles.title: Disjoint occurrence of an increasing and a decreasing event
articles.statement: For `A` increasing and `B` decreasing, `A □ B = A ∩ B`.

articles.title: Reimer's inequality for mixed monotone events, Bernoulli measure
articles.statement:
Reimer's inequality for an increasing and a decreasing event under the product Bernoulli
measure.

articles.title: Reimer's inequality for mixed monotone events, product weights
articles.statement:
Reimer's inequality for an increasing and a decreasing event under a product probability
weight.

articles.title: Harris–FKG inequality for an increasing and a decreasing event
articles.statement:
The Harris–FKG inequality for an increasing and a decreasing event: they are negatively
correlated.

articles.title: Harris–FKG inequality for increasing events
articles.statement:
The Harris–FKG inequality for a product probability weight: increasing events are positively
correlated.

articles.title: BK inequality for decreasing events
articles.statement:
The **BK inequality for decreasing events**: under the product Bernoulli(`p`) measure on a
finite set, `P_p(A □ B) ≤ P_p(A) * P_p(B)` for decreasing `A, B`.

articles.title: BK inequality for decreasing events under product weights
articles.statement:
The BK inequality for two decreasing events under a product probability weight, obtained
from `StatMech.bk_wprob_general` by flipping all coordinates.

articles.title: Flipping every coordinate of a configuration
articles.statement: The configuration with every coordinate flipped, `x ↦ !(ω x)`.

articles.title: Coordinate flip as an involutive equivalence
articles.statement: Flipping all coordinates, as an involutive equivalence of `ConfigSpace E`.

articles.title: Reimer's inequality for Bernoulli measures, assuming the core case
articles.statement:
Reimer's inequality `P_p(A □ B) ≤ P_p(A) * P_p(B)` for all events under the product
Bernoulli measure on a finite set, **assuming** `ReimerWprobCore`.

articles.title: Reimer's inequality
articles.statement:
**Reimer's inequality** (the van den Berg–Kesten conjecture, proved by Reimer 2000) for
product probability weights on `Fin n`: for every `n`, every weight `φ` with `φ ≥ 0` and
`φ i false + φ i true = 1`, and all events `A, B`, `wprob φ (A □ B) ≤ wprob φ A * wprob φ B`.

articles.title: Reimer's inequality for product weights, assuming the core case
articles.statement:
Reimer's inequality for product probability weights on any finite set, assuming
`ReimerWprobCore`.

articles.title: Reimer's inequality on the one-point configuration space
articles.statement: Reimer's inequality on the one-point configuration space `ConfigSpace (Fin 0)`.

articles.title: Reimer's inequality, ported hypothesis form
articles.statement:
Reimer's inequality in the form of the ported hypothesis `StatMech.ReimerWprobCore`
(definitionally `reimer_inequality`).

## Sources

- D. Reimer, *Proof of the van den Berg–Kesten conjecture*, Combin. Probab. Comput. 9 (2000), 27–32.

articles.title: Event that two coordinates agree
articles.statement: The event `ω 0 = ω 1` on two coordinates.

articles.title: Event that two coordinates differ
articles.statement: The event `ω 0 ≠ ω 1` on two coordinates.

articles.title: Negatively correlated events
articles.statement:
`A` and `B` are negatively correlated under the weight `φ`:
`wprob φ (A ∩ B) ≤ wprob φ A * wprob φ B`.

articles.title: Reimer's inequality for disjoint events
articles.statement:
Reimer's inequality for disjoint events under the product Bernoulli measure: both sides
are compared with `P(A □ B) = 0`.

articles.title: Reimer's inequality for negatively correlated events
articles.statement: Reimer's inequality for negatively correlated events (since `A □ B ⊆ A ∩ B`).

articles.title: Reimer's inequality for the XOR and XNOR events
articles.statement:
Reimer's inequality for `evXor` and `evXnor`, which are neither increasing nor decreasing
(and are disjoint).

articles.title: Slice inequalities in the one-coordinate BK induction step
articles.statement:
The slice inequalities of the one-coordinate BK induction step, with `A₀, A₁, B₀, B₁` the slices
at the first coordinate: `P(A₀ □ B₀) ≤ P((A₀ □ B₁) ∩ (A₁ □ B₀))` and
`P((A₀ □ B₁) ∪ (A₁ □ B₀)) ≤ P(A₁) P(B₁)`, for increasing events `A, B`.

articles.title: Weight of a family off one coordinate
articles.statement: `fmarg` with coordinate `i` omitted from the weights.

articles.title: Weight of a family of finsets
articles.statement: The weight `∑ S ∈ 𝒜, fwt w S` of a family.

articles.title: Product weight of a finset off one coordinate
articles.statement: The product weight of `S` over all coordinates except `i`.

articles.title: Product weight of a finset
articles.statement: The product weight `∏ x, w x (x ∈ S)` of the configuration with support `S`.

articles.title: First family in the weighted-pair counterexamples
articles.statement: The family `{∅, {0}}` on `Fin 2`, used in the counterexamples of this file.

articles.title: Second family in the weighted-pair counterexamples
articles.statement: The family `{∅}` on `Fin 2`, used in the counterexamples of this file.

articles.title: Down- and up-compressing two families can decrease disjoint pairs
articles.statement:
Down-compressing `𝒜` and up-compressing `ℬ` at the same coordinate can strictly decrease
the number of disjoint pairs.

articles.title: Box value of a doubled family under a symmetric weight
articles.statement: `(∏ x, w x true)^2 * #𝒰`: for a symmetric weight, the weight of a doubled family.

articles.title: Expansion of the Reimer deficit over one coordinate
articles.statement: The deficit `fmarg w 𝒜 * fmarg w ℬ - wdpairs w 𝒜 ℬ` expanded over coordinate `i`.

articles.title: Weighted number of disjoint pairs off one coordinate
articles.statement: `wdpairs` with coordinate `i` omitted from the weights.

articles.title: Weighted disjoint pairs bounded by the product of family weights
articles.statement:
For nonnegative weights, `wdpairs w 𝒜 ℬ ≤ fmarg w 𝒜 * fmarg w ℬ` (drop the disjointness
constraint).

articles.title: Box-value bound fails for non-symmetric weights
articles.statement: For a non-symmetric weight, `wdpairs w 𝒜 ℬ ≤ wboxValue w (boxDoubled 𝒜 ℬ)` can fail.

articles.title: Weighted number of disjoint pairs
articles.statement:
The weighted number of disjoint pairs: `∑ fwt w S * fwt w T` over disjoint
`(S, T) ∈ 𝒜 × ℬ`.

articles.title: Strassen's theorem on a finite poset, equal-mass form
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite partially
ordered set and let $p, q : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be nonnegative functions with
$\sum_{x \in \alpha} p(x) = \sum_{x \in \alpha} q(x)$. Then
$\sum_{x \in U} p(x) \le \sum_{x \in U} q(x)$ for every upper set $U \subseteq \alpha$ if and only
if there is a function $\pi : \alpha \times \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $\pi(x, y) \ge 0$
for all $x, y \in \alpha$, $\sum_{y \in \alpha} \pi(x, y) = p(x)$ for every $x \in \alpha$,
$\sum_{x \in \alpha} \pi(x, y) = q(y)$ for every $y \in \alpha$, and $\pi(x, y) = 0$ whenever
$x \not\le y$.

articles.title: Finite upper sets
articles.statement:
A finite subset $U$ of a preordered set $\alpha$ is an upper set (is
upward closed) if for all $x, y \in \alpha$ with $x \in U$ and $x \le y$, also $y \in U$.

articles.title: Strassen's theorem on a finite poset
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite partially ordered set and let
$p, q : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be probability mass functions, that is, nonnegative functions with
$\sum_{x \in \alpha} p(x) = 1$ and $\sum_{x \in \alpha} q(x) = 1$. Then
$\sum_{x \in U} p(x) \le \sum_{x \in U} q(x)$ for every upper set $U \subseteq \alpha$ if and only
if there is a function $\pi : \alpha \times \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $\pi(x, y) \ge 0$
for all $x, y \in \alpha$, $\sum_{y \in \alpha} \pi(x, y) = p(x)$ for every $x \in \alpha$,
$\sum_{x \in \alpha} \pi(x, y) = q(y)$ for every $y \in \alpha$, and $\pi(x, y) = 0$ whenever
$x \not\le y$.

## Sources

- V. Strassen, "The Existence of Probability Measures with Given Marginals", Ann. Math. Statist. 36 (1965), 423-439, DOI 10.1214/aoms/1177700153.

articles.title: Monotone coupling of two measures
articles.statement:
`κ` is a monotone coupling of `μ` and `ν`: a measure on pairs of configurations with first
marginal `μ`, second marginal `ν`, and no mass off the ordered pairs `ω ≤ ω'`.

articles.title: Set of coordinatewise ordered configuration pairs
articles.statement: The set of ordered pairs `(ω, ω')` of configurations with `ω ≤ ω'` coordinatewise.

articles.title: Existence of a monotone coupling implies stochastic domination
articles.statement: If a finite monotone coupling of `μ` and `ν` exists, then `μ ≼ ν`.

articles.title: Strassen's theorem, easy direction
articles.statement:
A finite monotone coupling of `μ` and `ν` shows `μ ≼ ν`: the easy direction of Strassen's
theorem.

articles.title: Marginals of a coupling have equal total mass
articles.statement: The two marginals of a coupling have the same total mass.

articles.title: Stochastic domination compares real-valued masses
articles.statement: For a finite upper measure, stochastic domination also compares real-valued masses.

articles.title: Stochastic domination is reflexive
articles.statement: Stochastic domination is reflexive.

articles.title: Stochastic domination of measures on configurations
articles.statement:
`μ` is stochastically dominated by `ν` if their actual `ENNReal` masses satisfy
`μ(A) ≤ ν(A)` for every measurable increasing event `A ⊆ ConfigSpace E`.

articles.title: Stochastic domination is transitive
articles.statement: Stochastic domination is transitive.

articles.title: Strassen's theorem
articles.statement:
**Strassen's theorem** on a finite poset `P`, for nonnegative vectors: if `μ` and `ν` have
equal total mass and `ν(D) ≤ μ(D)` for every down-set `D`, there is a nonnegative `c` on the
ordered pairs `x ≤ y` with first marginal `μ` and second marginal `ν`. This is the ordered-pair
vector form of
`MathlibExt.Probability.StrassenCouplingWanted.forall_isUpperSet_sum_le_iff_exists_coupling`.

articles.title: Strassen's theorem
articles.statement:
**Strassen's theorem** for configurations on a finite set: if `μ ≼ ν` are probability
measures on `ConfigSpace E`, there is a finite monotone coupling of `μ` and `ν`
(V. Strassen, *The existence of probability measures with given marginals*, 1965). The converse
is `StatMech.MonotoneCoupling.stochasticallyDominated`.

articles.title: Down-set of a partial order
articles.statement: `D` is a down-set of `P`: `x ≤ y` and `y ∈ D` imply `x ∈ D`.

articles.title: Measure on ordered pairs from a mass vector
articles.statement: The measure on pairs of configurations that puts mass `c q` on each ordered pair `q`.

articles.title: Ordered pairs of a partial order
articles.statement:
The ordered pairs `(x, y)` with `x ≤ y`; couplings supported on the order are vectors indexed
by `OrderPairs P`.

articles.title: Recurrence of the beta function in the first argument
Symmetry of the beta function
articles.statement: The beta function is symmetric.

articles.title: Beta-function identity for densities
articles.statement:
Multiplying the `Beta(α, β)` density by
`x ^ k (1 - x) ^ m` gives `B(α + k, β + m) / B(α, β)` times the `Beta(α + k, β + m)` density.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the beta density
articles.statement: The beta density is nonnegative for positive shape parameters.

articles.title: Integrals against the beta law
articles.statement:
An integral against `betaMeasure α β` is the integral of the function times the beta
density. No integrability hypothesis is needed: both sides are the junk value `0` together.

articles.title: Beta density integrates to one
articles.statement:
The beta density integrates to `1` (the Bochner-integral form of
`lintegral_betaPDF_eq_one`).

articles.title: Mean of the beta law
Mean of $X(1 - X)$ under a beta law
articles.statement:
For `α, β > 0`, `E[X (1 - X)] = α β / ((α + β) (α + β + 1))` (half the expected
heterozygosity of a `Beta(α, β)` allele frequency).

articles.title: Mixed moments of the beta law
articles.statement:
For `α, β > 0` and natural `k, m`,
`E[X ^ k (1 - X) ^ m] = B(α + k, β + m) / B(α, β)`.

articles.title: Second moment of the beta law
Chi-square distribution
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$, the chi-square law with $p$ degrees of
freedom is the gamma law on $\mathbb{R}$ with shape $p/2$ and rate $1/2$ (equivalently, scale $2$):
the measure with density $x \mapsto \frac{(1/2)^{p/2}}{\Gamma(p/2)} x^{p/2 - 1} e^{-x/2}$ for
$x > 0$ and $0$ for $x < 0$ with respect to Lebesgue measure.

For $p = 0$ the definition is degenerate: $\Gamma(0)$ is taken to be $0$ and division by $0$ gives
$0$, so the density vanishes and the measure is the zero measure rather than a point mass.

articles.title: The square of a standard normal variable is chi-square with one degree of freedom
articles.statement:
**The square of a standard normal variable is chi-square with one degree of freedom**, as
an identity of measures on `ℝ`. (Moved here from the likelihood-ratio development so that
both that development and Cochran's theorem reuse one declaration.)

articles.title: Exponential moments of the law of the square of a standard normal
articles.statement:
Let $\gamma$ be the
standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}$ (mean $0$, variance $1$) and let $\nu$ be its image under
$x \mapsto x^2$. For every real $t < 1/2$, the function $y \mapsto e^{t y}$ is integrable with
respect to $\nu$.

articles.title: Exponential moments of the chi-square distribution
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer and let
$\chi^2_p$ be the chi-square law with $p$ degrees of freedom. For every real $t < 1/2$, the
function $x \mapsto e^{t x}$ is integrable with respect to $\chi^2_p$.

articles.title: Exponential moments of the square of a standard normal
articles.statement:
Let $\gamma$ be the standard
Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}$ (mean $0$, variance $1$). For every real $t < 1/2$, the
function $x \mapsto e^{t x^2}$ is integrable with respect to $\gamma$.

articles.title: Moment generating function of the chi-square distribution
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer
and let $\chi^2_p$ be the chi-square law with $p$ degrees of freedom. For every real $t < 1/2$,
$\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{t x} \, d\chi^2_p(x) = \left(\frac{1/2}{1/2 - t}\right)^{p/2}$.

articles.title: Moment generating function of the gamma law with shape and rate one half
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be the
gamma law on $\mathbb{R}$ with shape $1/2$ and rate $1/2$. For every real $t < 1/2$,
$\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{t x} \, d\mu(x) = 1/\sqrt{1 - 2t}$.

This is the moment generating function of the square of a standard normal variable.

articles.title: Moment generating function of the law of the square of a standard normal
articles.statement:
Let $\gamma$
be the standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}$ (mean $0$, variance $1$) and let $\nu$ be its
image under $x \mapsto x^2$. For every real $t$, $\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{t y} \, d\nu(y) =
1/\sqrt{1 - 2t}$.

For $t \ge 1/2$ the integral diverges; the identity still holds there with the conventions that the
integral of a non-integrable function is $0$, that $\sqrt{s} = 0$ for $s \le 0$ and that $1/0 = 0$,
which make both sides $0$.

articles.title: Moment generating function of the square of a standard normal
articles.statement:
Let $\gamma$ be the
standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}$ (mean $0$, variance $1$). For every real $t$,
$\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{t x^2} \, d\gamma(x) = 1/\sqrt{1 - 2t}$.

For $t \ge 1/2$ the integral diverges; the identity still holds there with the conventions that the
integral of a non-integrable function is $0$, that $\sqrt{s} = 0$ for $s \le 0$ and that $1/0 = 0$,
which make both sides $0$.

articles.title: Chi-square moment generating functions multiply by adding degrees
articles.statement:
Chi-square MGFs multiply by adding degrees, below `1/2`. Requires a
nonempty index set so the summed degree stays positive.

articles.title: Closure of Gaussian processes under `L²` limits
articles.statement:
If each `X n` is a real Gaussian
process and `X n t → Y t` in `L²(P)` for every `t`, then `Y` is a Gaussian process.

articles.title: Closure of real Gaussian laws under `L²` limits
articles.statement:
If each `X n` is a real Gaussian random
variable and `X n → Y` in `L²(P)`, then `Y` is Gaussian.

articles.title: Closure of Gaussian laws under `L²` limits
articles.statement:
If each `X n` is a Gaussian random vector in
a separable Banach space `E` and `X n → Y` in `L²(P)`, then `Y` is Gaussian.

articles.title: Continuity of the second moment pairing in `L²`
articles.statement:
If `X n → Y` and `Z n → W` in `L²(P)`
(all square integrable), then `E[X n Z n] → E[Y W]`.

articles.title: The Dirichlet distribution is concentrated on the open simplex
articles.statement:
For every $n$ and every
parameter vector $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, almost every $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with
respect to the Dirichlet distribution $\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$ is a probability vector with positive
entries: $\theta_i > 0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_{i=0}^{n} \theta_i = 1$.

articles.title: Splitting off the first coordinate of the Dirichlet density
articles.statement:
Let
$\alpha = (\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n+1}) \in \mathbb{R}^{n+2}$, write $D_\alpha$ for the
unnormalized Dirichlet density with parameters $\alpha$ (a function on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$), and let
$\alpha' = (\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_{n+1}) \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$. For every real $t$ with
$0 < t < 1$ and every $u \in \mathbb{R}^n$,

$$D_\alpha(t, (1 - t) u) = t^{\alpha_0 - 1} (1 - t)^{\alpha_1 + \dots + \alpha_{n+1} - 1 - n}
D_{\alpha'}(u)$$

where $(t, (1 - t) u) \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is the vector with first coordinate $t$ followed by the
coordinates of $(1 - t) u$.

articles.title: Multiplying the Dirichlet density by a multinomial likelihood
articles.statement:
Let
$\alpha = (\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_n) \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ and let $k = (k_0, \dots, k_n)$ be
natural numbers; write $D_\beta$ for the unnormalized Dirichlet density with parameters $\beta$.
For every $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, let $\theta = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}, 1 - \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i)$ be
its completion to a vector summing to $1$, and write $\theta_i^+ = \max(\theta_i, 0)$. Then

$$D_\alpha(x) \prod_{i=0}^{n} (\theta_i^+)^{k_i} = D_{\alpha + k}(x).$$

Both sides vanish unless $x$ lies in the open corner simplex, where every $\theta_i$ is positive and
$\theta_i^+ = \theta_i$.

articles.title: Unnormalized Dirichlet density
articles.statement:
For parameters
$\alpha = (\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_n) \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, the unnormalized Dirichlet density is
the function $D_\alpha \colon \mathbb{R}^n \to [0, \infty]$ defined by

$$D_\alpha(x) = \Bigl(\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i^{\alpha_i - 1}\Bigr)
\Bigl(1 - \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i\Bigr)^{\alpha_n - 1}$$

when $x$ lies in the open corner simplex, that is $x_i > 0$ for every $i$ and
$\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i < 1$, and by $D_\alpha(x) = 0$ otherwise.

Here $x$ stands for the first $n$ coordinates of the probability vector
$(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}, 1 - \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i)$.

articles.title: Dirichlet distribution
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha = (\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_n) \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, let
$D_\alpha$ be the unnormalized Dirichlet density on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with parameters $\alpha$, and let
$B(\alpha) = \prod_{i=0}^{n} \Gamma(\alpha_i) / \Gamma(\sum_{i=0}^{n} \alpha_i)$ be the
multivariate Beta function. The Dirichlet distribution $\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$ is the measure on
$\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ obtained by pushing forward the measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with density
$D_\alpha(x) / B(\alpha)$ with respect to Lebesgue measure along the map
$x \mapsto (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}, 1 - \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i)$.

The quotient is taken in $[0, \infty]$, with a nonpositive $B(\alpha)$ read as $0$; this matters
only when some $\alpha_i \le 0$. For positive parameters $\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$ is a probability
measure concentrated on vectors with positive entries summing to $1$.

articles.title: Scaling the variable of a Lebesgue integral
articles.statement:
Let $F \colon \mathbb{R}^n \to [0, \infty]$ be
measurable and let $c > 0$ be a real number. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} F(y) \, dy = c^n \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} F(c u) \, du$$

where both integrals are taken with respect to Lebesgue measure.

articles.title: The Dirichlet integral for a single parameter
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha = (\alpha_0) \in \mathbb{R}^1$
with $\alpha_0 > 0$, let $D_\alpha$ be the unnormalized Dirichlet density with parameters
$\alpha$, a function on $\mathbb{R}^0$, and let $B(\alpha)$ be the multivariate Beta function.
Then $\int_{\mathbb{R}^0} D_\alpha(x) \, dx = B(\alpha)$, the integral being taken with respect to
Lebesgue measure.

Both sides equal $1$: $\mathbb{R}^0$ is a single point of measure $1$, $D_\alpha$ equals $1$ there,
and $B(\alpha) = \Gamma(\alpha_0) / \Gamma(\alpha_0)$.

articles.title: The Dirichlet integral
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha = (\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_n) \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with
$\alpha_i > 0$ for every $i$, and let
$\Delta = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : x_i > 0 \text{ for all } i \text{ and } \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i < 1\}$
be the open corner simplex. Then

$$\int_{\Delta} \Bigl(\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i^{\alpha_i - 1}\Bigr)
\Bigl(1 - \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i\Bigr)^{\alpha_n - 1} dx =
\frac{\prod_{i=0}^{n} \Gamma(\alpha_i)}{\Gamma\bigl(\sum_{i=0}^{n} \alpha_i\bigr)},$$

where $dx$ is Lebesgue measure. Equivalently, the integral of the unnormalized Dirichlet density
$D_\alpha$ over $\mathbb{R}^n$ equals the multivariate Beta function $B(\alpha)$.

articles.title: Mean of the Dirichlet distribution
articles.statement:
Let
$\alpha = (\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_n) \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with $\alpha_j > 0$ for every $j$. For
every $i$, the $i$-th coordinate of a random vector $\theta$ with the Dirichlet distribution
$\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$ has mean

$$\mathbb{E}[\theta_i] = \frac{\alpha_i}{\sum_{j=0}^{n} \alpha_j}.$$

Formally the left side is the integral of $\max(\theta_i, 0)$ with respect to
$\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$; this is the mean of $\theta_i$ because $\theta_i > 0$ almost surely.

articles.title: Tonelli's theorem for the first coordinate
articles.statement:
Let $G \colon \mathbb{R}^{n+1} \to [0, \infty]$
be measurable. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}} G(x) \, dx = \int_{\mathbb{R}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} G(t, y) \, dy \, dt$$

where $(t, y) \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ denotes the vector with first coordinate $t$ followed by the
coordinates of $y$, and all integrals are taken with respect to Lebesgue measure.

articles.title: The Beta integral
articles.statement:
For real numbers $a > 0$ and $b > 0$, the integral over the open
interval $(0, 1)$, taken as a Lebesgue integral with values in $[0, \infty]$, is

$$\int_0^1 t^{a-1} (1 - t)^{b-1} \, dt = B(a, b),$$

where $B(a, b) = \Gamma(a) \Gamma(b) / \Gamma(a + b)$ is the Beta function.

articles.title: Multivariate Beta function
articles.statement:
For real parameters
$\alpha = (\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_{n-1})$, the multivariate Beta function is

$$B(\alpha) = \frac{\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} \Gamma(\alpha_i)}{\Gamma(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \alpha_i)}.$$

It is the normalizing constant of the Dirichlet distribution.

articles.title: Simplex completion
articles.statement:
For $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}) \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the simplex
completion of $x$ is the vector
$(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}, 1 - \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i) \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, whose coordinates sum
to $1$.

articles.title: Dirichlet–multinomial conjugacy
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha = (\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_n)$ have positive
real entries and let $k = (k_0, \dots, k_n)$ be natural numbers (counts). The measure with density
$\theta \mapsto \prod_{i=0}^{n} \max(\theta_i, 0)^{k_i}$ with respect to the Dirichlet distribution
$\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$, that is, $\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$ weighted by the likelihood of the counts
$k$, equals

$$\frac{B(\alpha + k)}{B(\alpha)} \, \mathrm{Dir}(\alpha + k),$$

where $B$ is the multivariate Beta function and $\alpha + k$ is taken entrywise.

articles.title: Exponential density as an indicator on the half-line
articles.statement: The rate-`r` exponential density times `f`, as an indicator on `Ici 0`.

articles.title: Integrability criterion for the exponential law
articles.statement:
A function is integrable against the exponential law of rate `r > 0` iff
`r * exp (-(r * x)) * f x` is integrable on `(0, ∞)`.

articles.title: Integrability of the identity under the exponential law
articles.statement: The identity is integrable against the exponential law.

articles.title: Exponentially distributed random variables are integrable
articles.statement: A random variable with exponential law of rate `r > 0` is integrable.

articles.title: Finiteness of all moments of the exponential law
articles.statement: All moments of the exponential law are finite.

articles.title: Mean of an exponentially distributed random variable
articles.statement: A random variable with exponential law of rate `r > 0` has mean `r⁻¹`.

articles.title: Integrals against the exponential law
articles.statement:
Integrals against the exponential law of rate `r > 0` are integrals of
`r * exp (-(r * x)) * f x` over `(0, ∞)`.

articles.title: Mean of the exponential law
articles.statement: The mean of the exponential law of rate `r > 0` is `r⁻¹`.

articles.title: Moments of the exponential law
articles.statement: The `n`-th moment of the exponential law of rate `r > 0` is `n! / r ^ n`.

articles.title: Second moment of the exponential law
articles.statement: The second moment of the exponential law of rate `r > 0` is `2 / r ^ 2`.

articles.title: Power times exponential density in gamma-integrand form
articles.statement: Rewriting `x ^ n` times the exponential density in the gamma-integrand form.

articles.title: Variance of an exponentially distributed random variable
articles.statement: A random variable with exponential law of rate `r > 0` has variance `r⁻¹ ^ 2`.

articles.title: Variance of the exponential law
articles.statement: The variance of the exponential law of rate `r > 0` is `r⁻¹ ^ 2`.

articles.title: Gamma law is concentrated on the nonnegative reals
articles.statement: The Gamma law is concentrated on `[0, ∞)`.

articles.title: Moment generating function determines the gamma law
articles.statement:
MGF uniqueness for gamma laws: a real probability law whose MGF equals the gamma `(a, r)`
MGF as a function on all of `ℝ` (both vanish where the exponential moment is infinite) is that
gamma law.

articles.title: Gamma function at $a + k$ via the rising factorial
articles.statement: `Γ(a + k) = a⁽ᵏ⁾ Γ(a)` for `a > 0`.

articles.title: Scaling a gamma random variable
articles.statement:
Scaling a gamma variable by `c > 0` keeps its shape and divides its rate by `c`:
`c X ~ Gamma(a, r / c)` when `X ~ Gamma(a, r)`.

articles.title: Erlang tail formula
articles.statement:
The Erlang tail: for shape `n + 1`, `P(X > c) = e^{-r c} ∑_{k = 0}^{n} (r c) ^ k / (k!)`
when `c ≥ 0`.

articles.title: Upper tail of the gamma law
articles.statement: The upper tail of the gamma law: `P(X > c) = Γ(a, r c) / Γ(a)` for `c ≥ 0`.

articles.title: Half-line of exponential integrability for the gamma distribution
articles.statement:
Let $a > 0$ and
$r > 0$, and let $S$ be the set of real $t$ such that $x \mapsto e^{tx}$ is integrable with respect
to the gamma distribution with shape $a$ and rate $r$. Then the half-line $(-\infty, r)$ is
contained in $S$.

articles.title: Exponential moments of the gamma distribution
articles.statement:
Let $a > 0$ and $r > 0$. For every real
$t < r$, the function $x \mapsto e^{tx}$ is integrable with respect to the gamma distribution with
shape $a$ and rate $r$.

articles.title: Exponential moments of the gamma law are finite exactly below the rate
articles.statement:
The exponential moment `E[exp (t X)]` of a gamma `(a, r)` law is finite exactly for
`t < r`.

articles.title: Gamma law has finite first moment
articles.statement: `x ↦ x` is integrable for `Gamma(a, b)`.

articles.title: Integrability of the scaled gamma integrand
articles.statement:
For real numbers $a > 0$ and $s > 0$, the
function $x \mapsto x^{a-1} e^{-sx}$ is Lebesgue integrable on the open half-line $(0, \infty)$.

This generalizes the convergence of the integral $\int_0^\infty x^{a-1} e^{-x} \, dx$ defining
$\Gamma(a)$, which is the case $s = 1$.

articles.title: Integrability of $x^k e^{-cx}$ under the Gamma law
articles.statement: For `a, b > 0` and `c ≥ 0`, `x ↦ x ^ k e^{-c x}` is integrable for `Gamma(a, b)`.

articles.title: Gamma law has finite second moment
articles.statement: `x ↦ x²` is integrable for `Gamma(a, b)`.

articles.title: Mean of the gamma law
articles.statement: The mean of the gamma law with shape `a > 0` and rate `r > 0` is `a / r`.

articles.title: Gamma integrals
articles.statement:
For shape `a > 0`, rate `b > 0` and `c ≥ 0`,
`∫ x ^ k e^{-c x} dGamma(a, b) = a⁽ᵏ⁾ bᵃ / (b + c) ^ (a + k)`.

articles.title: Real moments of the gamma law
articles.statement:
Real moments of the gamma law: for shape `a > 0`, rate `r > 0` and `p > -a`,
`E[X ^ p] = Γ(a + p) / (Γ(a) r ^ p)`. (The law is carried by `[0, ∞)`, so the values of
`x ^ p` for `x < 0` play no role.)

articles.title: Second moment of the gamma law
articles.statement:
The second moment of the gamma law with shape `a > 0` and rate `r > 0` is
`a (a + 1) / r ^ 2`.

articles.title: A neighbourhood of zero of exponential integrability for the gamma distribution
articles.statement:
Let
$a > 0$, $r > 0$ and $0 < \varepsilon < r$, and let $S$ be the set of real $t$ such that
$x \mapsto e^{tx}$ is integrable with respect to the gamma distribution with shape $a$ and rate
$r$. Then the interval $(-\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$ is contained in the interior of $S$.

This is the form of hypothesis used to identify a distribution from its moment generating
function on such an interval.

articles.title: Gamma law has finite second moment
articles.statement: The gamma law has finite second moment.

articles.title: Moment generating function of the gamma distribution
articles.statement:
Let $a > 0$ and $r > 0$, and let
$X$ have the gamma distribution with shape $a$ and rate $r$. For every real $t < r$, the moment
generating function of $X$ at $t$ is $\mathbb{E}[e^{tX}] = \left(\frac{r}{r - t}\right)^a$.

articles.title: $r^k r^{a-1} = r^{a+k-1}$ for nonnegative $r$
Recurrence for the upper incomplete gamma function
articles.statement:
The recurrence `Γ(a + 1, x) = x ^ a e^{-x} + a Γ(a, x)` for `a > 0` and `x ≥ 0`
(DLMF 8.8.2), from integration by parts.

articles.title: Upper incomplete gamma function at natural shapes
articles.statement:
The closed form at natural shapes (DLMF 8.4.8): for `x ≥ 0`,
`Γ(n + 1, x) = n! e^{-x} ∑_{k = 0}^{n} x ^ k / (k!)`.

articles.title: Upper incomplete gamma function with shape one
Upper incomplete gamma function at zero
Upper incomplete gamma function
articles.statement:
The upper incomplete gamma function `Γ(a, x) = ∫_x^∞ t ^ (a - 1) e^{-t} dt` (DLMF 8.2.2).
The domain used below is `a > 0` and `x ≥ 0`, where the integral converges. Outside it the
Bochner integral may be the junk value `0` (for `a ≤ 0`, `x = 0` the integrand is not
integrable).

articles.title: Variance of the gamma law
articles.statement: The variance of the gamma law with shape `a > 0` and rate `r > 0` is `a / r ^ 2`.

articles.title: Horizontal block matrix
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$, $\iota$ and $\kappa$ be index sets with $\iota$ and
$\kappa$ finite. For real matrices $P$ with rows indexed by $\rho$ and columns by $\iota$, and $Q$
with rows indexed by $\rho$ and columns by $\kappa$, the block row $[P\ Q]$ is the real matrix with
rows indexed by $\rho$ and columns indexed by the disjoint union $\iota \sqcup \kappa$, whose
entry in row $r$ is $P_{ri}$ in the column of $i \in \iota$ and $Q_{rk}$ in the column of
$k \in \kappa$.

articles.title: Characteristic function of a product of blocks
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ and $\kappa$ be finite index
sets, let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be finite measures on $\mathbb{R}^\iota$ and $\mathbb{R}^\kappa$, and let
$\pi$ be the pushforward of the product measure $\mu \otimes \nu$ to
$\mathbb{R}^{\iota \sqcup \kappa}$ under concatenation of the two blocks. Write $\varphi_\rho$ for
the characteristic function of a measure $\rho$. Then for every
$t \in \mathbb{R}^{\iota \sqcup \kappa}$ with blocks $t_\iota \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$ and
$t_\kappa \in \mathbb{R}^\kappa$, we have
$\varphi_\pi(t) = \varphi_\mu(t_\iota) \, \varphi_\nu(t_\kappa)$.

articles.title: Conditioning on a signal observed in independent additive noise
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be a nonempty
standard Borel space that is an abelian group with measurable addition, let $F$ be a measurable
space, and let $Y \colon \Omega \to F$ and $Z \colon \Omega \to E$ be independent measurable random
variables on a probability space. For every measurable $f \colon F \to E$ and almost every $y$
with respect to the law of $Y$, the conditional distribution of $f(Y) + Z$ given $Y = y$ is the
law of $f(y) + Z$.

articles.title: Bayes' theorem for a linear-Gaussian observation
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $p$ be finite index sets,
and let $x$ and $v$ be independent measurable random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mathbb{R}^p$
on a probability space, with $x \sim N(m, S)$ and $v \sim N(0, R)$ for positive semidefinite
matrices $S$ and $R$. Let $H$ be a real $p \times n$ matrix such that $H S H^\top + R$ is
invertible, and let $Y = H x + v$. Then for almost every $y$ with respect to the law of $Y$, the
conditional distribution of $x$ given $Y = y$ is the Gaussian with mean
$m + S H^\top (H S H^\top + R)^{-1} (y - H m)$ and covariance
$S - S H^\top (H S H^\top + R)^{-1} H S$.

articles.title: Gaussian conditioning (Schur complement)
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ and $\kappa$ be finite index sets
and let $V$ be a measurable random vector in $\mathbb{R}^{\iota \sqcup \kappa}$ on a probability
space, with blocks $X \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$ and $Y \in \mathbb{R}^\kappa$. Suppose $V$ has law
$N(\mu, S)$ with $S$ positive semidefinite, write $\mu_X, \mu_Y$ for the blocks of $\mu$ and
$S_{11}, S_{12}, S_{21}, S_{22}$ for the blocks of $S$ indexed by $\iota \times \iota$,
$\iota \times \kappa$, $\kappa \times \iota$ and $\kappa \times \kappa$, and suppose $S_{22}$ is
invertible. Then for almost every $y$ with respect to the law of $Y$, the conditional
distribution of $X$ given $Y = y$ is
$N(\mu_X + S_{12} S_{22}^{-1} (y - \mu_Y), S_{11} - S_{12} S_{22}^{-1} S_{21})$.

articles.title: Gaussian conditioning
articles.statement:
Let $E$ and $F$ be finite-dimensional real inner product spaces,
and let $X$ and $Y$ be measurable random vectors in $E$ and $F$ on a probability space such that
$(X, Y)$ is jointly Gaussian. Let $A \colon F \to E$ be a linear map whose residual $X - A Y$ is
uncorrelated with $Y$ (the normal equations): for all $u \in E$ and $w \in F$,
$\operatorname{Cov}(\langle u, X - A Y \rangle, \langle w, Y \rangle) = 0$. Then $X - A Y$ is
Gaussian and independent of $Y$, and for almost every $y$ with respect to the law of $Y$, the
conditional distribution of $X$ given $Y = y$ is the law of $A y + (X - A Y)$.

articles.title: Covariances of linear functionals of a Gaussian vector
articles.statement:
Let $\nu$ be a finite index set
and let $V$ be a measurable random vector in $\mathbb{R}^\nu$ on a probability space with law
$N(\mu, S)$, where $S$ is positive semidefinite. Then for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^\nu$,
$\operatorname{Cov}(\langle a, V \rangle, \langle b, V \rangle) = a^\top S b$.

articles.title: Block-triangular congruence of a block-diagonal matrix
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $p$ be finite index
sets and let $S$, $R$ and $H$ be real matrices of sizes $n \times n$, $p \times p$ and
$p \times n$. Let $M$ be the block matrix with block rows $(I_n, 0)$ and $(H, I_p)$, and let $D$
be the block-diagonal matrix with diagonal blocks $S$ and $R$. Then $M D M^\top$ is the block
matrix with block rows $(S, S H^\top)$ and $(H S, H S H^\top + R)$.

When $x$ and $v$ are independent random vectors with covariances $S$ and $R$, this is the joint
covariance of $(x, H x + v)$.

articles.title: The inner product splits over blocks
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ and $\kappa$ be finite index sets. For
$p_1 \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$, $p_2 \in \mathbb{R}^\kappa$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}^{\iota \sqcup \kappa}$
with blocks $t_\iota \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$ and $t_\kappa \in \mathbb{R}^\kappa$, the inner product
of the concatenation of $p_1$ and $p_2$ with $t$ is
$\langle p_1, t_\iota \rangle + \langle p_2, t_\kappa \rangle$.

articles.title: Translating a multivariate Gaussian
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite index set. For all
$c, \mu \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$ and every real $\iota \times \iota$ matrix $S$, the pushforward of
$N(\mu, S)$ under the translation $x \mapsto c + x$ is $N(c + \mu, S)$.

No positive semidefiniteness is assumed: when $S$ is not positive semidefinite, $N(\mu, S)$ is
taken to be the point mass at $\mu$.

articles.title: The marginal of a linear-Gaussian model
articles.statement:
Write $\mathcal{N}(a, \Sigma)$ for the
multivariate Gaussian distribution with mean $a$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma$. Let $n$ and $p$
be finite index sets, and let $x$ and $w$ be independent measurable random vectors in
$\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mathbb{R}^p$ on a probability space, where $x$ has law
$\mathcal{N}(m, S)$ and $w$ has law $\mathcal{N}(c, Q)$ for positive semidefinite real matrices
$S$ and $Q$. Then for every real $p \times n$ matrix $F$, the random vector $F x + w$ has law
$\mathcal{N}(F m + c, F S F^\top + Q)$.

articles.title: Concatenation of independent Gaussian random vectors
articles.statement:
Write $\mathcal{N}(a, \Sigma)$ for
the multivariate Gaussian distribution with mean $a$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma$. Let $\iota$
and $\kappa$ be finite index sets, and let $x$ and $v$ be independent measurable random vectors in
$\mathbb{R}^\iota$ and $\mathbb{R}^\kappa$ on a probability space, with laws $\mathcal{N}(m, S)$
and $\mathcal{N}(m', R)$ for positive semidefinite real matrices $S$ and $R$. Then the
concatenated random vector $(x, v)$ in $\mathbb{R}^{\iota \sqcup \kappa}$ has law
$\mathcal{N}\left((m, m'), \begin{pmatrix} S & 0 \\ 0 & R \end{pmatrix}\right)$.

articles.title: Independent Gaussian blocks
articles.statement:
Write $\mathcal{N}(a, \Sigma)$ for the multivariate
Gaussian distribution with mean $a$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma$. Let $\iota$ and $\kappa$ be
finite index sets, let $m \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$ and $m' \in \mathbb{R}^\kappa$, and let $S$ and
$R$ be positive semidefinite real matrices indexed by $\iota$ and by $\kappa$. Then the image of
the product measure $\mathcal{N}(m, S) \otimes \mathcal{N}(m', R)$ under the concatenation map
$\mathbb{R}^\iota \times \mathbb{R}^\kappa \to \mathbb{R}^{\iota \sqcup \kappa}$ is
$\mathcal{N}\left((m, m'), \begin{pmatrix} S & 0 \\ 0 & R \end{pmatrix}\right)$.

articles.title: Linear images of multivariate Gaussians
articles.statement:
Write $\mathcal{N}(a, \Sigma)$ for the
multivariate Gaussian distribution with mean $a$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma$. Let $\iota$ and
$\kappa$ be finite index sets, let $M$ be a real $\iota \times \kappa$ matrix, let
$\mu \in \mathbb{R}^\kappa$ and let $S$ be a positive semidefinite real $\kappa \times \kappa$
matrix. Then the image of $\mathcal{N}(\mu, S)$ under the linear map $z \mapsto M z$ is
$\mathcal{N}(M \mu, M S M^\top)$.

articles.title: The additive-noise kernel
articles.statement:
Let $E$ be an additive commutative group with a measurable
structure for which addition $E \times E \to E$ is measurable, let $F$ be a measurable space, let
$f \colon F \to E$ be a measurable map and let $\nu$ be a measure on $E$. If $\nu$ is s-finite,
the additive-noise kernel from $F$ to $E$ sends $y \in F$ to the image of the product measure
$\delta_{f(y)} \otimes \nu$ (where $\delta_{f(y)}$ is the Dirac measure at $f(y)$) under addition
$(a, z) \mapsto a + z$, that is, to the image of $\nu$ under $z \mapsto f(y) + z$. If $\nu$ is not
s-finite, it is the zero kernel.

When $\nu$ is a probability measure, the kernel sends $y$ to the law of $f(y) + Z$ for a random
variable $Z$ with law $\nu$.

articles.title: The joint covariance of a linear-Gaussian model is positive semidefinite
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $p$
be finite index sets, let $S$ and $R$ be positive semidefinite real matrices indexed by $n$ and by
$p$, and let $H$ be a real $p \times n$ matrix. Then the block matrix
$\begin{pmatrix} S & S H^\top \\ H S & H S H^\top + R \end{pmatrix}$, indexed by $n \sqcup p$, is
positive semidefinite.

articles.title: Block-diagonal matrices with positive semidefinite blocks
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ and $\kappa$ be
finite index sets and let $S$ and $R$ be positive semidefinite real matrices indexed by $\iota$
and by $\kappa$. Then the block-diagonal matrix $\begin{pmatrix} S & 0 \\ 0 & R \end{pmatrix}$,
indexed by $\iota \sqcup \kappa$, is positive semidefinite.

articles.title: The posterior covariance is positive semidefinite
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $p$ be finite index sets,
let $S$ be a positive semidefinite real $n \times n$ matrix, let $R$ be a positive definite real
$p \times p$ matrix and let $H$ be a real $p \times n$ matrix. Then
$S - S H^\top (H S H^\top + R)^{-1} H S$ is positive semidefinite.

This matrix is the Schur complement of the lower-right block in the joint covariance
$\begin{pmatrix} S & S H^\top \\ H S & H S H^\top + R \end{pmatrix}$ of a linear-Gaussian model.

articles.title: The affine change of variables as a measurable equivalence
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite type,
$\mu \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$ and $A$ a real $\iota \times \iota$ matrix with nonzero determinant. The
map $x \mapsto \mu + Ax$ is a measurable equivalence of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^\iota$ with
itself, with inverse $y \mapsto A^{-1}(y - \mu)$.

articles.title: Lebesgue measure under an invertible affine map
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite type,
$\mu \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$ and $A$ a real $\iota \times \iota$ matrix with nonzero determinant. The
pushforward of Lebesgue measure on the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^\iota$ under the measurable
equivalence $x \mapsto \mu + Ax$ equals $|\det A|^{-1}$ times Lebesgue measure.

articles.title: Pushforward of a measure with density
articles.statement:
Let $e : \alpha 	o  eta$ be a measurable
equivalence between measurable spaces, $
u$ a measure on $\alpha$ and $g : \alpha 	o [0, \infty]$
any function. Then the pushforward under $e$ of the measure with density $g$ with respect to $
u$
is the measure with density $g \circ e^{-1}$ with respect to the pushforward $e_*
u$ of $
u$.

articles.title: The multivariate Gaussian density
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite set of size $n$, let
$\mu \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$ and let $S$ be a positive definite real $\iota \times \iota$ matrix. Then
the multivariate Gaussian measure on the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^\iota$ with mean $\mu$ and
covariance matrix $S$ (the image of the standard Gaussian under $x \mapsto \mu + S^{1/2} x$) has
density

$$\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{n/2} \sqrt{\det S}} \exp\left(-\frac{(x - \mu)^\top S^{-1} (x - \mu)}{2}\right)$$

with respect to Lebesgue measure.

articles.title: Multivariate Gaussian density function
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite set of size $n$. For
$\mu, x \in \mathbb{R}^\iota$ and a real $\iota \times \iota$ matrix $S$, this is the real number

$$\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{n/2}\sqrt{\det S}} \exp\left(-\frac{(x - \mu)^\top S^{-1}(x - \mu)}{2}\right).$$

It is defined for every $S$, with the conventions $\sqrt{t} = 0$ for $t < 0$, $1/0 = 0$ and
$S^{-1} = 0$ for singular $S$, so its value is $0$ when $\det S \le 0$.

articles.title: Quadratic form of the inverse square root
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite type, $S$ a positive
definite real $\iota \times \iota$ matrix and $S^{1/2}$ its positive semidefinite square root. Then
for every $u$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^\iota$,
$\|(S^{1/2})^{-1} u\|^2 = u^\top S^{-1} u$.

articles.title: Sheppard's formula (Gaussian arcsine law)
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a real number with $-1 < \rho < 1$,
and let $\gamma$ be the multivariate Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with mean $0$ and
covariance matrix whose diagonal entries are $1$ and whose off-diagonal entries are $\rho$ (the
law of a standard bivariate normal vector with correlation $\rho$). Then the open first quadrant
$\{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : x_1 > 0,\ x_2 > 0\}$ has $\gamma$-probability
$\frac{1}{4} + \frac{\arcsin \rho}{2\pi}$.

## Sources

- Y. L. Tong, The Multivariate Normal Distribution, Springer, 1990, Ch. 3; W. F. Sheppard, "On the application of the theory of error to cases of normal distribution and normal correlation", Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. A 192 (1899), 101–167; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multivariate_normal_distribution

articles.title: Standard Gaussian measure via its density
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite set of size $n$. This is
the measure on the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^\iota$ with density
$v \mapsto (2\pi)^{-n/2} \exp(-\|v\|^2/2)$ with respect to Lebesgue measure.

articles.title: The standard Gaussian has a density
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite set of size $n$. The standard
Gaussian measure on the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^\iota$ has density
$v \mapsto (2\pi)^{-n/2} \exp(-\|v\|^2/2)$ with respect to Lebesgue measure.

articles.title: Standard Gaussian density function
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ be a finite set of size $n$. The standard
Gaussian density on the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^\iota$ is the real-valued function
$v \mapsto (2\pi)^{-n/2} \exp(-\|v\|^2/2)$.

articles.title: Continuity of the Poisson distribution function in the mean
articles.statement: The distribution function is continuous in the mean.

articles.title: Poisson–Gamma duality
articles.statement:
The Gamma law of shape `k + 1` and rate `r` (Mathlib's
`gammaMeasure`) has upper tail `P(Gamma(k + 1, r) > x) = F_k(r x)`. This is the Erlang tail
`gammaMeasure_real_Ioi_natCast_add_one` in `GammaMoments`, rewritten with the definition of
`poissonCDF`.

articles.title: Exact coverage of Garwood's bound
articles.statement:
For every mean `r ≥ 0` and `0 < α < 1`,
`P_r(r ≤ u_α(K)) ≥ 1 - α` when `K ~ Poisson(r)`.

articles.title: Positivity of the Garwood upper bound
articles.statement: The bound is positive for `0 < α < 1`.

articles.title: Garwood upper bound is strictly increasing in the count
articles.statement: The bound is strictly increasing in the observed count.

articles.title: Garwood upper bound after observing zero
articles.statement: After observing `0` the bound is `u_α(0) = log (1 / α)` (`e^{-u} = α`).

articles.title: Garwood's exact upper confidence bound
articles.statement:
**Garwood's exact upper confidence bound** for a Poisson mean after observing `k`, at
level `α`: `u_α(k) = sup {x ≥ 0 | α ≤ F_k(x)}`. For `0 < α < 1` it is the root of
`F_k(u) = α` (`poissonCDF_garwoodUpper`).

articles.title: Derivative of the Poisson distribution function in the mean
articles.statement: The derivative in the mean telescopes: `∂_x F_k(x) = -e^{-x} x^k / (k!)`.

articles.title: Means below the Garwood upper bound are exactly the non-rejected ones
articles.statement: A nonnegative mean lies below the bound iff it is not rejected: `x ≤ u_α(k) ↔ α ≤ F_k(x)`.

articles.title: Garwood upper bound solves the distribution function equation
articles.statement: The bound solves `F_k(u_α(k)) = α`.

articles.title: Poisson distribution function is strictly increasing in the count
articles.statement: The distribution function is strictly increasing in `k` at every positive mean.

articles.title: Poisson distribution function is monotone in the count
articles.statement: The distribution function is monotone in `k` at every nonnegative mean.

articles.title: Positivity of the Poisson distribution function
articles.statement: The distribution function is positive at every nonnegative real mean.

articles.title: Poisson distribution function is strictly decreasing in the mean
articles.statement: The distribution function is strictly decreasing in the mean on `[0, ∞)`.

articles.title: Poisson distribution function at mean zero
articles.statement: At mean `0` the Poisson law is the point mass at `0`: `F_k(0) = 1`.

articles.title: Poisson distribution function at count zero
Poisson distribution function as a function of the mean
articles.statement:
The Poisson distribution function `F_k(x) = ∑_{j ≤ k} e^{-x} x^j / (j!)` as a function of
the mean `x` (defined for every real `x`; it is a probability only for `0 ≤ x`).

articles.title: Poisson distribution function agrees with the Poisson law
articles.statement: `poissonCDF r k` is the distribution function of Mathlib's `poissonMeasure r` at `k`.

articles.title: Super-uniformity of the distribution-function transform
articles.statement:
For `K ~ Poisson(r)` and
every `α ≥ 0`, `P(F_r(K) ≤ α) ≤ α`. (For `α < 0` the event is empty.)

articles.title: Poisson distribution function vanishes as the mean grows
articles.statement: For fixed `k`, `F_k(x) → 0` as the mean `x → ∞`.

articles.title: Poisson distribution function tends to one as the count grows
articles.statement: For a fixed nonnegative mean, `F_k(x) → 1` as `k → ∞`.

articles.title: Second factorial moment of the binomial law
Second factorial moment of a binomial random variable
articles.statement:
If `X` has law `Bin(ℝ, n, p)`
then `E[X (X - 1)] = n (n - 1) p²`.

articles.title: Second moment of the binomial law
articles.statement: `E[X²] = n p (1 - p) + (n p)²`.

articles.title: Second moment of a binomial random variable
articles.statement:
If `X` has law `Bin(ℝ, n, p)` then
`E[X²] = n p (1 - p) + (n p)²`.

articles.title: Variance of the binomial law
articles.statement: `Var X = n p (1 - p)`.

articles.title: Variance of a binomial random variable
articles.statement:
If `X` has law `Bin(ℝ, n, p)` then
`Var X = n p (1 - p)`.

articles.title: Probability of an event under the uniform distribution
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite
type carrying a σ-algebra. For every measurable set $s \subseteq \alpha$, the probability measure
associated to the uniform distribution on $\alpha$ gives $s$ the measure $|s| / |\alpha|$, computed
in the extended nonnegative reals.

articles.title: Outer measure of an event under the uniform distribution
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite
type. For every subset $s \subseteq \alpha$, the outer measure associated to the uniform
distribution on $\alpha$ assigns to $s$ the value $|s| / |\alpha|$, computed in the extended
nonnegative reals.

articles.title: Uniform distribution on the whole finite type
articles.statement:
For a nonempty finite type $\alpha$, the
uniform distribution on the finite set of all elements of $\alpha$ equals the uniform
distribution on $\alpha$.

articles.title: Uniform distribution on a finite set
articles.statement:
For a nonempty finite subset $s$ of a type $\alpha$,
the uniform distribution on $s$ is the probability mass function on $\alpha$ that gives mass
$1/|s|$ to each element of $s$ and mass $0$ to every other element of $\alpha$.

articles.title: Uniform distribution on a finite type
articles.statement:
For a nonempty finite type $\alpha$, the uniform
distribution on $\alpha$ is the probability mass function on $\alpha$ that gives mass $1/|\alpha|$
to every element of $\alpha$.

articles.title: Additivity of expectation on a finite type
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite set with a
$\sigma$-algebra in which singletons are measurable, let $p$ be a probability mass function on
$\alpha$, and write $\mathbb{E}_p[h]$ for the expectation of $h : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ under $p$.
For all $f, g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{E}_p[f + g] = \mathbb{E}_p[f] + \mathbb{E}_p[g]$.

No integrability hypothesis is needed.

articles.title: Homogeneity of expectation on a finite type
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite set with a
$\sigma$-algebra in which singletons are measurable, let $p$ be a probability mass function on
$\alpha$, and write $\mathbb{E}_p[h]$ for the expectation of $h : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ under $p$.
For every $c \in \mathbb{R}$ and $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, the function $a \mapsto c\,f(a)$ has
expectation $c\,\mathbb{E}_p[f]$.

articles.title: Expectation of a constant on a finite type
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite set with a
$\sigma$-algebra in which singletons are measurable and let $p$ be a probability mass function on
$\alpha$. For every $c \in \mathbb{R}$, the expectation of the constant function $a \mapsto c$
under $p$ is $c$.

articles.title: Additivity of extended expectation
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a set
$\alpha$, and write $\overline{\mathbb{E}}_p[h]$ for the extended expectation of
$h : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$ under $p$. For all $f, g : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$,
$\overline{\mathbb{E}}_p[f + g] = \overline{\mathbb{E}}_p[f] + \overline{\mathbb{E}}_p[g]$.

No finiteness or integrability hypothesis is needed: sums of terms in $[0, \infty]$ always
converge.

articles.title: Extended expectation of a constant
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a set
$\alpha$. For every $c \in [0, \infty]$, the extended expectation of the constant function
$a \mapsto c$ under $p$ is $c$.

The set $\alpha$ need not be finite.

articles.title: Extended expectation under a finitely supported distribution
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability
mass function on a set $\alpha$, and let $s \subseteq \alpha$ be a finite set with $p(a) = 0$ for
every $a \notin s$. For every $f : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$, the extended expectation of $f$
under $p$ equals $\sum_{a \in s} p(a)\, f(a)$.

The set $\alpha$ itself need not be finite.

articles.title: Extended expectation on a finite set
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a finite
set $\alpha$. For every $f : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$, the extended expectation of $f$ under $p$
equals the finite sum $\sum_{a \in \alpha} p(a)\, f(a)$.

articles.title: Change of variables for extended expectation
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a
set $\alpha$, let $g : \alpha \to \beta$ be a map to a set $\beta$, and let $g_* p$ be the
pushforward of $p$ along $g$, the probability mass function $b \mapsto \sum_{a : g(a) = b} p(a)$.
For every $f : \beta \to [0, \infty]$, the extended expectation of $f$ under $g_* p$ equals the
extended expectation of $f \circ g$ under $p$.

No finiteness or measurability hypothesis is needed: both sides are sums of terms in
$[0, \infty]$, whose order of summation can be interchanged freely.

articles.title: Extended and real expectations agree on natural-valued functions
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite
set with a $\sigma$-algebra in which singletons are measurable, let $p$ be a probability mass
function on $\alpha$, and let $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$. Let $x \in [0, \infty]$ be the
extended expectation of $g$, viewed as a function to $[0, \infty]$, under $p$, and send $x$ to
$\mathbb{R}$ by the map that is the identity on $[0, \infty)$ and sends $\infty$ to $0$. The
result is the expectation of $g$, viewed as a real-valued function, under $p$.

articles.title: Extended expectation of a finite sum
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a set
$\alpha$, and write $\overline{\mathbb{E}}_p[h]$ for the extended expectation of
$h : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$ under $p$. For every index set $\iota$, finite subset
$s \subseteq \iota$ and family of functions $f_i : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$ ($i \in \iota$),
$\overline{\mathbb{E}}_p\bigl[a \mapsto \sum_{i \in s} f_i(a)\bigr] =
\sum_{i \in s} \overline{\mathbb{E}}_p[f_i]$.

The set $\alpha$ need not be finite.

articles.title: Extended expectation under the uniform distribution
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite type
and $f : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$. The extended expectation of $f$ under the uniform distribution on
$\alpha$ equals $|\alpha|^{-1} \sum_{a \in \alpha} f(a)$, computed in $[0, \infty]$.

articles.title: Extended expectation
articles.statement:
For a probability mass function $p$ on a type $\alpha$ and a function
$f : \alpha \to [0, \infty]$, the extended expectation of $f$ under $p$ is the unordered sum
$\sum_{a \in \alpha} p(a) f(a)$ in $[0, \infty]$, which always exists.

Unlike the real-valued expectation, it needs no measurability or integrability hypothesis and
takes the value $\infty$ when the expected value diverges, rather than collapsing to $0$.

articles.title: Expectation of a finitely supported distribution
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function
on a measurable space $\alpha$ in which singletons are measurable, and let $s$ be a finite subset
of $\alpha$ such that $p(a) = 0$ for every $a \notin s$. Then for every function
$f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, the expectation of $f$ under $p$ equals $\sum_{a \in s} p(a) f(a)$.

No integrability hypothesis on $f$ and no finiteness assumption on $\alpha$ is needed.

articles.title: Expectation on a finite type
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a finite measurable
space $\alpha$ in which singletons are measurable, and let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$. Then the
expectation of $f$ under $p$ equals the finite sum $\sum_{a \in \alpha} p(a) f(a)$.

articles.title: Expectation as a series
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a measurable space
$\alpha$ in which singletons are measurable, and let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ be integrable with
respect to the probability measure associated to $p$. Then the expectation of $f$ under $p$ equals
the unordered sum $\sum_{a \in \alpha} p(a) f(a)$.

articles.title: Expectation of an indicator
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a finite measurable
space $\alpha$ in which singletons are measurable, and let $q$ be a property of elements of
$\alpha$. The expectation under $p$ of the function equal to $1$ where $q$ holds and $0$ elsewhere
is $\sum_{a \in \alpha,\ q(a)} p(a)$, the total mass of the elements satisfying $q$.

articles.title: Monotonicity of expectation
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a finite measurable
space $\alpha$ in which singletons are measurable, and let $f, g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy
$f(a) \le g(a)$ for every $a \in \alpha$. Then the expectation of $f$ under $p$ is at most the
expectation of $g$ under $p$.

articles.title: Change of variables for expectation
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a finite
measurable space $\alpha$ in which singletons are measurable, let $\beta$ be a measurable space in
which singletons are measurable, and let $g : \alpha \to \beta$ and $f : \beta \to \mathbb{R}$.
Write $g_* p$ for the pushforward of $p$ along $g$, which gives each $b \in \beta$ the mass
$\sum_{a :\, g(a) = b} p(a)$. Then the expectation of $f$ under $g_* p$ equals the expectation of
$f \circ g$ under $p$.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of expectation
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a finite measurable
space $\alpha$ in which singletons are measurable, and let $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy
$f(a) \ge 0$ for every $a \in \alpha$. Then the expectation of $f$ under $p$ is nonnegative.

articles.title: Expectation of a scalar multiple
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a finite
measurable space $\alpha$ in which singletons are measurable, let $c \in \mathbb{R}$ and let
$f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$. The expectation under $p$ of the scalar multiple $c f$ (the function
$a \mapsto c \cdot f(a)$) equals $c$ times the expectation of $f$ under $p$.

articles.title: Expectation of a finite sum
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a probability mass function on a finite type
$\alpha$ carrying a σ-algebra in which singletons are measurable, and write $\mathbb{E}_p[g]$ for
the expectation of $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ under $p$. For every finite subset $s$ of an index
type $\iota$ and every family of functions $f_i : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, $i \in \iota$, we have
$\mathbb{E}_p[a \mapsto \sum_{i \in s} f_i(a)] = \sum_{i \in s} \mathbb{E}_p[f_i]$.

articles.title: Expectation under the uniform distribution
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite type carrying
a σ-algebra in which singletons are measurable. For every function $f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$,
the expectation of $f$ under the uniform distribution on $\alpha$ equals the average
$\frac{1}{|\alpha|} \sum_{a \in \alpha} f(a)$.

articles.title: Expectation under a probability mass function
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a type carrying a σ-algebra
in which singletons are measurable, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\alpha$ and let
$f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$. The expectation of $f$ under $p$ is the Bochner integral
$\int f \, d\mu_p$, where $\mu_p$ is the probability measure on $\alpha$ associated to $p$.

On a finite type it equals the finite sum $\sum_{a \in \alpha} p(a) f(a)$, with each mass $p(a)$
read as a real number. As a Bochner integral it is $0$ when $f$ is not integrable; nonnegative
or natural-valued observables should use the extended nonnegative expectation, whose value in
$[0, \infty]$ can be $\infty$.

articles.title: Point masses of the hypergeometric distribution
articles.statement: The mass of `k` under `hypergeometric N K n` is `hypergeometricReal N K n k`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the hypergeometric mass function
articles.statement: The hypergeometric mass function is nonnegative.

articles.title: Hypergeometric mass vanishes above the number of marked items
articles.statement: The hypergeometric mass function vanishes above the number of marked items.

articles.title: Hypergeometric mass vanishes above the number of draws
articles.statement: The hypergeometric mass function vanishes above the number of draws.

articles.title: Hypergeometric mass function
articles.statement:
The hypergeometric mass function: the probability `C(K, k) C(N - K, n - k) / C(N, n)` of
drawing exactly `k` marked items in `n` draws without replacement from `N` items of which `K`
are marked; it is `0` for `k > n`. The parameter domain is `K ≤ N`, `n ≤ N`; outside it the
value is not a probability (`N - K` truncates, and `C(N, n) = 0` makes it `0` for `n > N`).

articles.title: Hypergeometric distribution
articles.statement:
The hypergeometric law on `ℕ` with population size `N`, `K ≤ N` marked items, and
`n ≤ N` draws without replacement.

articles.title: Normalization
articles.statement:
For `K ≤ N` and `n ≤ N` the hypergeometric probabilities sum to one;
this is Vandermonde's identity `∑ₖ C(K, k) C(N - K, n - k) = C(N, n)`.

articles.title: Mean
articles.statement: For `0 < N`, `K ≤ N` and `n ≤ N` the hypergeometric law has mean `n K / N`.

articles.title: Poisson conditioning, two cells
articles.statement:
For independent `X ~ Po(a)` and `Y ~ Po(b)` with
`a + b > 0`, the law of `X` given `X + Y = N` is binomial `Bin(N, a / (a + b))`.

articles.title: Poisson conditioning
articles.statement:
Let `Xᵢ ~ Po(λᵢ)`, `i ∈ ι`, be independent Poisson counts with
`∑ᵢ λᵢ > 0`. Given their total `∑ᵢ Xᵢ = N`, the count vector is multinomial with
`N` throws and cell probabilities `λᵢ / ∑ⱼ λⱼ`:
`P(X = x | ∑ᵢ Xᵢ = N) = multinomialReal N (λ / ∑ λ) x`.

articles.title: Mass of the multinomial distribution at a count vector
articles.statement: The mass of the multinomial PMF at `x` is `multinomialReal N p x`.

articles.title: Multinomial mass formula on the simplex
articles.statement: On the simplex the multinomial mass is `N! / ∏ᵢ xᵢ! · ∏ᵢ pᵢ ^ xᵢ`.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the multinomial mass function
articles.statement: The multinomial mass function is nonnegative for a nonnegative vector `p`.

articles.title: Support of the multinomial mass lies in the antidiagonal
articles.statement:
The multinomial mass function vanishes outside the finite set `piAntidiag univ N` of
count vectors with total `N`: the support is contained in the antidiagonal. Equality of
the support with the antidiagonal needs all `p i > 0` (e.g. for `p = (1, 0)`, `N = 1` the
vector `(0, 1)` is in the antidiagonal but has mass `0`).

articles.title: Multinomial mass vanishes off the simplex
articles.statement: The multinomial mass function vanishes off the simplex `∑ᵢ xᵢ = N`.

articles.title: Multinomial mass function
articles.statement:
The multinomial mass function: the probability `N! / ∏ᵢ xᵢ! · ∏ᵢ pᵢ ^ xᵢ` that `N`
independent throws, landing in cell `i` with probability `pᵢ`, produce the cell counts `x`; it is
`0` unless `∑ᵢ xᵢ = N`. The formula is a polynomial in `p` and is defined for every real vector
`p`; it is a probability mass function when `p` is a probability vector
(`0 ≤ pᵢ`, `∑ᵢ pᵢ = 1`), which the normalization theorems assume. The converse does not hold
in general: for `N = 0` it is the point mass at the zero vector for every `p`, even vectors
that are not probability vectors.

articles.title: Multinomial distribution as a probability mass function
articles.statement:
The multinomial law of `N` throws with cell probabilities `p` (a probability vector), as a
probability mass function on count vectors `ι → ℕ`.

articles.title: Covariance
articles.statement:
For a probability vector (`0 ≤ pᵢ`, `∑ₗ pₗ = 1`),
`Cov(Xᵢ, Xⱼ) = ∑ₓ (xᵢ - N pᵢ) (xⱼ - N pⱼ) P(x) = N (δᵢⱼ pᵢ - pᵢ pⱼ)`; in particular
`Var Xᵢ = N pᵢ (1 - pᵢ)` and `Cov(Xᵢ, Xⱼ) = -N pᵢ pⱼ` for `i ≠ j`.

articles.title: Second factorial moment, polynomial form
articles.statement:
For `i ≠ j`,
`∑ₓ xᵢ xⱼ P(x) = N (N - 1) pᵢ pⱼ (∑ₗ pₗ) ^ (N - 2)` for every real vector `p`.

articles.title: Mixed second moment
articles.statement: For a probability vector and `i ≠ j`, `E[Xᵢ Xⱼ] = N (N - 1) pᵢ pⱼ`.

articles.title: Mean, polynomial form
articles.statement: `∑ₓ xᵢ P(x) = N pᵢ (∑ⱼ pⱼ) ^ (N - 1)` for every real vector `p`.

articles.title: Mean
articles.statement:
For a probability vector (`0 ≤ pᵢ`, `∑ⱼ pⱼ = 1`), `E Xᵢ = N pᵢ`. The
underlying `sum_mul_multinomialReal_eq` is a polynomial identity holding for every real `p`.

articles.title: Second factorial moment, polynomial form
articles.statement: `∑ₓ xᵢ (xᵢ - 1) P(x) = N (N - 1) pᵢ² (∑ₗ pₗ) ^ (N - 2)` for every real vector `p`.

articles.title: Second factorial moment
articles.statement: For a probability vector, `E[Xᵢ (Xᵢ - 1)] = N (N - 1) pᵢ²`.

articles.title: Multinomial theorem
articles.statement: `∑ₓ P(x) = (∑ᵢ pᵢ) ^ N` for every real vector `p`.

articles.title: Normalization
articles.statement: For `∑ᵢ pᵢ = 1` the multinomial masses sum to one.

articles.title: Chu–Vandermonde identity for rising factorials
articles.statement: `(α + β)^{(n)} = ∑_{k ≤ n} C(n, k) α^{(k)} β^{(n - k)}`, for all real `α, β`.

articles.title: Beta-binomial mass function
articles.statement:
Beta-binomial mass `C(n, k) α^{(k)} β^{(n - k)} / (α + β)^{(n)}` (zero for `k > n`, since
`C(n, k) = 0`). A probability mass function for `α, β > 0`.

articles.title: Bursty expression stationary law
articles.statement:
**Bursty expression stationary law** (Shahrezaei–Swain). For burst rate `κ > 0`, decay rate
`γ > 0` and mean burst size `b ≥ 0`, the negative binomial law with size `a = κ / γ` (bursts per
lifetime) and mean `a b` satisfies global balance for the bursty production–degradation
chain.

articles.title: Net probability flow of the bursty production–degradation chain
articles.statement:
The net probability flow into state `n` of the bursty production–degradation chain:
bursts arrive at rate `κ` and add `B` molecules, `B` geometric with mean `b`,
`P(B = j) = b ^ j / (1 + b) ^ (j + 1)` for `j ≥ 0`; each molecule decays at rate `γ`. A burst
of size `0` changes nothing, so state `n` is left by a burst at rate `κ P(B ≥ 1) = κ b / (1 + b)`.
The flow is `κ ∑_{m < n} p(m) P(B = n - m) + γ (n + 1) p(n + 1) - (κ b / (1 + b) + γ n) p(n)`.

articles.title: Squared coefficient of variation
articles.statement:
**Squared coefficient of variation** (Brennecke et al. 2013; Svensson 2020). For a
probability measure `ν` on `[0, ∞)` with square-integrable rate and `E Λ > 0`,
`CV²(N) = Var N / (E N)² = 1 / E Λ + Var Λ / (E Λ)² = 1 / E Λ + CV²(Λ)`.

articles.title: Zero inflation by mixing
articles.statement:
**Zero inflation by mixing** (Jensen's inequality for `λ ↦ e^{-λ}`). For a probability
measure `ν` with integrable rate, `P(N = 0) = E e^{-Λ} ≥ e^{-E Λ}`, the zero class of the Poisson
law with the same mean.

articles.title: Zero class versus the Poisson law
articles.statement:
For `θ > 0` and `μ ≥ 0`,
`P(0) = (θ / (θ + μ)) ^ θ ≥ e^{-μ}`: a negative binomial law puts at least as much mass at zero
as the Poisson law with the same mean.

articles.title: Fano factor of bursty expression
articles.statement:
For `a > 0` and `b > 0`, the negative binomial law with
size `a` and mean `a b` has `Var N / E N = 1 + b`.

articles.title: Fano factor of the Poisson law
articles.statement:
For mean `m > 0`, `Var N / E N = 1`; in particular the
stationary law of the immigration–death chain has Fano factor `1`.

articles.title: Gamma–Poisson conjugacy, posterior
articles.statement:
With prior `Λ ~ Gamma(a, b)` (`a, b > 0`) and one
observation `N = k` from `Po(Λ)`, the posterior density (likelihood times prior over the
marginal `NB(k; a, a / b)`) is the `Gamma(a + k, b + 1)` density.

articles.title: Mean
articles.statement: For `θ > 0` and `μ ≥ 0` the negative binomial law has mean `μ`.

articles.title: Mean
articles.statement:
For a mixing measure `ν` on `[0, ∞)` with integrable rate, `E N = E Λ`
(finiteness of `ν` is not needed for this identity).

articles.title: Second factorial moment
articles.statement:
For a mixing measure `ν` on `[0, ∞)` with square-integrable
rate, `E[N (N - 1)] = E Λ²` (finiteness of `ν` is not needed for this identity).

articles.title: Negative binomial masses sum to one
articles.statement:
The negative binomial masses sum to one for `r > 0` and `p ∈ (0, 1]` (the binomial series
`∑ₖ r^{(k)} xᵏ / k! = (1 - x)^{-r}` at `x = 1 - p`).

articles.title: Normalization
articles.statement:
