articles.statement: The event `{o ↔ x inside S}`: `o` and `x` lie in `S` and are joined by an open path in `S`.

articles.title: Translation invariance of the Bernoulli product measure
articles.statement: The Bernoulli product measure on `{0, 1}^E` is invariant under the shift action of `G`.

articles.title: Open boundary edge of a cluster
articles.statement: The edge `{x, y}` is open, with `x ∈ C` and `y ∉ C`.

articles.title: Box edges with no endpoint in a cluster
articles.statement: The edges of `Λ_n` with no endpoint in `C`.

articles.title: Event that the cluster of the origin inside a set equals a given set
articles.statement: The event `{C_S(o) = K}` that the open cluster of `o` inside `S` is exactly `K`.

articles.title: Open cluster of a site inside a set
articles.statement:
The open cluster `C_S(o)` of `o` inside `S`: sites of `S` joined to `o` by an open path in
`S`.

articles.title: Exponential decay below `p̃_c`
articles.statement:
**Exponential decay below `p̃_c`** (Duminil-Copin–Tassion 2016): if
`φ_p(S) < 1` for some finite `S ∋ 0`, then `ℙ_p(0 ↔ ℤ^d \ Λ_{n-1}) ≤ C e^{-cn}` for some
`c, C > 0`.

articles.title: One-arm probability
articles.statement: The one-arm probability `ℙ_p(0 ↔ ℤ^d \ Λ_{n-1})`.

articles.title: One-arm event from a shifted origin
articles.statement: The event that `y` is joined by an open path to a site outside `Λ_{n-1}`.

articles.title: One-arm event from the origin
articles.statement:
The event `{0 ↔ ℤ^d \ Λ_{n-1}}` that the origin is joined by an open path to a site outside
`Λ_{n-1}`.

articles.title: Exploration independence of a cluster inside a set
articles.statement:
Exploration independence: for `K ⊆ S` finite and an event `B` depending only on edges in `U`,
disjoint from the edges between `K` and `S`, `ℙ_p(C_S(o) = K, B) = ℙ_p(C_S(o) = K) ℙ_p(B)`.

articles.title: Edges joining a finite set to a region
articles.statement: The finite set of edges `{x, y}` with `x ∈ K` and `y ∈ S`.

articles.title: Edges from a subset into a set
articles.statement: The set of edges `{x, y}` with `x ∈ K` and `y ∈ S`.

articles.title: Crossing inside the box that avoids a cluster
articles.statement: `y ∈ Λ_n \ C` is joined by an open path inside `Λ_n \ C` to a site outside `Λ_{n-1}`.

articles.title: Crossing to the box exterior that avoids a cluster
articles.statement: `y ∉ C` is joined by an open path avoiding `C` to a site outside `Λ_{n-1}`.

articles.title: Exponential decay from a one-step recursion
articles.statement:
If `φ_p(S) < 1` and `crossProb((k + 1)L) ≤ φ_p(S) · crossProb(kL)` for all `k`, then
`crossProb d p n ≤ C e^{-cn}` for some `c, C > 0`.

articles.title: Bernoulli weight of a single edge
articles.statement: The Bernoulli(`p`) weight of a single edge state: `p` for open, `1 - p` for closed.

articles.title: Product weight of an edge configuration
articles.statement: The product weight `∏_e w1(ω_e)` of a configuration on a finite edge set.

articles.title: Expectation under Bernoulli product weights
articles.statement:
The expectation `∑_ω f(ω) W(ω)` of `f` under the Bernoulli(`p`) product weights on a finite
edge set.

articles.title: Mean-field lower bound for $\theta(p)$ from a differential inequality
articles.statement:
The mean-field lower bound `θ(p) ≥ (p - p₀)/(p(1 - p₀))` from the differential inequality for
crossing probabilities. Reference: H. Duminil-Copin, V. Tassion, "A new proof of the sharpness of
the phase transition for Bernoulli percolation and the Ising model", Comm. Math. Phys. 343 (2016)
725–745.

articles.title: $p_c \le \tilde p_c$ if $\theta > 0$ above $\tilde p_c$
articles.statement:
`p_c ≤ p̃_c` when `θ` is positive above `p̃_c`. See also `Percolation.pc_le_tildePc`
(MathlibExt), stated with hypotheses on `θ(1)` and on `(p̃_c, 1)`.

articles.title: $\tilde p_c \le p_c$ if $\theta = 0$ on the set defining $\tilde p_c$
articles.statement:
`p̃_c ≤ p_c` when `θ` vanishes on the set defining `p̃_c`. See also `Percolation.tildePc_le_pc`
(MathlibExt), stated with exponential decay of crossing probabilities.

articles.title: Russo's formula
articles.statement:
**Russo's formula** in pivotal-factor form: for increasing `A` and `0 < p < 1`,
`d/dp ℙ_p(A) = (p(1 - p))⁻¹ ∑_e 𝔼_p[1_A (ω_e - p)]`.

articles.title: Probability of an event under Bernoulli product measure
articles.statement:
The probability `ℙ_p(A)` of `A` under the Bernoulli(`p`) product measure on `{0, 1}^E` for
`p ∈ [0, 1]`; outside `[0, 1]` it is the polynomial `StatMech.prob p A`, so that the function is
defined on all of `ℝ`.

articles.title: Real-valued indicator that an edge is open
articles.statement: The indicator `ω_e ∈ {0, 1}` (as a real number) that the edge `e` is open in `ω`.

articles.title: Russo's formula for the Bernoulli product measure
articles.statement:
Russo's formula for `p : ℝ≥0`, packaged with the identification of `measureProb A p` with
`(bernoulliProductMeasure p hp).real A`.

articles.title: Russo's formula
articles.statement:
**Russo's formula** (Margulis–Russo): for an increasing event `A` on a finite edge set and
`0 < p < 1`, `p ↦ ℙ_p(A)` has derivative `∑_e ℙ_p(e is pivotal for A)` at `p`.
See also `StatMech.hasDerivAt_prob_eq_sum_pivotalProb` (the polynomial form, for all `p`) and
`StatMech.hasDerivAt_realProb_cylinder_pivotal` (cylinder events on an infinite edge set).

articles.title: Russo's formula
articles.statement:
**Russo's formula**, `deriv` form: `d/dp ℙ_p(A) = ∑_e ℙ_p(e is pivotal for A)` for an
increasing event `A` and `0 < p < 1`.

articles.title: One-arm probability as a function of a real density
articles.statement:
The one-arm probability `crossProb d t n` as a function of a real density `t` (`0` outside
`[0, 1]`).

articles.title: Sharpness of the phase transition, conditional form
articles.statement:
Sharpness of the phase transition, **conditional form**: from `p̃_c > 0`, `θ(1) ≠ 0`,
exponential decay of the one-arm probability on `tildePcSet`, and the Duminil-Copin–Tassion
differential inequality on `(p̃_c, q)` (with continuity and derivative hypotheses), conclude
`p̃_c = p_c`, exponential decay on `tildePcSet`, and `θ(q) ≥ (q - p̃_c)/(q(1 - p̃_c))` for
`p̃_c < q < 1`. The hypotheses are discharged in `sharp_phase_transition`.

articles.title: Equality of the Duminil-Copin–Tassion threshold and $p_c$
articles.statement:
`p̃_c = p_c`, assuming exponential decay on `tildePcSet`, `θ(1) ≠ 0`, and `θ(q) > 0` for
`p̃_c < q < 1`.

articles.title: Exponential decay of the one-arm probability below the threshold
articles.statement:
Exponential decay of the one-arm probability for every `p ∈ tildePcSet d`, i.e. every `p`
admitting a finite `S ∋ 0` with `φ_p(S) < 1`.

articles.title: Straight path along the first coordinate axis
articles.statement: The direction sequence of the straight path from the origin along the first coordinate axis.

articles.title: Sharpness of the phase transition
articles.statement:
**Sharpness of the phase transition** for Bernoulli bond percolation on `ℤ^d`, `d ≥ 1`
(Duminil-Copin–Tassion 2016; Aizenman–Barsky 1987; Menshikov 1986):

1. `p̃_c = p_c`;
2. for every `p ∈ tildePcSet d` (a finite `S ∋ 0` has `φ_p(S) < 1`),
   `ℙ_p(0 ↔ ℤ^d \ Λ_{n-1}) ≤ C e^{-cn}` for some `c, C > 0`;
3. `θ(q) ≥ (q - p̃_c)/(q(1 - p̃_c))` for `p̃_c < q < 1`.

Scope of the items:
* Item 2 is stated on `tildePcSet d`, not on `[0, p_c)`: passing from `p < p̃_c` to
  `p ∈ tildePcSet d` needs monotonicity of `p ↦ φ_p(S)`, and passing from `p < p_c` to `θ(p) = 0`
  needs monotonicity of `θ`; neither is proved in MathlibExt (θ monotonicity is
  `theta_mono_parameter` in PhyslibExt `RandomCluster/PcUpperViaFK`).
* Item 3 is informative only when `p̃_c < 1`. This file does not prove that for any `d`; at `d = 1`
  it fails (`p̃_c = p_c = 1`) and item 3 is vacuous. For `d = 2`, `p_c < 1` is proved in PhyslibExt
  (`StatMech.Percolation.pc_two_lt_one_via_fk`), which with item 1 makes item 3 non-vacuous
  there.

articles.title: Positivity of the Duminil-Copin–Tassion threshold
Oriented edge boundary of a finite lattice set
articles.statement:
The oriented edge boundary `∂S = {(x, x ± e_i) : x ∈ S, x ± e_i ∉ S}` of a finite set
`S ⊆ ℤ^d`, as ordered pairs (inner endpoint first).

articles.title: Size bound for the edge boundary
articles.statement: The edge boundary of `S` has at most `2d |S|` elements.

articles.title: Probability of connection inside a set
articles.statement:
The probability `ℙ_p(0 ↔ x inside S)` that the origin and `x` are joined by an open path
using only vertices of `S`; it is `0` if `0 ∉ S` or `x ∉ S`.

articles.title: Shift of a lattice site in one coordinate
articles.statement: The site `x + δ e_i` obtained by moving `x` by `δ` in coordinate `i`.

articles.title: Duminil-Copin–Tassion quantity
articles.statement: The Duminil-Copin–Tassion quantity `φ_p(S) = p ∑_{(x, y) ∈ ∂S} ℙ_p(0 ↔ x inside S)`.

articles.title: Sign of a unit lattice step
articles.statement: The unit step `+1` (for `true`) or `-1` (for `false`).

articles.title: Densities with a finite set of small Duminil-Copin–Tassion quantity
articles.statement: The set of densities `p ∈ [0, 1]` for which some finite `S ∋ 0` has `φ_p(S) < 1`.

articles.title: Duminil-Copin–Tassion threshold
articles.statement: The Duminil-Copin–Tassion threshold `p̃_c(d) = sup {p : ∃ S ∋ 0 finite, φ_p(S) < 1}`.

articles.title: Counting measure of a set as a sum of indicators
articles.statement: `(∑ δ_{x_i})(s) = #{i | x_i ∈ s}`, as a sum of indicators.

articles.title: Image of a counting measure under a map
articles.statement: The image of `∑ δ_{x_i}` under `T` is `∑ δ_{T(x_i)}`.

articles.title: Counting measure of a finite tuple of points
articles.statement: The counting measure `∑_{i < n} δ_{x_i}` of a finite tuple of points.

articles.title: Laplace functional
articles.statement:
For measurable `f : E → [0, ∞)`,
`E exp(-∫ f dη) = exp(-∫ (1 - e^{-f}) dμ)` (Last–Penrose Thm. 3.9). The integral `∫ f dη` is a
finite sum `∑ f(x_i)` for every configuration charged by the process.

articles.title: Integral against a counting measure
Mecke equation
articles.statement:
For measurable `h : E × Measure E → [0, ∞]`,
`E ∫ h(x, η) η(dx) = ∫ E h(x, η + δ_x) μ(dx)` (Mecke 1967; Last–Penrose Thm. 4.1).

articles.title: Campbell's formula
articles.statement:
`E ∫ f dη = ∫ f dμ` for measurable `f : E → [0, ∞]`
(Last–Penrose Prop. 2.7).

articles.title: Integral of a coordinate function under a product measure
Point counts of a Poisson point process are Poisson
articles.statement: The number of points `η(B)` in a measurable set `B` has the Poisson law of mean `μ(B)`.

articles.title: Mixed binomial process is a Poisson process
articles.statement:
The counts `η(A i)` of pairwise disjoint measurable sets are independent, and `η(A i)`
has the Poisson law of mean `μ(A i)`: the mixed binomial process is a Poisson process with
intensity `μ` in the sense of Last–Penrose Def. 3.1 (Last–Penrose Prop. 3.5).

articles.title: Mapping theorem
articles.statement:
The image `η ∘ T⁻¹` of a Poisson point process under a measurable map
`T : E → F` is the Poisson point process with intensity `μ ∘ T⁻¹` (Last–Penrose Thm. 5.1).

articles.title: Restriction theorem
articles.statement:
The restrictions `η|_{A i}` of a Poisson point process with finite
intensity `μ` to pairwise disjoint measurable sets `A i` are independent Poisson point processes
with intensities `μ|_{A i}` (Last–Penrose Thm. 5.2).

articles.title: Measurability of the counting measure in the points
articles.statement: The counting measure of a tuple depends measurably on the tuple.

articles.title: Poisson point process with finite intensity
articles.statement:
The law of the Poisson point process with finite intensity `μ` on `E`:
`∑_n e^{-μ(E)} / n! • (μ^{⊗n}).map countingMeasure`, a probability measure on `Measure E`
(Last–Penrose Prop. 3.5, mixed binomial construction).

articles.title: Poisson weights sum to one
articles.statement: The Poisson weights sum to one: `∑_n e^{-μ(E)} μ(E)^n / n! = 1`.

articles.title: Superposition
articles.statement:
**Superposition** (Kingman 1993, §2.2): the sum of two independent Poisson processes of rates
`r₁` and `r₂` is a Poisson process of rate `r₁ + r₂`. Independence is of the two processes as
random paths.

articles.title: Counting process has nondecreasing paths almost surely
articles.statement:
The counting process of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals has nondecreasing paths
almost surely (the arrival times tend to infinity almost surely, so every arrival set in
`[0, t]` is finite).

articles.title: Counting process starts at zero almost surely
articles.statement:
The counting process of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals starts at `0` almost
surely (all interarrival times are positive almost surely).

articles.title: Arrival times from interarrival times
articles.statement: The `n`-th arrival time `S n = T 0 + ⋯ + T (n - 1)` of the interarrival times `T`.

articles.title: Counting process of interarrival times
articles.statement:
The counting process of the interarrival times `T`: `count T t ω` is the number of arrivals
`n ≥ 1` with `S n ≤ t`. When that set is infinite (a null event for exponential interarrivals of
positive rate) `Set.ncard` returns `0`.

articles.title: Arrival times of exponential interarrivals are Erlang
articles.statement:
The `(n + 1)`-th arrival time of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals has the Gamma
(Erlang) law with shape `n + 1` and rate `r` (Karlin–Taylor 1975, §4.2).

articles.title: Independent Poisson increments of the counting process
articles.statement:
The increments of the counting process of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals over
consecutive intervals `(t i, t (i + 1)]` are independent with the Poisson laws of means
`r (t (i + 1) - t i)`: the increment vector has the product law (Kingman 1993, ch. 4;
Karlin–Taylor 1975, ch. 4).

articles.title: Arrival counts of exponential interarrivals are Poisson
articles.statement:
The number of arrivals in `[0, t]` of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrivals has the
Poisson law of mean `r t` (Karlin–Taylor 1975, §4.2, Theorem 2.1).

articles.title: Exponential interarrivals give a Poisson process
articles.statement:
**Exponential interarrivals give a Poisson process** (Kingman 1993, ch. 4; Karlin–Taylor
1975, ch. 4): the counting process of i.i.d. rate-`r` exponential interarrival times is a Poisson
process of rate `r`.

articles.title: Poisson process
articles.statement:
`N : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℕ` is a **Poisson process of rate `r`** under `P` (Kingman 1993, ch. 4;
Karlin–Taylor 1975, ch. 4): `N 0 = 0` and the paths are nondecreasing almost surely, the
increments over consecutive intervals are independent, and for `s ≤ t` the increment `N t - N s`
has the Poisson law of mean `r (t - s)`.

articles.title: Thinning
articles.statement:
**Thinning** (Kingman 1993, §5.1; Karlin–Taylor 1975, §4.1): keeping each point of a Poisson
process of rate `r` independently with probability `p`, independently of the process, gives a
Poisson process of rate `p r`. The marks `B i` are i.i.d. with `P(B i) = p` and independent of
`N` as a random path.

articles.title: Thinning of a Poisson process
articles.statement:
The thinning of `N` by the marks `B`: the number of indices `i < N t` with `B i`, i.e. the
number of points of `N` in `[0, t]` that are kept when the `i`-th point (in time order, from
`0`) is kept iff `B i`.

articles.title: Stationary random functions (Slutsky–Khinchin)
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable
space $\Omega$, and let $v$ assign to each real $t$ a function $v_t : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$.
Then $v$ is stationary if there are a real number $c$ and a function $R : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$
such that for all real $t$ and $h$, $\int v_t \, d\mu = 0$, $\int v_t^2 \, d\mu = c$ and
$\int v_t \, v_{t+h} \, d\mu = R(h)$.

The integrals are Bochner integrals, which are $0$ for non-integrable functions, so integrability
of $v_t$, $v_t^2$ and $v_t v_{t+h}$ is not required.

articles.title: Scottish Book Problem 180 fails
articles.statement:
The claim of Scottish Book Problem 180 is false: there are a
probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ carrying a measurable random variable uniformly distributed on
$[0, 1]$ and a stationary random function $v$ on $\Omega$ with every $v_t$ measurable, such that
no measurable random variable $A : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ uniformly distributed on $[0, 1]$ and no
map $\varphi : \mathbb{R} \to \Omega$ satisfy both $A(\varphi(\alpha)) = \alpha$ for every
$\alpha \in [0, 1]$ and, for all real $t_1 \ne t_2$, the independence of
$\alpha \mapsto v_{t_1}(\varphi(\alpha))$ and $\alpha \mapsto v_{t_2}(\varphi(\alpha))$ with
respect to Lebesgue measure on $[0, 1]$.

A counterexample is $\Omega = \mathbb{R}$ with $\mu$ Lebesgue measure restricted to $[0, 1]$, the
identity as uniform variable, and $v_t(\omega) = \omega - 1/2$ for every $t$, which is stationary
with $c = R(h) = 1/12$. If $A$ and $\varphi$ existed, $\varphi$ would be injective on $[0, 1]$,
while both functions in the independence condition equal $f(\alpha) = \varphi(\alpha) - 1/2$. A
function independent of itself is almost everywhere constant, and an injective function on
$[0, 1]$ is not. No non-degeneracy hypothesis is added, since the source asks for none.

## Sources

- J. Kampe de Feriet, Problem 180 of the Scottish Book, typescript PDF pp. 82-83, printed pp. 79-80; see the commentary in R. D. Mauldin (ed.), The Scottish Book, 2nd ed. (Birkhäuser, 2015).

articles.title: Scottish Book Problem 180 (Kampé de Fériet's claim)
articles.statement:
The claim that for every probability
space $(\Omega, \mu)$ that carries a measurable random variable $U : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$
uniformly distributed on $[0, 1]$, and every stationary random function $v$ on $\Omega$ (in the
sense of Slutsky and Khinchin) such that each $v_t : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ is measurable, there
exist a measurable random variable $A : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ uniformly distributed on $[0, 1]$
and a map $\varphi : \mathbb{R} \to \Omega$ such that $A(\varphi(\alpha)) = \alpha$ for every
$\alpha \in [0, 1]$, and such that for all real $t_1 \ne t_2$ the functions
$\alpha \mapsto v_{t_1}(\varphi(\alpha))$ and $\alpha \mapsto v_{t_2}(\varphi(\alpha))$ are
independent with respect to Lebesgue measure on $[0, 1]$.

Here a variable is uniformly distributed on $[0, 1]$ when its law is Lebesgue measure restricted
to $[0, 1]$. The equation $A(\varphi(\alpha)) = \alpha$ is condition (1) of the problem and the
independence, in the sense of Steinhaus, is condition (2). The existence of $U$ is an added
hypothesis; it rules out refutations that only exploit a space carrying no uniform variable.

articles.title: Mass of a configuration under a finite Bernoulli product measure
articles.statement: For finite `E`, the mass of a configuration is the product of its coordinate masses.

articles.title: Bernoulli distribution agrees with the library Bernoulli measure
articles.statement: `bernoulliMeasure p hp` is Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.bernoulliMeasure true false p`.

articles.title: Point masses of the Bernoulli distribution
articles.statement: The mass of a point under the Bernoulli distribution: `p` at `true`, `1 - p` at `false`.

articles.title: Bernoulli distribution on the Booleans
articles.statement:
The Bernoulli distribution on `Bool` with success probability `p`: mass `p` on `true` and
`1 - p` on `false`. This is Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.bernoulliMeasure true false p`, with the
parameter given as an `ℝ≥0` bounded by `1`.

articles.title: Bernoulli product measure of a cylinder event
articles.statement:
The infinite Bernoulli product measure of a cylinder over `F` is the finite Bernoulli product
measure of its base.

articles.title: Bernoulli product measure on bonds is the bond percolation law
articles.statement:
On bond configurations `Sym2 V → Bool`, `bernoulliProductMeasure` is the bond percolation law
`MathlibExt.Probability.ProductBondPercolation.gbernoulliLaw`.

articles.title: Bernoulli product measure on configuration space
articles.statement:
The Bernoulli product measure on `ConfigSpace E`: the coordinates are independent and each is
`true` with probability `p` (`Measure.infinitePi` of `bernoulliMeasure p hp`). See also Mathlib's
`ProbabilityTheory.setBernoulli`, the same product measure on `Set E`.

articles.title: Russo's formula
articles.statement: **Russo's formula**, `deriv` form of `hasDerivAt_realProb_cylinder_pivotal`.

articles.title: Differentiability in $p$ of the probability of a cylinder event
articles.statement:
The weight of the projection of an event onto finitely many coordinates is differentiable
in `p`.

articles.title: Events depending on finitely many coordinates are cylinders
articles.statement:
An event whose indicator depends only on the coordinates in `F` is the cylinder over its
projection onto `F`.

articles.title: Configuration patched from one configuration on a finite set and another off it
articles.statement: The configuration that agrees with `η` on the finite set `F` and with `ω` off `F`.

articles.title: Bernoulli product measure of an event on a finite index set
articles.statement: On a finite index set, the Bernoulli product measure of an event is its weight `prob p`.

articles.title: Russo's formula
articles.statement:
**Russo's formula** for an increasing event `A` projected onto finitely many coordinates `F`:
the derivative in `p` of its weight is the sum over `e ∈ F` of the weight of the event that `e`
is pivotal (L. Russo, 1981).

articles.title: Finite projections of increasing events are increasing
articles.statement: The projection of an increasing event onto finitely many coordinates is increasing.

articles.title: Probability of an event as a sum of configuration masses
articles.statement: For finite `E`, the probability of an event is the sum of the masses of its configurations.

articles.title: Probability of a finitely dependent event as a polynomial in $p$
articles.statement:
The probability of an event depending only on the coordinates in `F`, as an explicit
polynomial in `p`.

articles.title: Probability of a finitely dependent event as a finite weight
articles.statement:
The probability of an event depending only on the coordinates in `F` is the finite weight
`prob p` of its projection onto `F`.

articles.title: Bernoulli product measure of a cylinder event, real-valued form
articles.statement: Real-valued form of `bernoulliProductMeasure_cylinder`.

articles.title: Mass of a configuration on a finite index set is its product weight
articles.statement: On a finite index set, the mass of a configuration is its product weight `configWeight`.

articles.title: Log-modularity of Bernoulli product weights
articles.statement:
The configuration weights of a Bernoulli product measure are log-modular:
`w(a) w(b) = w(a ⊔ b) w(a ⊓ b)`. In particular they satisfy the FKG lattice condition.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of configuration masses
articles.statement: Configuration masses are nonnegative.

articles.title: Mass of a configuration under a finite Bernoulli product measure, real form
articles.statement: For finite `E`, the mass of a configuration is the product of its coordinate masses.

articles.title: Configuration masses sum to one
articles.statement: For finite `E`, the configuration masses sum to `1`.

articles.title: Complete graph on the boundary vertices
articles.statement: The complete graph on the boundary vertices, used to wire the boundary together.

articles.title: Boundary conditions for a bond model
articles.statement: Boundary conditions for a bond model on a finite graph.

articles.title: Open edge in a bond configuration
articles.statement: The edge `{x, y}` of `G` is open in the configuration `ω`.

articles.title: Number of open clusters with free boundary conditions
articles.statement:
The number of open clusters (connected components of the open graph) with free boundary
conditions.

articles.title: Number of open clusters with wired boundary conditions
articles.statement:
The number of open clusters with wired boundary conditions: all boundary vertices lie in a
single cluster.

articles.title: Number of open clusters under a boundary condition
articles.statement:
The number of open clusters under a boundary condition. The periodic case uses the free count:
the periodic identification is built into the graph `G`.

articles.title: Open subgraph of a bond configuration
articles.statement: The spanning subgraph of `G` consisting of the open edges of `ω`.

articles.title: Boundary wiring relation
articles.statement: Both vertices lie on the boundary.

articles.title: Wired open graph
articles.statement:
The wired open graph: the open edges of `ω` together with an edge between every two distinct
boundary vertices.

articles.title: Agreement classes of configurations have equal size
articles.statement:
Let $V$ and $\alpha$ be finite types
and $W \subseteq V$. For any two configurations $x, z : V \to \alpha$, the number of
configurations $y : V \to \alpha$ with $y(v) = z(v)$ for all $v \in W$ equals the number of
configurations $y$ with $y(v) = x(v)$ for all $v \in W$.

articles.title: Conditional independence in ratio form
articles.statement:
Let $V$ and $\alpha$ be finite types, let $p$ be a
real-valued weight on the configurations $x : V \to \alpha$, and for $U \subseteq V$ write
$p(x_U)$ for the marginal of $p$ on $U$ at $x$. If, for $A, B, S \subseteq V$, the variables in
$A$ and in $B$ are conditionally independent given those in $S$ under $p$, then every
configuration $x$ with $p(x_S) \ne 0$ satisfies

$$\frac{p(x_{A\cup B\cup S})}{p(x_S)} = \frac{p(x_{A\cup S})}{p(x_S)}\frac{p(x_{B\cup S})}{p(x_S)}$$

For a nonnegative weight of positive total mass these ratios are the conditional probabilities of
the normalized distribution, so this is $P(x_A, x_B \mid x_S) = P(x_A \mid x_S)\, P(x_B \mid x_S)$.

articles.title: Conditional independence can be read off a marginal
articles.statement:
Let $V$ and $\alpha$ be finite types,
let $p$ be a real-valued weight on the configurations $x : V \to \alpha$, let $W \subseteq V$, and
let $p_W$ be the $W$-marginal of $p$, the weight sending $x$ to the total weight of the
configurations that agree with $x$ on $W$. For all $A, B, S \subseteq W$, the variables in $A$
and in $B$ are conditionally independent given those in $S$ under $p_W$ if and only if they are
conditionally independent given those in $S$ under $p$.

articles.title: The factorization criterion for conditional independence
articles.statement:
Let $V$ and $\alpha$ be finite
types, let $f$ and $g$ be real-valued weights on the configurations $x : V \to \alpha$, and let
$P, Q \subseteq V$ with $P \cup Q = V$ such that $f(x)$ depends only on the values of $x$ on $P$
and $g(x)$ only on its values on $Q$. If $A \subseteq V$ is disjoint from $Q$ and $B \subseteq V$
is disjoint from $P$, then the variables in $A$ and in $B$ are conditionally independent given
those in $P \cap Q$ under the pointwise product $fg$.

articles.title: Conditional independence from the variables outside the conditioning set
articles.statement:
Let $V$ and
$\alpha$ be finite types, let $p$ be a real-valued weight on the configurations
$x : V \to \alpha$, and let $A, B, S \subseteq V$. If the variables in $A \setminus S$ and in
$B \setminus S$ are conditionally independent given those in $S$ under $p$, then the variables in
$A$ and in $B$ are conditionally independent given those in $S$ under $p$.

articles.title: Conditional independence for a finite weight
articles.statement:
Let $V$ and $\alpha$ be finite types, let $p$
be a real-valued weight on the configurations $x : V \to \alpha$, and for $U \subseteq V$ write
$p(x_U)$ for the marginal of $p$ on $U$ at $x$, the total weight of the configurations that agree
with $x$ on $U$. For $A, B, S \subseteq V$, the variables in $A$ and in $B$ are conditionally
independent given those in $S$ under $p$ when

$$p(x_{A \cup B \cup S})\, p(x_S) = p(x_{A \cup S})\, p(x_{B \cup S})$$

for every configuration $x$.

articles.title: Monotonicity of marginals in the fixed variables
articles.statement:
Let $V$ and $\alpha$ be finite types, let
$p$ be a real-valued weight on the configurations $x : V \to \alpha$ with $p(x) \ge 0$ for every
$x$, and let $U \subseteq U' \subseteq V$. Then for every configuration $x$, the marginal of $p$
on $U'$ at $x$ is at most the marginal of $p$ on $U$ at $x$.

articles.title: Marginalizing in two steps
articles.statement:
Let $V$ and $\alpha$ be finite types, let $p$ be a real-valued
weight on the configurations $x : V \to \alpha$, let $U \subseteq W \subseteq V$, and let $p_W$
be the $W$-marginal of $p$, the weight sending $x$ to the total weight of the configurations that
agree with $x$ on $W$. Then for every configuration $x$, the $U$-marginal of $p_W$ at $x$ equals
$N$ times the $U$-marginal of $p$ at $x$, where $N$ is the number of configurations that agree
with $x$ on $W$ (the number of assignments of values to the variables outside $W$).

articles.title: Marginals of a product
articles.statement:
Let $V$ and $\alpha$ be finite types, let $f$ and $g$ be real-valued
weights on the configurations $x : V \to \alpha$, and let $P, Q, U \subseteq V$ with
$P \cup Q = V$ and $P \cap Q \subseteq U$, such that $f(x)$ depends only on the values of $x$ on
$P$ and $g(x)$ only on its values on $Q$. Write $fg$ for the pointwise product, $P^c$ and $Q^c$
for the complements in $V$, and, for a weight $h$, a set $T \subseteq V$ and a configuration $x$,
$m_h(T, x)$ for the marginal of $h$ on $T$ at $x$, the total weight of the configurations that
agree with $x$ on $T$. Then for every configuration $x$,

$$m_{fg}(U, x) = m_f(U \cup P^c, x)\, m_g(U \cup Q^c, x).$$

Here the free variables of $f$ are those of $P$ outside $U$, and those of $g$ are those of $Q$
outside $U$.

articles.title: Marginal of a weight
articles.statement:
Let $V$ and $\alpha$ be finite types, a configuration being a map
$x : V \to \alpha$, and let $p$ be a real-valued weight on configurations. The (unnormalized)
marginal of $p$ on a set of variables $U \subseteq V$ at a configuration $x$ is

$$\sum_{y \,:\, y(v) = x(v) \text{ for all } v \in U} p(y),$$

the total weight of the configurations that agree with $x$ on $U$.

articles.title: Outside conditional distribution is a version of the conditional probability
articles.statement: `gibbsConditional μ Λ` is a version of the conditional probability `μ⟦s | outsideSigma Λ⟧`.

articles.title: Disintegration in product form for the outside conditional distribution
articles.statement: Disintegration in product form: `μ.trim ⊗ₘ gibbsConditional μ Λ` is the law of `(ω, ω)`.

articles.title: Averaging the outside conditional distribution recovers the measure
articles.statement: Disintegration: averaging the conditional distribution over `μ` gives back `μ`.

articles.title: Conditional distribution given the outside of a region
articles.statement:
The conditional distribution of a finite measure `μ` on `ConfigSpace E` given the
configuration outside `Λ`: a regular version of `μ(· | outsideSigma Λ)`, namely Mathlib's
`condExpKernel μ (outsideSigma Λ)`. For a Gibbs measure this is the Gibbs specification in `Λ`
(DLR condition).

articles.title: Outside σ-algebra is a sub-σ-algebra of the product σ-algebra
articles.statement: The outside σ-algebra is a sub-σ-algebra of the product σ-algebra.

articles.title: σ-algebra of the configuration outside a region
articles.statement:
The σ-algebra on `ConfigSpace E` generated by the coordinates outside `Λ`: the information
about a configuration that is visible from outside the region `Λ`.

articles.title: Configuration space of a statistical-mechanics model
articles.statement:
The configuration space `E → Bool` of a statistical-mechanics model with sites (or bonds)
indexed by `E`, carrying the product topology and the product σ-algebra.

articles.title: Coordinate projection of a configuration
articles.statement: The coordinate projection `ω ↦ ω e` of a configuration at the site `e`.

articles.title: Product σ-algebra on configuration space is generated by the coordinates
articles.statement:
The product σ-algebra on `ConfigSpace E` is generated by the coordinate projections; this
holds by definition of `MeasurableSpace.pi`.

articles.title: Bernoulli zero-one law for infinite groups acting finite-to-one
articles.statement: Invariant events of the Bernoulli product measure have probability `0` or `1`.

articles.title: Independence of coordinates under the Bernoulli product measure
articles.statement:
Coordinates are independent under the Bernoulli product measure. See also Mathlib's
`ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun_infinitePi`, of which this is a special case.

articles.title: Ergodicity of Bernoulli measures under free infinite-group actions
articles.statement:
The Bernoulli product measure is ergodic under every action of an infinite group with injective
orbit maps.

articles.title: Ergodic measure on configuration space
articles.statement:
A measure on `ConfigSpace E` is ergodic for the shift action of `G` if it is translation
invariant and every measurable set with `shift g ⁻¹' s = s` for all `g` has measure `0` or
`μ univ`. See also Mathlib's `ErgodicSMul`, which asks the same for a.e.-invariant sets.

articles.title: Translation-invariant measure on configuration space
articles.statement:
A measure on `ConfigSpace E` is translation invariant if every shift `shift g`, `g : G`,
preserves it.

articles.title: Configuration shift is the action on functions
articles.statement: `shift` is Mathlib's `arrowAction` of `G` on functions `E → Bool`.

articles.title: Shift of a configuration by a group element
articles.statement:
The shift of a configuration by `g : G`: `(shift g ω) e = ω (g⁻¹ • e)`. This is the action
`arrowAction` of Mathlib on functions out of `E`.

articles.title: Increasing-event probabilities along a decreasing chain are antitone
articles.statement: Along a chain `⋯ ≼ μ₁ ≼ μ₀`, the probability of an increasing event is antitone.

articles.title: Stochastic domination from below passes to weak limits
articles.statement:
If `ρ ≼ μₙ` for all `n` and `μₙ → ν` weakly, then `ρ(A) ≤ ν(A)` for every increasing clopen
event `A`.

articles.title: Probability measures agreeing on clopen sets are equal
articles.statement:
Two probability measures on `ConfigSpace E` that agree on clopen sets are equal: the clopen
cylinder events form a generating π-system.

articles.title: Weak limit of a decreasing chain is dominated by its terms
articles.statement:
The weak limit of a decreasing chain gives each increasing clopen event at most the
probability any term of the chain gives it.

articles.title: Subsequential weak limits are determined by clopen-event limits
articles.statement:
If the probabilities of clopen events converge to `L`, every subsequential weak limit `ξ`
satisfies `ξ(A) = L(A)` on clopen `A`.

articles.title: Cylinder events are clopen
articles.statement: A cylinder event of `ConfigSpace E`, determined by finitely many coordinates, is clopen.

articles.title: Weak limit of an increasing chain dominates its terms
articles.statement:
The weak limit of an increasing chain gives each increasing clopen event at least the
probability any term of the chain gives it.

articles.title: Lower bounds on clopen-event probabilities pass to weak limits
articles.statement:
A lower bound on the probabilities of a clopen event along a weakly convergent sequence passes
to the limit.

articles.title: Increasing-event probabilities along an increasing chain are monotone
articles.statement: Along a chain `μ₀ ≼ μ₁ ≼ ⋯`, the probability of an increasing event is monotone.

articles.title: Upper bounds on clopen-event probabilities pass to weak limits
articles.statement:
An upper bound on the probabilities of a clopen event along a weakly convergent sequence passes
to the limit.

articles.title: Weak convergence implies convergence of integrals
articles.statement: Under weak convergence, the integral of every bounded continuous function converges.

articles.title: Convergence of increasing-event probabilities along an increasing chain
articles.statement:
Along a chain `μ₀ ≼ μ₁ ≼ ⋯`, the probability of an increasing clopen event converges to its
supremum.

articles.title: Portmanteau theorem for clopen events
articles.statement:
Under weak convergence on `ConfigSpace E`, the probability of every clopen event converges
(portmanteau theorem).

articles.title: Convergence on clopen events implies weak convergence
articles.statement:
If the probability of every clopen event converges along a sequence of probability measures on
`ConfigSpace E`, the sequence converges weakly: all subsequential limits (which exist by
Prokhorov) agree on clopen sets, hence coincide.

articles.title: Convergence of integrals implies weak convergence
articles.statement:
If the integral of every bounded continuous function converges, the measures converge
weakly.

articles.title: Weak convergence of probability measures on configuration space
articles.statement:
Weak convergence of a sequence of probability measures on `ConfigSpace E`: convergence in the
topology of `ProbabilityMeasure (ConfigSpace E)`, whose open sets are generated by the integrals of
bounded continuous functions.

articles.title: Stochastic domination from above passes to weak limits
articles.statement:
If `μₙ ≼ ρ` for all `n` and `μₙ → ν` weakly, then `ν(A) ≤ ρ(A)` for every increasing clopen
event `A`.

articles.title: Bertrand's ballot theorem
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be natural numbers with $1 \le q < p$. Call a
sequence of $p + q$ votes, each for A or for B, favourable if it contains exactly $p$ votes for A
and, for every $k$ with $1 \le k \le p + q$, strictly more of its first $k$ votes are for A than
for B. Then the number of favourable sequences, multiplied by $p + q$, equals
$(p - q)\binom{p+q}{q}$.

Equivalently, when the $p + q$ votes are counted in uniformly random order, the probability that
A is strictly ahead of B throughout the count is $\frac{p-q}{p+q}$, since there are
$\binom{p+q}{q}$ sequences with exactly $p$ votes for A.

## Sources

- *Bertrand's ballot theorem*, Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertrand%27s_ballot_theorem.

articles.title: A zero walk converges to a finite limit
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random
variables on a probability space and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. If almost surely $S_n = 0$ for
every $n$, then almost surely there is $l \in \mathbb{R}$ with $S_n \to l$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Vanishing steps give a convergent random walk
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\Omega$ and
let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real-valued functions on $\Omega$, with partial sums
$S_n = \sum_{i\lt n} X_i$. If for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$ we have $X_i(\omega) = 0$ for all
$i$, then for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$ the sequence $S_n(\omega)$ converges to a finite real
limit.

articles.title: Random walk with a finite limit
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random variables on a
probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. The random walk $(S_n)$
converges to a finite limit if for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$ there is $l \in \mathbb{R}$ with
$S_n(\omega) \to l$ as $n \to \infty$.

The limit may depend on $\omega$; the zero-walk alternative of the i.i.d. random-walk dichotomy
implies this property.

articles.title: Coordinate process on sequence space
articles.statement:
For $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate is
the map $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}} \to \mathbb{R}$ sending a real sequence
$\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$ to its $i$-th term $\omega_i$.

articles.title: Random-walk dichotomy on sequence space
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a probability measure on
$\mathbb{R}$, let $\nu = \rho^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$ be the product measure on
$\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$, and let $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} \omega_i$ be the partial sums of
the coordinates. Then one of the following holds: $\nu$-almost surely $S_n = 0$ for every $n$;
$\nu$-almost surely $S_n \to +\infty$; $\nu$-almost surely $S_n \to -\infty$; or $\nu$-almost
surely $\limsup_n S_n = +\infty$ and $\liminf_n S_n = -\infty$.

articles.title: Random-walk dichotomy on sequence space, finite-limit form
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a probability
measure on $\mathbb{R}$, let $\nu = \rho^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$ be the product measure on
$\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$, and let $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} \omega_i$ be the partial sums of
the coordinates. Then one of the following holds: $\nu$-almost surely $S_n$ converges to a
finite limit (which may depend on $\omega$); $\nu$-almost surely $S_n \to +\infty$;
$\nu$-almost surely $S_n \to -\infty$; or $\nu$-almost surely $\limsup_n S_n = +\infty$ and
$\liminf_n S_n = -\infty$.

articles.title: Random walk drifting to $-\infty$
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random variables on a
probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. The random walk $(S_n)$ drifts
to $-\infty$ if for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$, $S_n(\omega) \to -\infty$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Random walk drifting to $+\infty$
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random variables on a
probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. The random walk $(S_n)$ drifts
to $+\infty$ if for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$, $S_n(\omega) \to +\infty$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Zero–one sublevel sets force an almost surely constant variable
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a
probability measure on $\Omega$ and let $F : \Omega \to [-\infty, +\infty]$ be measurable. If
for every real $a$ the set $\{\omega : F(\omega) \le a\}$ has $\mu$-measure $0$ or $1$, then
there is $c \in [-\infty, +\infty]$ with $F = c$ $\mu$-almost everywhere.

articles.title: Liminf commutes with adding a constant
articles.statement:
For every real $c$ and every real sequence
$(u_n)$, with limits inferior taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$,
$\liminf_{n \to \infty} (c + u_n) = c + \liminf_{n \to \infty} u_n$.

articles.title: Finite permutations do not change the liminf of the partial sums
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a
permutation of $\mathbb{N}$ that moves only finitely many points. For every real sequence
$\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$, the limit inferior in $[-\infty, +\infty]$ of the partial
sums $\sum_{i\lt n} \omega_{\sigma(i)}$ equals the limit inferior of the partial sums
$\sum_{i\lt n} \omega_i$.

articles.title: A real sequence tending to $+\infty$ has liminf $+\infty$
articles.statement:
If a real sequence $(S_n)$
tends to $+\infty$, then its limit inferior in the extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$ is
$+\infty$.

articles.title: One-step shift identity for the liminf of the partial sums
articles.statement:
For a real sequence
$\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$ write $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i\lt n} \omega_i$, and let
$\omega'$ be its shift, $\omega'_i = \omega_{i+1}$. Then, with limits inferior taken in
$[-\infty, +\infty]$, we have
$\liminf_{n \to \infty} S_n(\omega) = \omega_0 + \liminf_{n \to \infty} S_n(\omega')$.

articles.title: Dropping the first term does not change the liminf
articles.statement:
For every sequence $(u_n)$ in the
extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$,
$\liminf_{n \to \infty} u_{n+1} = \liminf_{n \to \infty} u_n$.

articles.title: Limsup commutes with adding a constant
articles.statement:
For every real $c$ and every real sequence
$(u_n)$, with limits superior taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$,
$\limsup_{n \to \infty} (c + u_n) = c + \limsup_{n \to \infty} u_n$.

articles.title: Finite permutations do not change the limsup of the partial sums
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a
permutation of $\mathbb{N}$ that moves only finitely many points. For every real sequence
$\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$, the limit superior in $[-\infty, +\infty]$ of the partial
sums $\sum_{i\lt n} \omega_{\sigma(i)}$ equals the limit superior of the partial sums
$\sum_{i\lt n} \omega_i$.

articles.title: A sequence tending to $-\infty$ has limsup $-\infty$
articles.statement:
Let $(S_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$
be a sequence of real numbers with $S_n \to -\infty$ as $n \to \infty$. Then the limit
superior of $(S_n)$, taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$, equals $-\infty$.

articles.title: One-step shift identity for the limsup of partial sums
articles.statement:
For a real sequence
$\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$ write $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} \omega_i$, and let
$\theta\omega = (\omega_1, \omega_2, \dots)$ be the one-step shift. Then for every $\omega$,
$\limsup_{n \to \infty} S_n(\omega) = \omega_0 + \limsup_{n \to \infty} S_n(\theta\omega)$,
where both limits superior are taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$.

articles.title: Dropping the first term preserves the limsup
articles.statement:
For every sequence
$(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of extended reals,
$\limsup_{n \to \infty} u_{n+1} = \limsup_{n \to \infty} u_n$.

articles.title: Shift invariance of the i.i.d. product measure
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a probability measure on
$\mathbb{R}$, and let $\rho^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$ be the product measure on the sequence space
$\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$. The image of $\rho^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$ under the one-step shift
$(\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots) \mapsto (\omega_1, \omega_2, \dots)$ is
$\rho^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$.

articles.title: Tail partial sums are measurable for the σ-algebra from their first index
articles.statement:
Let
$X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real-valued functions on a set $\Omega$, and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let
$\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ be the smallest σ-algebra on $\Omega$ for which every $X_i$ with
$i \ge n$ is Borel measurable. For all $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$, the function
$\omega \mapsto \sum_{n \le i < m} X_i(\omega)$ is measurable with respect to
$\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$.

articles.title: Later terms are measurable for the σ-algebra from a given index
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be
real-valued functions on a set $\Omega$, and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let
$\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ be the smallest σ-algebra on $\Omega$ for which every $X_i$ with
$i \ge n$ is Borel measurable. If $n \le i$, then $X_i$ is measurable with respect to
$\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$.

articles.title: Convergence of a random walk is measurable from every index
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be
real-valued functions on a set $\Omega$, let $S_m = \sum_{i < m} X_i$ be their partial sums, and
for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ be the smallest σ-algebra on $\Omega$ for
which every $X_i$ with $i \ge n$ is Borel measurable. For every $n$, the set of $\omega \in \Omega$
for which $S_m(\omega)$ converges to a real limit as $m \to \infty$ is measurable with respect to
$\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$.

The proof rewrites convergence as a Cauchy condition on the tail partial sums
$\sum_{n \le i < m} X_i$.

articles.title: Convergence of a random walk is a tail event
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real-valued
functions on a set $\Omega$ and let $S_m = \sum_{i < m} X_i$ be their partial sums. The set of
$\omega \in \Omega$ for which $S_m(\omega)$ converges to a real limit as $m \to \infty$ belongs to
the tail σ-algebra $\bigcap_{n} \sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ of the sequence, where
$\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ is the smallest σ-algebra on $\Omega$ for which every $X_i$ with
$i \ge n$ is Borel measurable.

articles.title: The convergence event on sequence space is measurable
articles.statement:
Equip $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$
with its product σ-algebra and write $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} \omega_i$. The set of
$\omega \in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ for which $S_n(\omega)$ converges to a finite real limit as
$n \to \infty$ is measurable.

articles.title: The event of drift to $-\infty$ on sequence space is measurable
articles.statement:
Equip
$\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with its product σ-algebra and write
$S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} \omega_i$. The set of $\omega \in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with
$S_n(\omega) \to -\infty$ as $n \to \infty$ is measurable.

articles.title: The event of drift to $+\infty$ on sequence space is measurable
articles.statement:
Equip
$\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with its product σ-algebra and write
$S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} \omega_i$. The set of $\omega \in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with
$S_n(\omega) \to +\infty$ as $n \to \infty$ is measurable.

articles.title: The zero-sequence event is measurable
articles.statement:
In the sequence space $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with
its product σ-algebra, the set of sequences $\omega$ with $\omega_i = 0$ for every $i$ is
measurable.

articles.title: The oscillation event on sequence space is measurable
articles.statement:
Equip $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with
its product σ-algebra and write $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} \omega_i$. The set of
$\omega \in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with $\limsup_{n \to \infty} S_n(\omega) = +\infty$ and
$\liminf_{n \to \infty} S_n(\omega) = -\infty$ (limits taken in the extended reals) is
measurable.

articles.title: Drift of a random walk to −∞ is measurable from every index
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be
real-valued functions on a set $\Omega$, let $S_m = \sum_{i < m} X_i$ be their partial sums, and
for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ be the smallest σ-algebra on $\Omega$ for
which every $X_i$ with $i \ge n$ is Borel measurable. For every $n$, the set of $\omega \in \Omega$
with $S_m(\omega) \to -\infty$ as $m \to \infty$ is measurable with respect to
$\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$.

articles.title: Drift of a random walk to −∞ is a tail event
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real-valued functions
on a set $\Omega$ and let $S_m = \sum_{i < m} X_i$ be their partial sums. The set of
$\omega \in \Omega$ with $S_m(\omega) \to -\infty$ as $m \to \infty$ belongs to the tail σ-algebra
$\bigcap_{n} \sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ of the sequence, where $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ is
the smallest σ-algebra on $\Omega$ for which every $X_i$ with $i \ge n$ is Borel measurable.

articles.title: Drift of a random walk to +∞ is measurable from every index
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be
real-valued functions on a set $\Omega$, let $S_m = \sum_{i < m} X_i$ be their partial sums, and
for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ be the smallest σ-algebra on $\Omega$ for
which every $X_i$ with $i \ge n$ is Borel measurable. For every $n$, the set of $\omega \in \Omega$
with $S_m(\omega) \to +\infty$ as $m \to \infty$ is measurable with respect to
$\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$.

The proof writes this set as a countable Boolean combination of sets defined by the tail
partial sums $\sum_{n \le i < m} X_i$.

articles.title: Drift of a random walk to +∞ is a tail event
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real-valued functions
on a set $\Omega$ and let $S_m = \sum_{i < m} X_i$ be their partial sums. The set of
$\omega \in \Omega$ with $S_m(\omega) \to +\infty$ as $m \to \infty$ belongs to the tail σ-algebra
$\bigcap_{n} \sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ of the sequence, where $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ is
the smallest σ-algebra on $\Omega$ for which every $X_i$ with $i \ge n$ is Borel measurable.

articles.title: A limit inferior −∞ of a random walk is measurable from every index
articles.statement:
Let
$X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real-valued functions on a set $\Omega$, let $S_m = \sum_{i < m} X_i$ be their
partial sums, and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ be the smallest
σ-algebra on $\Omega$ for which every $X_i$ with $i \ge n$ is Borel measurable. For every $n$, the
set of $\omega \in \Omega$ with $\liminf_{m \to \infty} S_m(\omega) = -\infty$, the limit inferior
taken in the extended reals, is measurable with respect to $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$.

articles.title: A limit superior +∞ of a random walk is measurable from every index
articles.statement:
Let
$X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real-valued functions on a set $\Omega$, let $S_m = \sum_{i < m} X_i$ be their
partial sums, and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$ be the smallest
σ-algebra on $\Omega$ for which every $X_i$ with $i \ge n$ is Borel measurable. For every $n$, the
set of $\omega \in \Omega$ with $\limsup_{m \to \infty} S_m(\omega) = +\infty$, the limit superior
taken in the extended reals, is measurable with respect to $\sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots)$.

articles.title: Tail measurability of the oscillation event
articles.statement:
Let $X_n : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ for
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ be a sequence of functions with partial sums $S_m = \sum_{i < m} X_i$. Then the
event that $\limsup_{m \to \infty} S_m = +\infty$ and $\liminf_{m \to \infty} S_m = -\infty$,
with the limit superior and inferior taken in the extended reals, belongs to the tail
σ-algebra of $X$.

articles.title: Oscillating random walk
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random variables on a probability
space $(\Omega, \mu)$ and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. The random walk $(S_n)$ oscillates if for
$\mu$-almost every $\omega$, $\limsup_n S_n(\omega) = +\infty$ and
$\liminf_n S_n(\omega) = -\infty$, the limits taken in the extended reals.

articles.title: Partial sums are unchanged by permuting the first coordinates
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a
permutation of $\mathbb{N}$ with $\sigma(m) = m$ for every $m \ge N$. Then for every real
sequence $(\omega_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ and every $n \ge N$,
$\sum_{i < n} \omega_{\sigma(i)} = \sum_{i < n} \omega_i$.

articles.title: Random-walk dichotomy
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be independent, identically distributed
real random variables on a probability space and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. Then one of the
following events has probability one: $S_n = 0$ for every $n$; $S_n \to +\infty$;
$S_n \to -\infty$; or $\limsup_n S_n = +\infty$ and $\liminf_n S_n = -\infty$.

articles.title: Random-walk dichotomy, finite-limit form
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be independent,
identically distributed real random variables on a probability space and
$S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. Then one of the following events has probability one: $S_n$
converges to a finite limit (which may depend on the outcome); $S_n \to +\infty$;
$S_n \to -\infty$; or $\limsup_n S_n = +\infty$ and $\liminf_n S_n = -\infty$.

articles.title: Liminf of a random walk
articles.statement:
For real-valued functions $X_0, X_1, \dots$ on a set $\Omega$ and
a point $\omega \in \Omega$, this is $\liminf_{n \to \infty} S_n(\omega)$, taken in the extended
reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$, where $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} X_i(\omega)$ is the $n$-th partial
sum.

articles.title: Limsup of a random walk
articles.statement:
For real-valued functions $X_0, X_1, \dots$ on a set $\Omega$ and
a point $\omega \in \Omega$, this is $\limsup_{n \to \infty} S_n(\omega)$, taken in the extended
reals $[-\infty, +\infty]$, where $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} X_i(\omega)$ is the $n$-th partial
sum.

articles.title: Partial sums of a random walk
articles.statement:
For a sequence of functions
$X_i : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th partial sum is
$S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} X_i(\omega)$, the position at time $n$ of the random walk on
$\mathbb{R}$ with increments $X_i$.

articles.title: Shift of a real sequence
articles.statement:
The one-step shift sends a real sequence
$\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \omega_2, \dots)$ to the sequence $(\omega_1, \omega_2, \dots)$
whose $i$-th term is $\omega_{i+1}$.

articles.title: σ-algebras generated by a sequence of functions
articles.statement:
For a sequence of functions
$X_n : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$, this is the sequence of σ-algebras $\sigma(X_n)$ on $\Omega$, where
$\sigma(X_n)$ consists of the preimages under $X_n$ of Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: σ-algebra generated by a tail of a sequence of σ-algebras
articles.statement:
Given σ-algebras
$\mathcal{A}_0, \mathcal{A}_1, \dots$ on $\Omega$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, this is
$\sigma(\mathcal{A}_n, \mathcal{A}_{n+1}, \dots)$, the smallest σ-algebra on $\Omega$
containing every $\mathcal{A}_i$ with $i \ge n$.

articles.title: Tail σ-algebra of a sequence of functions
articles.statement:
Let $\beta$ be a measurable space and let
$X_n : \Omega \to \beta$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$. The tail σ-algebra of $X$ is

$$\mathcal{T} = \bigcap_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \sigma(X_n, X_{n+1}, \dots),$$

the tail σ-algebra of the sequence of σ-algebras $\sigma(X_n)$, where $\sigma(X_n)$ consists of
the preimages under $X_n$ of measurable subsets of $\beta$. This is the tail σ-algebra
appearing in Kolmogorov's 0-1 law.

articles.title: Tail σ-algebra of a sequence of σ-algebras
articles.statement:
Given σ-algebras
$\mathcal{A}_0, \mathcal{A}_1, \dots$ on $\Omega$, the tail σ-algebra is

$$\mathcal{T} = \bigcap_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \sigma(\mathcal{A}_n, \mathcal{A}_{n+1}, \dots),$$

where $\sigma(\mathcal{A}_n, \mathcal{A}_{n+1}, \dots)$ is the smallest σ-algebra containing
every $\mathcal{A}_i$ with $i \ge n$. It contains the information observable by looking only at
events arbitrarily far into the future.

articles.title: Limsup minus infinity forces divergence to minus infinity
articles.statement:
Let $(S_n)$ be a sequence of
real numbers. If $\limsup_{n \to \infty} S_n = -\infty$ in the extended reals, then
$S_n \to -\infty$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Liminf plus infinity forces divergence to plus infinity
articles.statement:
Let $(S_n)$ be a sequence of real
numbers. If $\liminf_{n \to \infty} S_n = +\infty$ in the extended reals, then $S_n \to +\infty$ as
$n \to \infty$.

articles.title: A random walk is zero exactly when its steps are
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random
variables on a probability space and $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$. Then almost surely $S_n = 0$ for
every $n$ if and only if almost surely $X_i = 0$ for every $i$.

articles.title: Zero random walk
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, let
$X_0, X_1, \ldots$ be real-valued functions on $\Omega$, and let $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$ be the
partial sums of the random walk. The walk is a zero walk when, for $\mu$-almost every
$\omega \in \Omega$, we have $S_n(\omega) = 0$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

articles.title: Fair coin measure
articles.statement:
The fair coin measure is the measure
$\tfrac12 \delta_{\mathrm{false}} + \tfrac12 \delta_{\mathrm{true}}$ on the Booleans
$\{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$: it gives mass $1/2$ to each of the two values.

articles.title: Fair coin product measure
articles.statement:
The fair coin product measure is the measure on the space of
Boolean sequences $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$ given by the infinite
product, over $n \in \mathbb{N}$, of the fair coin measure, which gives mass $1/2$ to each of
$\mathrm{false}$ and $\mathrm{true}$.

articles.title: Successive products along a coin sequence
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group, let $\varphi, \psi \in G$,
and let $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$. For $i \ge 1$ let $f_i$ be the
generator chosen at index $i - 1$: $f_i = \varphi$ if $c(i - 1) = \mathrm{false}$ and
$f_i = \psi$ if $c(i - 1) = \mathrm{true}$. The successive products are defined by $P_0 = 1$
and $P_{n+1} = P_n f_{n+1}$, so $P_n = f_1 f_2 \cdots f_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, with
$P_0$ the empty product.

The typescript writes the terms as $f_1, f_1(f_2), f_1(f_2 f_3), \ldots$, read as successive
products.

articles.title: Scottish Book Problem 116(b) fails for arbitrary measurable sets
articles.statement:
The measurable-set form
of Scottish Book Problem 116(b) is false. For $\varphi, \psi$ in a group $G$ and a Boolean
sequence $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$, let $f_{n+1} = \varphi$ if
$c(n) = \mathrm{false}$ and $f_{n+1} = \psi$ if $c(n) = \mathrm{true}$, and define the successive
products by $P_0 = 1$ and $P_{n+1} = P_n f_{n+1}$. It is not the case that for every compact
Hausdorff topological group $G$ with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra and Haar probability measure
$\mu$, for $(\mu \otimes \mu)$-almost every pair $(\varphi, \psi) \in G \times G$ generating a
dense subgroup of $G$, for almost every $c$ under the fair coin product measure and every
measurable set $V \subseteq G$, the proportion of $P_0, \ldots, P_{N-1}$ that lie in $V$ tends
to $\mu(V)$ as $N \to \infty$.

Counterexample: take $G$ to be the circle $S^1$ with normalized Lebesgue measure. Almost every
pair $(\varphi, \psi)$ generates a dense subgroup. For any such pair and any $c$, the set $V_c$
of all successive products is countable, hence measurable with $\mu(V_c) = 0$, yet every
successive product lies in $V_c$, so the proportion equals $1$ for every $N \ge 1$. The set $V$
may depend on $c$ because it is quantified after $c$, and the only condition on $V$ is
measurability. The version restricted to sets $V$ whose frontier has measure $0$ is a different
statement, filed separately in OpenConjectures.

## Sources

- J. Schreier and S. Ulam, Problem 116, part (b) of the Scottish Book, typescript PDF p. 56, printed p. 53; see the commentary in R. D. Mauldin (ed.), The Scottish Book, 2nd ed. (Birkhäuser, 2015).

articles.title: Scottish Book Problem 116(b), measurable-set form
articles.statement:
The claim is the following. Let $G$ be
any compact Hausdorff topological group with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and let $\mu$ be a Haar
measure on $G$ that is a probability measure. For $\varphi, \psi \in G$ and a Boolean sequence
$c : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$, let $f_{n+1} = \varphi$ if
$c(n) = \mathrm{false}$ and $f_{n+1} = \psi$ if $c(n) = \mathrm{true}$, and define the successive
products by $P_0 = 1$ and $P_{n+1} = P_n f_{n+1}$. Then for $(\mu \otimes \mu)$-almost every pair
$(\varphi, \psi) \in G \times G$, if the subgroup generated by $\varphi$ and $\psi$ is dense in
$G$, then for almost every $c$ with respect to the fair coin product measure, for every
measurable set $V \subseteq G$,

$$\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{\#\{n < N : P_n \in V\}}{N} = \mu(V).$$

The typescript's "region" is read as an arbitrary measurable set, since the typescript does not
specify a class of regions; the set $V$ is quantified after $c$ and may depend on it.

articles.title: Generator chosen by a coin sequence
articles.statement:
Let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be elements of a type $G$
and let $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$ be a sequence. For
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th chosen generator is $\varphi$ if $c(n) = \mathrm{false}$ and
$\psi$ if $c(n) = \mathrm{true}$.

Index $0$ corresponds to $f_1$ in the Scottish Book typescript.

articles.title: First-return probability
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a $k$-regular Cayley graph on a group $G$ with
generating set $S$. For $n \ge 1$, the first-return probability of $\Gamma$ at time $n$ is the
real number obtained by dividing by $k^n$ the number of words $(s_1, \dots, s_n) \in S^n$ with
$s_1 s_2 \cdots s_n = 1$ and $s_1 \cdots s_m \ne 1$ for every $0 < m < n$; at time $n = 0$ it
is $0$.

Since $S$ has $k$ elements, this is the probability that the walk $1, s_1, s_1 s_2, \dots$ with
independent uniform steps in $S$ is back at $1$ for the first time at step $n$.

articles.title: Regular Cayley graph
articles.statement:
For a group $G$ and a natural number $k$, the data of a $k$-regular
Cayley graph on $G$ is a finite set $S \subseteq G$ of generators such that $S$ is closed under
inverses ($s \in S$ implies $s^{-1} \in S$), the identity $1$ does not belong to $S$, every
element of $G$ is the product of a finite (possibly empty) list of elements of $S$, and $S$ has
exactly $k$ elements.

articles.title: Uniform return-probability gap for transient Cayley graphs
articles.statement:
For every natural number
$k > 1$ there is a real number $C < 1$ such that for every group $G$ and every $k$-regular Cayley
graph $\Gamma$ on $G$ whose return probability is less than $1$, the return probability of
$\Gamma$ is at most $C$.

This follows from Tessera and Tointon, Corollary 1.3: there is a universal $c > 0$ such that
simple random walk on every connected, locally finite, vertex-transitive graph is recurrent or
escapes with probability at least $c$, so $C = 1 - c$ works for every $k$.

## Sources

- Romain Tessera and Matthew Tointon, Sharp relations between volume growth, isoperimetry and escape probability in vertex-transitive graphs, arXiv preprint (2020, v2 2024), arXiv:2001.01467, https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.01467.

articles.title: Uniform return-probability gap
articles.statement:
The statement that for every natural number $k > 1$ there
is a real number $C < 1$ such that for every group $G$ and every $k$-regular Cayley graph
$\Gamma$ on $G$, if the return probability of $\Gamma$ is less than $1$ (that is, $\Gamma$ is
transient), then it is at most $C$.

articles.title: Return probability
articles.statement:
The return probability of a $k$-regular Cayley graph $\Gamma$ is the
sum $\sum_{n \ge 0} p_n$, where $p_n$ is the first-return probability of $\Gamma$ at time $n$.

It is the probability that simple random walk on $\Gamma$ started at the identity ever returns
to the identity.

articles.title: The post-stopping-time sequence is a.e. measurable
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable
space $\Omega$, let $(\mathcal{F}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a filtration on $\Omega$, let
$X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be maps from $\Omega$ to a measurable space $S$ that are each
$\mu$-almost-everywhere measurable, and let $T : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$ be a stopping time for
$(\mathcal{F}_n)$. Then for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ the map
$\omega \mapsto X_{T(\omega)+k+1}(\omega)$ is $\mu$-almost-everywhere measurable.

articles.title: Shifted terms of an identically distributed sequence
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on a
measurable space $\Omega$ and let $X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be maps from $\Omega$ to a measurable
space $S$ such that $X_i$ and $X_j$ are identically distributed under $\mu$ for all $i, j$. Then
for all $n, k \in \mathbb{N}$ the map $X_{n+k+1}$ has the same distribution under $\mu$ as
$X_0$.

articles.title: A stopping-time event is independent of finitely many later observations
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a
probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, let $(\mathcal{F}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a
filtration on $\Omega$, and let $X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be measurable maps from $\Omega$ to a
measurable space $S$ that are mutually independent under $\mu$. Suppose that for every $n$ the
σ-algebra $\mathcal{F}_n$ is contained in the σ-algebra generated by $X_0, \dots, X_n$, and let
$T : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$ be a stopping time for $(\mathcal{F}_n)$. Then for every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, every finite set $F \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and all sets $A_k \subseteq S$
($k \in \mathbb{N}$) such that $A_k$ is measurable for every $k \in F$,
$\mu(\{T = n\} \cap \bigcap_{k \in F} X_{n+k+1}^{-1}(A_k)) =
\mu(\{T = n\}) \prod_{k \in F} \mu(X_{n+k+1}^{-1}(A_k))$.

articles.title: A stopping-time event is independent of a later observation
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability
measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, let $(\mathcal{F}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a filtration
on $\Omega$, and let $X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be measurable maps from $\Omega$ to a measurable space
$S$ that are mutually independent under $\mu$. Suppose that for every $n$ the σ-algebra
$\mathcal{F}_n$ is contained in the σ-algebra generated by $X_0, \dots, X_n$, and let
$T : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$ be a stopping time for $(\mathcal{F}_n)$. Then for all
$n, k \in \mathbb{N}$ and every measurable set $A \subseteq S$,
$\mu(\{T = n\} \cap X_{n+k+1}^{-1}(A)) = \mu(\{T = n\})\,\mu(X_{n+k+1}^{-1}(A))$.

articles.title: Level sets of a stopping time are measurable
articles.statement:
Let $(\mathcal{F}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a
filtration on a measurable space $\Omega$ and let $T : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$ be a stopping time
for $(\mathcal{F}_n)$. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ the set $\{\omega : T(\omega) = n\}$ is
measurable in the σ-algebra of $\Omega$.

articles.title: Preimage measures of a post-stopping-time variable
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on
a measurable space $\Omega$, let $(\mathcal{F}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a filtration on $\Omega$,
and let $X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be measurable maps from $\Omega$ to a measurable space $S$ that are
mutually independent and identically distributed under $\mu$. Suppose that for every $n$ the
σ-algebra $\mathcal{F}_n$ is contained in the σ-algebra generated by $X_0, \dots, X_n$, and let
$T : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$ be a stopping time for $(\mathcal{F}_n)$. Then for every
$k \in \mathbb{N}$ and every measurable set $A \subseteq S$,
$\mu(\{\omega : X_{T(\omega)+k+1}(\omega) \in A\}) = \mu(X_0^{-1}(A))$.

articles.title: Post-stopping-time sequence
articles.statement:
Given maps $X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ from a set $\Omega$ to a set
$S$ and a map $T : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$, the post-stopping-time sequence is the sequence
$(Y_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ of maps from $\Omega$ to $S$ given by
$Y_k(\omega) = X_{T(\omega)+k+1}(\omega)$. When $T$ is a stopping time, this is the sequence of
observations immediately after time $T$.

articles.title: Strong Markov property for i.i.d. sequences: independence after a stopping time
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$
be a probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, let $(\mathcal{F}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$
be a filtration on $\Omega$, and let $X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be measurable maps from $\Omega$ to a
measurable space $S$ that are mutually independent and identically distributed under $\mu$.
Suppose that for every $n$ the σ-algebra $\mathcal{F}_n$ is contained in the σ-algebra generated
by $X_0, \dots, X_n$, and let $T : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$ be a stopping time for
$(\mathcal{F}_n)$. Then the maps $Y_k(\omega) = X_{T(\omega)+k+1}(\omega)$, $k \in \mathbb{N}$,
are mutually independent under $\mu$.

articles.title: Strong Markov property for i.i.d. sequences: the law after a stopping time
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a
probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, let $(\mathcal{F}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a
filtration on $\Omega$, and let $X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be measurable maps from $\Omega$ to a
measurable space $S$ that are mutually independent and identically distributed under $\mu$.
Suppose that for every $n$ the σ-algebra $\mathcal{F}_n$ is contained in the σ-algebra generated
by $X_0, \dots, X_n$, and let $T : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$ be a stopping time for
$(\mathcal{F}_n)$. Then for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ the map
$\omega \mapsto X_{T(\omega)+k+1}(\omega)$ has the same distribution under $\mu$ as $X_0$.

articles.title: Strong Markov property (independence from the past)
articles.statement:
Let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be measurable
random variables on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ with values in a measurable space $S$,
mutually independent and all with the same distribution. Let $(\mathcal F_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a
filtration with $\mathcal F_n \subseteq \sigma(X_0, \dots, X_n)$ for every $n$, and let
$T : \Omega \to \mathbb N$ be a stopping time for $(\mathcal F_n)$, finite everywhere. Then the
stopped σ-algebra $\mathcal F_T$ is independent of the σ-algebra generated by the
post-stopping-time sequence $(X_{T+k+1})_{k \ge 0}$.

articles.title: Strong Markov property for i.i.d. sequences: the post-stopping-time sequence is i.i.d
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$, let
$(\mathcal{F}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a filtration on $\Omega$, and let
$X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be measurable maps from $\Omega$ to a measurable space $S$ that are
mutually independent and identically distributed under $\mu$. Suppose that for every $n$ the
σ-algebra $\mathcal{F}_n$ is contained in the σ-algebra generated by $X_0, \dots, X_n$, and let
$T : \Omega \to \mathbb{N}$ be a stopping time for $(\mathcal{F}_n)$. Then the
post-stopping-time sequence $Y_k(\omega) = X_{T(\omega)+k+1}(\omega)$, $k \in \mathbb{N}$, is
again i.i.d. with the law of $X_0$: each $Y_k$ has the same distribution under $\mu$ as $X_0$,
and $(Y_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ is mutually independent under $\mu$.

articles.title: Fisher information is the second moment of the score
articles.statement:
For a positive density family, `E_θ [score²] = I(θ)`: the Fisher information of
`FisherInformation.fisherInformation` is the second moment of the score under `p θ ν`.

articles.title: Product of a distributionally convergent and a vanishing sequence
articles.statement:
A sequence `A i` converging in distribution, times a sequence `η i` converging in
probability to `0`, converges in probability to `0` (a consequence of Slutsky's theorem).

articles.title: Score function
articles.statement: The **score** `∂_θ log p θ x` of a one-parameter family of densities `p`.

articles.title: Central limit theorem for the score
articles.statement:
For i.i.d. observations with law `p θ₀ ν`, a
positive density family differentiable in `θ` at `θ₀`, a measurable score with mean zero and
`∫ score² d(p θ₀ ν) < ∞`, the normalized score `n^{-1/2} ∑_{i<n} score p θ₀ (X i)` converges in
distribution to `N(0, I(θ₀))`.

## Sources

- Lehmann & Casella (1998), §6.3; van der Vaart (1998), ch. 5.

articles.title: Asymptotic normality of consistent roots of the likelihood equation
articles.statement:
**Asymptotic normality of consistent roots of the likelihood equation** (Cramér's
conditions). Let `p θ` be positive
densities with respect to `ν`, and on the ball of radius `δ > 0` about `θ₀` let each `p θ` be
measurable with `∫ p θ dν = 1`, so that the family is a statistical model there (as in
`FisherInformation.cramerRao`). The proof uses measurability only at `θ₀` and does not use the
normalization `_hp_int`: the limit theorem holds for roots of any criterion with these
derivatives.
Let `X 0, X 1, …` be i.i.d. with law `p θ₀ ν`. Assume that on the same ball the log-likelihood
`log p θ x` is differentiable in `θ` for every `x` (so that `score p θ x` is its true derivative
there, not Lean's junk value `0` of `deriv` at a nondifferentiable point) and the score
`∂_θ log p θ x` is twice differentiable in `θ` for every `x`, with `|∂³_θ log p θ x| ≤ M x`
for an integrable `M`; that the score `∂_θ log p θ₀` is measurable and square integrable with
mean zero; that `∂²_θ log p θ₀` is measurable and integrable with `E ∂²_θ log p θ₀ = -I(θ₀)`
(the information identity); and that `0 < I(θ₀)`. The two moment identities are what
differentiating `∫ p θ dν = 1` twice under the integral sign gives; they are assumed directly.
Let `θhat n` be estimators that solve the likelihood equation `∑_{i<n} ∂_θ log p θ (X i) = 0`
with probability tending to one and converge to `θ₀` in probability. Then
`√n (θhat n - θ₀) → N(0, 1 / I(θ₀))` in distribution. The roots need not maximize the
likelihood; for a maximum-likelihood estimator, consistency and the likelihood equation must
be established separately (for example, from an interior maximum of a differentiable
likelihood).

## Sources

- Cramér (1946), §33.3; Lehmann & Casella (1998), Theorem 6.3.10; van der Vaart (1998), Theorem 5.41.

articles.title: Asymptotic normality of a consistent root of an estimating equation
articles.statement:
**Asymptotic normality of a consistent root of an estimating equation** (one-dimensional
Z-estimator under Cramér-type conditions). Let `X 0, X 1, …` be i.i.d. with law `μX` and let
`ψ θ x` satisfy, for every `x` and every `θ` in the ball of radius `δ > 0` about `θ₀`: `ψ · x`
and `∂_θ ψ · x` are differentiable at `θ`, and `|∂²_θ ψ θ x| ≤ M x` with `M` integrable. Assume
`E ψ θ₀ = 0`, `E ψ θ₀² < ∞`, `∂_θ ψ θ₀` integrable with `E ∂_θ ψ θ₀ ≠ 0`. Let `θhat n` be
estimators that solve `∑_{i<n} ψ θ (X i) = 0` with probability tending to one and converge to
`θ₀` in probability. Then `√n (θhat n - θ₀)` converges in distribution to
`N(0, E ψ θ₀² / (E ∂_θ ψ θ₀)²)`.

## Sources

- van der Vaart (1998), Theorem 5.41 (one-dimensional case, with the third-derivative envelope of Cramér (1946), §33.3); Lehmann & Casella (1998), §6.3.

articles.title: Convergence to zero in probability by domination on likely events
articles.statement:
If `|W i| ≤ V i` on events `G i` whose complements have probability tending to `0`, and
`V i` tends to `0` in probability, then `W i` tends to `0` in probability.

articles.title: Bias as an integral
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a measurable space, $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator,
$\mu$ a probability measure on $S$ for which $W$ is integrable, and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ a
target. Then the bias of $W$ under $\mu$ at $\theta$ equals $\int_S W \, d\mu - \theta$.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_723199a7ca6fb3e936a73618`.

articles.title: Bias of an estimator
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a measurable space, $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator,
$\mu$ a probability measure on $S$ for which $W$ is integrable, and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ a
target. The bias of $W$ under $\mu$ at $\theta$ is $\int_S W \, d\mu - \theta$, the expected value
of $W$ under $\mu$ minus $\theta$.

Integrability of $W$ is part of the input: it is the domain on which the expectation exists in
the source (Chapter 2, Definition 2.2.1), so a nonintegrable estimator has no finite bias.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_723199a7ca6fb3e936a73618`.

articles.title: An unbiased estimator has the target as its expectation
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a measurable space,
$W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator, $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of probability
measures on $S$ and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function. If $W$ is unbiased for
$\tau$ under the family $(P_\theta)$, then $\int_S W \, dP_\theta = \tau(\theta)$ for every
$\theta \in \Theta$.

articles.title: Family bias as an integral
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a measurable space, $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an
estimator, $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of probability measures on $S$ such that $W$
is integrable for every $P_\theta$, and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function. Then for
every $\theta \in \Theta$ the family bias of $W$ at $\theta$ equals
$\int_S W \, dP_\theta - \tau(\theta)$.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_723199a7ca6fb3e936a73618`.

articles.title: Family bias of an estimator
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a measurable space, $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an
estimator, $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of probability measures on $S$ such that $W$
is integrable for every $P_\theta$, and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function. The
family bias of $W$ is the function on $\Theta$ whose value at $\theta$ is the bias of $W$ under
$P_\theta$ at the target $\tau(\theta)$, that is, $\int_S W \, dP_\theta - \tau(\theta)$.

The estimator $W$ is fixed before the family and does not depend on $\theta$.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_723199a7ca6fb3e936a73618`.

articles.title: Family mean squared error as an integral
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a measurable space,
$W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator, $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of probability
measures on $S$ and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function such that
$(W - \tau(\theta))^2$ is integrable for $P_\theta$ for every $\theta \in \Theta$. Then for every
$\theta \in \Theta$ the family mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ equals
$\int_S (W(x) - \tau(\theta))^2 \, dP_\theta(x)$.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_fd40353442120bd19166139d`.

articles.title: Bias–variance decomposition for a parametric family
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a measurable space,
$W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator, $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of probability
measures on $S$ and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function. Suppose that for every
