$\theta \in \Theta$, $W$ has a finite second moment under $P_\theta$, and $W$ and
$(W - \tau(\theta))^2$ are integrable for $P_\theta$. Then for every $\theta \in \Theta$ the family
mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ equals the variance $\operatorname{Var}_{P_\theta}(W)$ of
$W$ under $P_\theta$ plus the square of the family bias of $W$ at $\theta$.

## Sources

- equation 7.3.1, in family form for a single fixed estimator.

articles.title: An unbiased estimator has mean squared error equal to its variance
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a
measurable space, $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator, $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of
probability measures on $S$ and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function. Suppose that $W$
is unbiased for $\tau$ under the family, and that for every $\theta \in \Theta$, $W$ has a finite
second moment under $P_\theta$ and $(W - \tau(\theta))^2$ is integrable for $P_\theta$. Then for
every $\theta \in \Theta$ the family mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ equals the variance
$\operatorname{Var}_{P_\theta}(W)$ of $W$ under $P_\theta$.

articles.title: Family mean squared error of an estimator
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a measurable space,
$W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator, $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of probability
measures on $S$ and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function such that
$(W - \tau(\theta))^2$ is integrable for $P_\theta$ for every $\theta \in \Theta$. The family mean
squared error of $W$ is the function on $\Theta$ whose value at $\theta$ is the mean squared error
of $W$ under $P_\theta$ at the target $\tau(\theta)$, that is,
$\int_S (W(x) - \tau(\theta))^2 \, dP_\theta(x)$.

The estimator $W$ is fixed before the family and does not depend on $\theta$.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_fd40353442120bd19166139d`.

articles.title: Frequentist risk as an integral
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a measurable space, $\delta : S \to A$ a
decision rule, $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of probability measures on $S$ and
$\ell : \Theta \times A \to [0, \infty)$ a loss function such that
$x \mapsto \ell(\theta, \delta(x))$ is integrable for $P_\theta$ for every $\theta \in \Theta$.
Then for every $\theta \in \Theta$ the frequentist risk of $\delta$ at $\theta$ equals
$\int_S \ell(\theta, \delta(x)) \, dP_\theta(x)$.

articles.title: Extended frequentist risk of a measurable non-integrable loss is infinite
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a
measurable space, $\delta : S \to A$ a decision rule, $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of
probability measures on $S$, $\ell : \Theta \times A \to [0, \infty)$ a loss, and
$\theta \in \Theta$. If the function $x \mapsto \ell(\theta, \delta(x))$ is almost everywhere
strongly measurable with respect to $P_\theta$ but not $P_\theta$-integrable, then the extended
frequentist risk $\int_S \ell(\theta, \delta(x)) \, dP_\theta(x) \in [0, \infty]$ of $\delta$ at
$\theta$ equals $\infty$.

So a measurable non-integrable loss is never assigned a finite extended risk.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_36871388da7326a07a5e4f71`.

articles.title: Extended frequentist risk
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a measurable space, $\delta : S \to A$ a decision
rule, $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of probability measures on $S$, and
$\ell : \Theta \times A \to [0, \infty)$ a loss. The extended frequentist risk of $\delta$ at
$\theta \in \Theta$ is the Lebesgue integral $\int_S \ell(\theta, \delta(x)) \, dP_\theta(x)$, taken
in $[0, \infty]$.

When the loss is $P_\theta$-integrable for every $\theta$, this is the frequentist risk; when it is
measurable but not integrable at $\theta$, it equals $\infty$.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_36871388da7326a07a5e4f71`.

articles.title: Frequentist risk is nonnegative
articles.statement:
Let $\delta : S \to A$ be a decision rule,
$(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of probability measures on $S$, and
$\ell : \Theta \times A \to [0, \infty)$ a loss such that $x \mapsto \ell(\theta, \delta(x))$ is
$P_\theta$-integrable for every $\theta \in \Theta$. Then the frequentist risk $R(\theta, \delta)$
of $\delta$ at $\theta$ is nonnegative for every $\theta \in \Theta$.

articles.title: Mean squared error is frequentist risk under squared-error loss
articles.statement:
Let
$(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ be a family of probability measures on $S$,
$W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function such that
$x \mapsto (W(x) - \tau(\theta))^2$ is $P_\theta$-integrable for every $\theta \in \Theta$. Then for
every $\theta$, the frequentist risk at $\theta$ of $W$, as a decision rule with actions in
$\mathbb{R}$, under the squared-error loss $\ell(\theta, a) = (a - \tau(\theta))^2$ equals the
family mean squared error of $W$ for $\tau$ at $\theta$.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_36871388da7326a07a5e4f71`.

articles.title: Frequentist risk
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a measurable space, $\delta : S \to A$ a decision rule,
$(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ a family of probability measures on $S$, and
$\ell : \Theta \times A \to [0, \infty)$ a loss such that $x \mapsto \ell(\theta, \delta(x))$ is
$P_\theta$-integrable for every $\theta \in \Theta$. The frequentist risk of $\delta$ is the
function $\Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ given by
$R(\theta, \delta) = \int_S \ell(\theta, \delta(x)) \, dP_\theta(x)$.

The rule $\delta$ does not depend on $\theta$, and the action space $A$ may differ from $\Theta$.
No prior, kernel or optimality criterion enters.

## Sources

- Casella–Berger equation 7.3.16; the integrability hypothesis is the expectation domain of Chapter 2 Definition 2.2.1. Blueprint `af_36871388da7326a07a5e4f71`.

articles.title: A finite second moment makes the squared error integrable
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability
measure on $S$ and $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator in $L^2(\mu)$. Then for every
$\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ the squared error $x \mapsto (W(x) - \theta)^2$ is $\mu$-integrable.

articles.title: Unbiased estimators are integrable
articles.statement:
Let $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ be a family of
probability measures on $S$ and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function. If an estimator
$W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ is unbiased for $\tau$, then $W$ is $P_\theta$-integrable for every
$\theta \in \Theta$.

articles.title: An estimator is unbiased exactly when its bias vanishes
articles.statement:
Let
$(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ be a family of probability measures on $S$,
$\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function, and $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator that is
$P_\theta$-integrable for every $\theta \in \Theta$. Then $W$ is unbiased for $\tau$ if and only if
its family bias $\int_S W \, dP_\theta - \tau(\theta)$ is zero for every $\theta \in \Theta$.

articles.title: Unbiased estimator
articles.statement:
Let $(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}$ be a family of probability measures
on a measurable space $S$ and $\tau : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}$ a target function. An estimator
$W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ is unbiased for $\tau$ if for every $\theta \in \Theta$ the function $W$ is
$P_\theta$-integrable and $\int_S W \, dP_\theta = \tau(\theta)$.

Integrability is part of the definition, so a non-integrable estimator is never unbiased. The
estimator $W$ is fixed and does not depend on $\theta$.

## Sources

- Casella–Berger Definition 7.3.2 is the case $\tau(\theta) = \theta$ on real parameters; the general target follows section 7.3.2. Blueprint `af_95118d196fd6478105a6eb43`.

articles.title: Extended mean squared error of a measurable non-integrable squared error is infinite
articles.statement:
Let
$\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ an estimator and
$\theta \in \mathbb{R}$. If the squared error $x \mapsto (W(x) - \theta)^2$ is almost everywhere
strongly measurable with respect to $\mu$ but not $\mu$-integrable, then the extended mean squared
error $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x) \in [0, \infty]$ of $W$ at $\theta$ equals $\infty$.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_fd40353442120bd19166139d`.

articles.title: Extended mean squared error
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$,
let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be an estimator and let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ be a target value. The
extended mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ is the (lower) Lebesgue integral
$\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x)$ of the nonnegative squared error, computed in $[0, \infty]$.
It is defined for every $W$, with no integrability hypothesis.

When the squared error is $\mu$-integrable, this value is finite and equals the mean squared error;
when the squared error is almost everywhere strongly measurable but not $\mu$-integrable, it equals
$\infty$.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_fd40353442120bd19166139d`.

articles.title: Mean squared error as an integral
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable
space $S$, let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, and suppose the squared error
$x \mapsto (W(x) - \theta)^2$ is $\mu$-integrable. Then the mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$
under $\mu$ equals $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x)$.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_fd40353442120bd19166139d`.

articles.title: Bias–variance decomposition of the mean squared error
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure
on a measurable space $S$, let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be
square-integrable with respect to $\mu$, that is, $W \in L^2(\mu)$. Then the mean squared error of
$W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ equals $\operatorname{Var}_\mu(W) + b^2$, where
$b = \int_S W \, d\mu - \theta$ is the bias of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$.

The integrability that the mean squared error and the bias require follows from $W \in L^2(\mu)$.

## Sources

- Casella–Berger, equation (7.3.1); blueprint `af_3a1bafba0b7dff99554b01f0`.

articles.title: Mean squared error as variance plus squared mean deviation
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability
measure on a measurable space $S$, let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be
square-integrable with respect to $\mu$, that is, $W \in L^2(\mu)$. Then the mean squared error of
$W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ equals
$\operatorname{Var}_\mu(W) + \left(\int_S W \, d\mu - \theta\right)^2$.

## Sources

- Casella–Berger, equation (7.3.1) in expectation form; blueprint `af_3a1bafba0b7dff99554b01f0`.

articles.title: Mean squared error of an unbiased estimator
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a
measurable space $S$, let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be
square-integrable with respect to $\mu$ (that is, $W \in L^2(\mu)$) and satisfy
$\int_S W \, d\mu = \theta$. Then the mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$ equals
$\operatorname{Var}_\mu(W)$.

## Sources

- the display following Definition 7.3.2.

articles.title: Mean squared error
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $S$, let
$W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be an estimator and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$ a target value, and suppose the
squared error $x \mapsto (W(x) - \theta)^2$ is $\mu$-integrable. The mean squared error of $W$ at
$\theta$ under $\mu$ is the real number $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x)$.

The integrability hypothesis is part of the definition: without it no finite mean squared error is
defined.

## Sources

- Casella–Berger, Definition 7.3.1; blueprint `af_fd40353442120bd19166139d`.

articles.title: Finite and extended frequentist risk agree
articles.statement:
Let $\Theta$ and $A$ be sets, let
$(P_\vartheta)_{\vartheta \in \Theta}$ be a family of probability measures on a measurable space
$S$, let $\delta : S \to A$ be a decision rule and $\ell : \Theta \times A \to [0, \infty)$ a
loss, and suppose $x \mapsto \ell(\vartheta, \delta(x))$ is $P_\vartheta$-integrable for every
$\vartheta \in \Theta$. Then for every $\theta \in \Theta$ the extended frequentist risk
$\int_S \ell(\theta, \delta(x)) \, dP_\theta(x)$, computed in $[0, \infty]$, is finite and equals
the frequentist risk of $\delta$ at $\theta$.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_36871388da7326a07a5e4f71`.

articles.title: Finite and extended mean squared error agree
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a
measurable space $S$, let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, and suppose the
squared error $x \mapsto (W(x) - \theta)^2$ is $\mu$-integrable. Then the extended mean squared
error $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x)$, computed in $[0, \infty]$, is finite and equals the
mean squared error of $W$ at $\theta$ under $\mu$.

## Sources

- blueprint `af_fd40353442120bd19166139d`.

articles.title: Bias–variance decomposition of the extended mean squared error
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability
measure on a measurable space $S$, let $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $W : S \to \mathbb{R}$ be
square-integrable with respect to $\mu$, that is, $W \in L^2(\mu)$. Then the extended mean squared
error $\int_S (W(x) - \theta)^2 \, d\mu(x)$, computed in $[0, \infty]$, is finite and equals
$\operatorname{Var}_\mu(W) + b^2$, where $b = \int_S W \, d\mu - \theta$ is the bias of $W$ at
$\theta$ under $\mu$.

articles.title: Exponential tilting of a centered Gaussian
articles.statement:
The law `N(0, v)` reweighted by the density
`exp(h x - h² v / 2)` is `N(h v, v)`. For `v = 0` both sides are the Dirac mass at `0`.

articles.title: Le Cam's first lemma
articles.statement:
**Le Cam's first lemma** (LAN case). Let `Qₙ = exp(Λₙ) · P` be probability measures. If
`Sₙ → N(0, v)` in distribution under `P` and `Λₙ - h Sₙ → -h² v / 2` in `P`-probability, then
`Qₙ` is contiguous with respect to `P`. This is the case of Le Cam's first lemma in which
`Λₙ → N(-σ²/2, σ²)` under `P`, `σ² = h² v`; the general form (any limit `L` of `dQₙ/dP` with
`E L = 1`) is not stated here.

## Sources

- Le Cam (1960); van der Vaart (1998), Lemma 6.4 and Example 6.5.

articles.title: Contiguity of sequences of measures
articles.statement:
The sequence of measures `Q n` is **contiguous** with respect to `P n` (`Q ◁ P`): every
sequence of measurable sets whose `P n`-measure tends to `0` has `Q n`-measure tending to `0`.

## Sources

- van der Vaart (1998), Definition 6.3.

articles.title: Le Cam's third lemma
articles.statement:
**Le Cam's third lemma** (LAN case). Let `Qₙ = exp(Λₙ) · P` be probability measures. If
`Sₙ → N(0, v)` in distribution under `P` and `Λₙ - h Sₙ → -h² v / 2` in `P`-probability, then
`Sₙ → N(h v, v)` in distribution under `Qₙ`. This is the case of Le Cam's third lemma for the
central sequence itself (covariance `h v` with `Λₙ`); the general form, for an arbitrary
statistic jointly asymptotically normal with `Λₙ`, is not stated here.

## Sources

- Le Cam (1960); van der Vaart (1998), Theorem 6.6.

articles.title: Contiguity transfers convergence in probability
articles.statement:
If `Q ◁ P` (a fixed `P`) and the
measurable functions `T n` converge to `c` in `P`-probability, then
`Q n {ω | ε ≤ |T n ω - c|} → 0` for every `ε > 0`.

## Sources

- van der Vaart (1998), ch. 6.

articles.title: Wald's consistency theorem for maximum likelihood
articles.statement:
**Wald's consistency theorem for maximum likelihood** (Ferguson's form, positive
densities). Let `Θ` be a compact metric space and `p θ` probability densities with respect to
`ν`, positive, measurable in `x` and continuous in `θ`. Assume the model is identifiable
(`p θ = p θ₀` `ν`-a.e. only for `θ = θ₀`) and that the log-likelihood ratios have an upper
envelope `K` integrable under `p θ₀`. Let `X 0, X 1, …` be independent with law `p θ₀ ν`, and
let `θhat n ω` maximize the log-likelihood `∑_{i<n} log p θ (X i ω)` over `θ ∈ Θ`. Then
`θhat n → θ₀` almost surely.

## Sources

- Wald (1949); Ferguson (1996), Theorem 17. Proves the deferred entry `ae_tendsto_maximumLikelihood`.

articles.title: Cramér–Rao inequality
articles.statement:
**Cramér–Rao inequality**, with only the hypotheses the proof needs. Let `p θ'` be
nonnegative probability densities with respect to `ν` for `θ'` near `θ`, with square-integrable
score at `θ`, and let `T` be an estimator with finite second moment under `p θ` that is unbiased
for `g θ'` near `θ`. If `∫ p θ' dν` and `∫ T p θ' dν` can be differentiated under the integral
sign at `θ`, then `g'(θ)² / I(θ) ≤ Var_θ T`. When `I(θ) = 0` the left side is the junk value
`0` and the statement is trivial; the informative case is `0 < I(θ)`.

## Sources

- Cramér (1946), ch. 32; Rao (1945); Lehmann & Casella (1998), ch. 2.

articles.title: Cramér–Rao inequality
articles.statement:
Let `p θ'` be probability densities with respect to `ν` for
`θ'` near `θ`, differentiable in the parameter at `θ`, with finite positive Fisher information
`I(θ)`, and let `T` be an estimator with finite second moment that is unbiased for `g θ'` near
`θ`. If `∫ p θ' dν` and `∫ T p θ' dν` can be differentiated under the integral sign at `θ`,
then `Var_θ T ≥ g'(θ)² / I(θ)`. The hypotheses `hp_meas`, `hp_diff` and `hI_pos` are not
needed; see `cramerRao_general`.

## Sources

- Cramér (1946), ch. 32; Rao (1945); Lehmann & Casella (1998), ch. 2. Proves the deferred entry `cramerRao`.

articles.title: Fisher information
articles.statement:
The **Fisher information** at `θ` of the one-parameter family of densities `p θ` with
respect to `ν`: `∫ (∂_θ p θ x)² / p θ x dν(x)`. Points with `p θ x = 0` contribute `0` (for a
nonnegative family, `∂_θ p θ x = 0` there).

articles.title: Probability law of a density family member
articles.statement: The probability law with density `p θ` with respect to `ν`.

articles.title: Cramér–Rao inequality, multiplicative form
articles.statement:
Under the hypotheses of `cramerRao_general`,
`g'(θ)² ≤ I(θ) · Var_θ T`. Unlike the quotient form, this is informative when `I(θ) = 0`: it then
says `g'(θ) = 0`.

## Sources

- Cramér (1946), ch. 32; Rao (1945); Lehmann & Casella (1998), ch. 2.

articles.title: Normalized density families are determined by their densities
articles.statement:
Let $F$ and $G$ be
normalized density families on a measurable space $\Omega$ with the same parameter set
$\Theta$ and the same dominating measure $\mu$. If for every $\theta \in \Theta$ and every
$x \in \Omega$ the density of $F$ at $\theta$ and the density of $G$ at $\theta$ take the same
value at $x$, then $F = G$.

Only the densities are compared; the measurability and normalization conditions are
propositions.

articles.title: Likelihood of the empty sample
articles.statement:
For a normalized density family $F$, every parameter
$\theta$ and the empty sample $x$ (sample size $n = 0$), the iid likelihood of $\theta$ at $x$
equals $1$, the empty product.

articles.title: Likelihood of an iid sample
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a normalized density family on $\Omega$ with
parameter set $\Theta$ and densities $f_\theta$ for $\theta \in \Theta$. For a sample size $n$,
a parameter $\theta \in \Theta$ and a sample $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}) \in \Omega^n$, the iid
likelihood of $\theta$ at $x$ is $L_n(\theta; x) = \prod_{i < n} f_\theta(x_i)$, a value in
$[0, \infty]$. For $n = 0$ this is the empty product $1$.

articles.title: Induced likelihood
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a normalized density family on $\Omega$ with parameter
set $\Theta$, let $n$ be a sample size, let $\tau : \Theta \to H$ be a map into a set $H$, and
let $x \in \Omega^n$ be a sample. For $\eta$ in the image of $\tau$, the induced likelihood of
$\eta$ at $x$ is the supremum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the iid likelihood $L_n(\theta; x)$ over
the fiber of $\tau$ above $\eta$:

$$L^*_n(\eta; x) = \sup_{\theta \in \Theta,\ \tau(\theta) = \eta} L_n(\theta; x).$$

Since $\eta$ lies in the image of $\tau$, the fiber is nonempty; no inverse of $\tau$ is
chosen.

articles.title: Characterization of maximum likelihood estimators
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a normalized density
family on $\Omega$ with parameter set $\Theta$, let $n$ be a sample size, let $L_n(\theta; x)$
denote the iid likelihood of $\theta \in \Theta$ at a sample $x \in \Omega^n$, and let
$\hat\theta$ be a map from $\Omega^n$ to $\Theta$. Then $\hat\theta$ is a maximum likelihood
estimator for samples of size $n$ if and only if $L_n(\theta; x) \le L_n(\hat\theta(x); x)$
for every sample $x \in \Omega^n$ and every $\theta \in \Theta$.

articles.title: Maximum likelihood estimator
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a normalized density family on $\Omega$ with
parameter set $\Theta$, let $n$ be a sample size, and let $L_n(\theta; x)$ denote the iid
likelihood of $\theta \in \Theta$ at a sample $x \in \Omega^n$. A map $\hat\theta$ from
$\Omega^n$ to $\Theta$ is a maximum likelihood estimator for samples of size $n$ if for every
sample $x \in \Omega^n$ the parameter $\hat\theta(x)$ maximizes $\theta \mapsto L_n(\theta; x)$
over all of $\Theta$.

articles.title: Population laws are probability measures
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a normalized density family on
$\Omega$ with parameter set $\Theta$, dominating measure $\mu$ and densities $f_\theta$. For
every $\theta \in \Theta$, the population law $P_\theta$, the measure with density $f_\theta$
with respect to $\mu$, is a probability measure.

articles.title: Population law
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a normalized density family on a measurable space $\Omega$
with parameter set $\Theta$, dominating measure $\mu$ and densities $f_\theta$. The population
law at $\theta \in \Theta$ is the measure $P_\theta$ on $\Omega$ with density $f_\theta$ with
respect to $\mu$, so that $P_\theta(A) = \int_A f_\theta \, d\mu$ for every measurable set
$A \subseteq \Omega$.

articles.title: Normalized density family
articles.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a measurable space with a measure $\mu$ and
let $\Theta$ be a set of parameters. A normalized density family on $\Omega$ indexed by $\Theta$
with dominating measure $\mu$ consists of a function $f_\theta : \Omega \to [0, \infty]$ for
each $\theta \in \Theta$ such that $f_\theta$ is $\mu$-almost everywhere measurable and
$\int_\Omega f_\theta \, d\mu = 1$.

Taking $\mu$ to be counting measure gives probability mass functions, and taking $\mu$ to be
volume gives probability density functions. The densities may take the value $\infty$.

articles.title: Integrability of a convex loss of a conditional expectation
articles.statement: For a convex loss `L`, `L ∘ μ[W | m]` is integrable whenever `W` and `L ∘ W` are.

articles.title: Rao–Blackwell inequality for one law
articles.statement:
For a convex loss `L` and an integrable `W` with
integrable loss, `∫ L(μ[W | m]) dμ ≤ ∫ L(W) dμ`.

articles.title: Equality case under squared error
articles.statement:
Conditioning leaves the squared-error risk at `c`
unchanged if and only if `W` already equals `μ[W | m]` almost everywhere.

articles.title: Squared-error decomposition
articles.statement:
For `W` with a finite second moment and any target `c`,
`E (W - c)² = E (μ[W | m] - c)² + E (W - μ[W | m])²`. This is the Pythagorean identity
`MeasureTheory.integral_sq_sub_eq_integral_sq_sub_condExp_add` with the constant predictor
`fun _ => c`, with the two summands commuted; it is not a second Pythagorean proof.

articles.title: The Rao–Blackwell theorem for a sufficient statistic
articles.statement:
If the statistic `T` is
sufficient for `P` and `W` is a measurable estimator with finite second moment under every
`P θ`, there is a measurable `φ` such that `φ ∘ T` is a version of every `E_θ[W | T]`, has the
same mean as `W`, and for every target `τ θ` satisfies
`E_θ (W - τ θ)² = E_θ (φ(T) - τ θ)² + E_θ (W - φ(T))²`.

articles.title: The Rao–Blackwell theorem
articles.statement:
Let `m` be sufficient for the family of probability measures
`P`, and let `W` be a measurable estimator that is integrable under every `P θ`. There is one
parameter-free `m`-measurable estimator `η`, a version of `P_θ[W | m]` for every `θ`, with
the same mean as `W` under every `θ` and no larger risk under every loss `ℓ θ` that is convex
in the estimate (for which `ℓ θ ∘ W` is integrable).

## Sources

- Rao (1945); Blackwell (1947); Casella–Berger, Section 7.3.

articles.title: James–Stein
articles.statement:
**James–Stein** (1961): for `p ≥ 3` and `X ~ N(θ, I_p)`, `‖X‖⁻²` is integrable and the risk
of the James–Stein estimator is `p - (p - 2)² E[‖X‖⁻²]`.

articles.title: Stein's lemma
articles.statement:
For `X ~ N(μ, v)` and an everywhere differentiable `g` with integrable
derivative, `(X - μ) g(X)` is integrable and `E[(X - μ) g(X)] = v E[g'(X)]`. For `v = 0` both
sides vanish.

articles.title: James–Stein dominance
articles.statement:
**James–Stein dominance** (Stein 1956, James–Stein 1961): for `p ≥ 3`, the James–Stein
estimator has strictly smaller quadratic risk than `X` at every mean `θ`.

articles.title: Stein's lemma
articles.statement:
**Stein's lemma**, coordinate form: for `X ~ N(θ, I_p)` and a function `h` whose slices
along the `i`-th axis are differentiable everywhere (for almost every base point) with
integrable partial derivative `dh`, `E[(Xᵢ - θᵢ) h(X)] = E[dh(X)]` whenever `(Xᵢ - θᵢ) h(X)` is
integrable. Unlike the one-dimensional case, this integrability does not follow from that of
`dh`: `h(x) = exp(x₁²)` has `∂₀ h = 0` but `x₀ h(x)` is not integrable.

articles.title: Stein's unbiased risk estimate
articles.statement:
For `X ~ N(θ, I_p)` and an estimator `X + g(X)` whose
coordinates `gᵢ` are square integrable and satisfy the hypotheses of Stein's lemma in the `i`-th
coordinate with partial derivative `dgᵢ`, the quadratic risk is
`p + E[∑ gᵢ(X)² + 2 ∑ dgᵢ(X)]`.

articles.title: Quadratic risk of the usual Gaussian mean estimator
articles.statement: The quadratic risk of the usual estimator `X` of the mean of `N(θ, I_p)` is `p`.

articles.title: James–Stein estimator
articles.statement:
The James–Stein estimator `δ(x) = (1 - (p - 2) / ‖x‖²) x` of the mean of `N(θ, I_p)`. At
`x = 0` the factor is `1` by Lean's `a / 0 = 0` convention, so `δ(0) = 0`.

articles.title: Common conditional expectation under a sufficient σ-algebra
articles.statement:
If `m` is sufficient for a family of probability measures, every `m₀`-measurable real
function `W` that is integrable under all the measures has one `m`-measurable version of the
conditional expectation `P_θ[W | m]` for every `θ`. (Measurability of `W` itself, not only
under each `P θ`, is what lets one approximating sequence serve every parameter.)

articles.title: Halmos–Savage factorization, necessity
articles.statement:
If the family of probability measures `P` is
dominated by a σ-finite measure `μ` and the statistic `T` is sufficient for `P`, then the
densities factor as `dP_θ/dμ = g_θ(T) · h` with measurable `g_θ` and `h`, `h` free of `θ`.

## Sources

- P. R. Halmos and L. J. Savage, *Application of the Radon–Nikodym theorem to the theory of sufficient statistics*, Ann. Math. Statist. 20 (1949), 225–241.

articles.title: Factorization, necessity
articles.statement:
If `T` is sufficient for `P`, then
`P θ x = g θ (T x) * h x` with `g θ t = P_θ(T = t)` and a parameter-free `h` with values in
`[0, 1]`.

articles.title: Factorization criterion, sufficiency direction, for a statistic, under an extra σ-finiteness hypothesis
articles.statement:
**Factorization criterion, sufficiency direction, for a statistic, under an extra
σ-finiteness hypothesis.** If `dP_θ/dμ = g_θ(T) · h` with `g_θ` and `h` measurable and
`h · μ` σ-finite on the σ-algebra generated by `T`, then `T` is sufficient for `P`.

The σ-finiteness hypothesis on `(μ.withDensity h).trim (comap T)` is an extra,
nonstandard assumption, named in the theorem: it is strictly stronger than `μ` being
σ-finite, since restriction to a sub-σ-algebra need not preserve σ-finiteness, and it
can fail even when `μ` is σ-finite and `h` is a density. This theorem is therefore the
factorization criterion under that extra hypothesis, not the classical criterion as
stated. Removing the hypothesis would require a different proof.

## Sources

- Halmos and Savage (1949); Lehmann–Romano, Chapter 2.

articles.title: Factorization implies sufficiency
articles.statement:
**Factorization implies sufficiency** (Halmos–Savage, the sufficiency half). If every
`P θ` has a density `g θ` with respect to one measure `ν` that is σ-finite on `m`, and each
`g θ` is `m`-measurable, then `m` is sufficient for `P`.

articles.title: The Fisher–Neyman factorization theorem
articles.statement:
**The Fisher–Neyman factorization theorem** (discrete case). A statistic `T` is sufficient
for the family of mass functions `P` if and only if there are nonnegative functions `g` and
`h`, with `h` free of the parameter, such that `P θ x = g θ (T x) * h x` for every `θ`, `x`.

## Sources

- Neyman (1935); Casella–Berger, Theorem 6.2.6.

articles.title: Factorization, sufficiency
articles.statement:
If `P θ x = g θ (T x) * h x` for nonnegative real `g`, `h`
with `h` free of `θ`, then `T` is sufficient for `P`.

articles.title: Sufficient statistic for a discrete family
articles.statement:
A statistic `T : X → τ` is *sufficient* for the discrete family `P : Θ → PMF X` if the
conditional probability `P θ x / P_θ(T = T x)` of `x` given `T = T x` is the same under any
two parameters `θ, θ'` for which `{T = T x}` has positive probability. Here
`P_θ(T = t) = (P θ).map T t`.

articles.title: Sufficient sub-σ-algebra
articles.statement:
A sub-σ-algebra `m` is *sufficient* for the family of measures `P` on `(Ω, m₀)` if
`m ≤ m₀`, every `P θ` is finite, and for every `m₀`-measurable set `s` one `m`-measurable
function is a version of the conditional probability `P_θ[1_s | m]` under every `P θ`.
Bundling `m ≤ m₀` and finiteness into the predicate means an `IsSufficient` hypothesis
itself represents a sufficient sub-σ-algebra for statistical laws: the conditional
expectations it mentions are genuine, not Mathlib's totalized fallback on unrelated
σ-algebras or infinite measures.

articles.title: Germ sigma-algebra lies in every positive-time level
articles.statement:
The germ σ-algebra is contained in every positive-time component of the
filtration.

articles.title: Germ sigma-algebra at time zero
articles.statement:
The *germ σ-algebra at `0`* of a filtration `𝓕` indexed by `NNReal`,
defined as the intersection `⨅_{t > 0} 𝓕_t`. For Brownian motion this is the
`𝓕_0^+` σ-algebra of events observable "immediately after" time `0`. Ported
verbatim from `v1/Atlas/TheoryOfProbability/code/Blumenthal01.lean`.

articles.title: Continuous process with independent increments
articles.statement:
A continuous process `B : NNReal → Ω → E` with independent increments,
started at `x` and adapted to `𝓕`. The measure is a probability measure,
`B 0 = x` a.e., each increment after `s` is independent of `𝓕 s`, and a.e.
paths are continuous. These are the five meaningful fields of the archived
v1 specification; its tautological pushforward-law field is omitted.
No Gaussian-law or stationary-increment condition is encoded.

articles.title: Process is measurable for its natural filtration at later times
articles.statement:
Each `B u` is measurable with respect to the natural filtration at any
later time `t`.

articles.title: Coordinates of a continuous independent-increment process are measurable
articles.statement: Each coordinate of the adapted continuous process is measurable.

articles.title: Natural filtration is the smallest adapted filtration
articles.statement:
The natural filtration is contained in any filtration to which `B` is
adapted.

articles.title: Natural filtration of a process
articles.statement:
The natural filtration of a process: `𝓕^nat_t = σ(B_u : u ≤ t)`. Unlike
Mathlib's `Filtration.natural`, this is built from measurability rather than
strong measurability, which is all that is available from adaptedness.

articles.title: Germ sigma-algebra of the natural filtration
articles.statement: The germ σ-algebra of the natural filtration of `B`.

articles.title: Blumenthal zero-one law
articles.statement:
Every event in the natural germ of a continuous process with independent
increments and a deterministic a.e. initial value has probability `0` or `1`.
This general form includes the classical Brownian natural-filtration law.

articles.title: Free-energy decay
articles.statement:
Under the hypotheses of `hasDerivAt_freeEnergy`, on a convex open
time set `I` the free energy is nonincreasing.

articles.title: Rotational drifts share the Gibbs stationary density
articles.statement:
**Rotational drifts share the Gibbs stationary density** (non-identifiability): for a
`C²` potential `Ψ`, `D ≠ 0` and an antisymmetric matrix `A` (`Aᵀ = -A`), the drift
`-(∇Ψ + A ∇Ψ)` satisfies `div J = 0` for `p = e^{-Ψ / D}`.

articles.title: Divergence of a vector field
articles.statement: The divergence `div F (x) = ∑ᵢ ∂ᵢ Fᵢ (x)` of a vector field.

articles.title: Identifiability of the potential
articles.statement:
Two differentiable potentials whose gradient drifts
both have zero flux for the same positive differentiable density differ by a constant.

articles.title: An explicit rotational drift with nonzero flux
articles.statement:
**An explicit rotational drift with nonzero flux** (our derivation): on `ℝ²` with
`Ψ(x) = (x₀² + x₁²) / 2`, `D = 1` and the rotation generator `A = [[0, 1], [-1, 0]]`, the
drift `-(∇Ψ + A ∇Ψ)` has the Gibbs (standard Gaussian, up to normalization) density as a
stationary density, yet its flux at `(1, 0)` is nonzero, so it is not the gradient drift.

articles.title: The Gibbs density has zero flux
articles.statement:
**The Gibbs density has zero flux** under the gradient drift `-∇Ψ`: for differentiable `Ψ`,
`D ≠ 0` and any constant `c`, `J = -∇Ψ · c e^{-Ψ/D} - D ∇(c e^{-Ψ/D}) = 0`.

articles.title: Flux of the Gibbs density under a rotational gradient drift
articles.statement:
The flux of the Gibbs density under the drift `-(∇Ψ + A ∇Ψ)` is the rotational part
`-(A ∇Ψ) e^{-Ψ / D}` (for differentiable `Ψ`, `D ≠ 0`, any matrix `A`).

articles.title: Probability flux of a diffusion
articles.statement:
The **probability flux** `J = b p - D ∇p` of the diffusion `dX = b dt + √(2D) dW` with
density `p`.

articles.title: The Gibbs density is stationary
articles.statement: **The Gibbs density is stationary** for the gradient drift: `-div J = 0`.

articles.title: Fokker–Planck operator
articles.statement:
The **Fokker–Planck operator** `-div J`: the density evolves by `∂ₜ p = fokkerPlanckOp D b p`,
and `p` is stationary iff this vanishes.

articles.title: Free energy of a Fokker–Planck density
articles.statement:
The **free energy** `F(t) = ∫ₐᵇ (Ψ p + D p log p) dx` of the density `p(t, ·)` on
`[a, b]` (potential `Ψ`, diffusion coefficient `D`).

articles.title: Gibbs density
articles.statement: The (unnormalized) **Gibbs density** `e^{-Ψ(x) / D}`.

articles.title: Gradient of a function on Euclidean coordinate space
articles.statement: The gradient `∇f(x) = (∂ᵢ f(x))ᵢ`.

articles.title: Dissipation identity
articles.statement:
Let `p` be `C²` in `(t, x)`, positive for times in an open set
`I`, and solve the no-flux gradient-drift Fokker–Planck equation on `[a, b]` for `t ∈ I`, with
`C²` potential `Ψ` (any real `D`). Then for `t ∈ I`,
`F'(t) = -∫ₐᵇ p (Ψ' + D ∂ₓ log p)² dx`. Only the values of `p` on `[a, b]` enter `F`;
positivity is asked of the whole `C²` function `p t` so that `log (p t)` is `C²`.

articles.title: Mass conservation
articles.statement:
If `p` is `C²` and solves the no-flux equation on `[a, b]` for times
in `I` (positivity is not needed), the total mass `∫ₐᵇ p(t, x) dx` has zero time derivative at
every `t ∈ I`.

articles.title: No-flux solution of the gradient-drift Fokker–Planck equation
articles.statement:
`p` solves the **gradient-drift Fokker–Planck equation** `∂ₜ p = ∂ₓ (p Ψ' + D ∂ₓ p)` on
`[a, b]` with **zero flux** at both ends, for times `t ∈ I`.

articles.title: Negative probability flux of the Fokker–Planck equation
articles.statement:
The (negative) probability flux `p Ψ' + D ∂ₓ p` of the gradient-drift Fokker–Planck
equation at `(t, x)`; the flux itself is `-(p Ψ' + D ∂ₓ p)`.

articles.title: A zero-flux density determines the drift
articles.statement:
If `p > 0` is differentiable and the
gradient drift `-∇Ψ` has zero flux for `p`, then `∂ᵢ Ψ = -D ∂ᵢ log p`.

articles.title: Partial derivative on Euclidean coordinate space
articles.statement: The partial derivative `∂ᵢ f (x) = Df(x) eᵢ` on `Fin n → ℝ`.

articles.title: Uniform bound on an elementary integrand
articles.statement: An elementary integrand with `n` intervals is bounded by `n * bound`.

articles.title: Lebesgue differentiation along shrinking off-center intervals
articles.statement:
For a locally integrable
`f : ℝ → ℝ`, for almost every `u`, the averages of `f` over intervals `[a n, b n]` converge to
`f u` whenever the lengths `b n - a n > 0` tend to `0` and the distance from `u` to the midpoint
of `[a n, b n]` is at most twice the length.

articles.title: The Itô form of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck solution
articles.statement:
For a Brownian motion `B`, almost surely,
for every `t ≥ 0` and every initial value `X₀`, the Itô–Riemann sums
`e^{-θt} X₀ + σ e^{-θt} ∑_{k < n} e^{θ t k / n} (B (t (k + 1) / n) - B (t k / n))` of
`e^{-θt} X₀ + σ ∫_0^t e^{-θ(t-s)} dB_s` converge to the pathwise solution `ouPathSolution`
(any real `θ`, `σ`).

articles.title: Measurability of the $L^2$ Itô integral
articles.statement: The `L²` Itô integral is (almost surely equal to) an `F t`-measurable function.

articles.title: Locality of approximability
articles.statement:
Itô-approximability on `[0, t]` only depends on the
integrand at times in `(0, t]`.

articles.title: Delayed-average approximation of a progressive process
articles.statement:
The **delayed-average approximation** of a progressive process `H` on `[0, t]`, truncated at
level `M`, with `n + 1` intervals: on `(t_k, t_{k+1}]`, with `t_k = k t / (n + 1)`, it equals the
average of `truncation (H ·) M` over `[t_{k-1}, t_k]` for `k ≥ 1`, and `0` for `k = 0`. For
`M ≤ 0` the truncation, and hence the approximation, is `0`.

articles.title: Partition intervals of an elementary integrand are disjoint
articles.statement: The partition intervals of an elementary integrand are pairwise disjoint.

articles.title: Elementary integrand
articles.statement:
An **elementary integrand** for a filtration `F` indexed by `ℝ≥0`: partition times
`time 0 ≤ ⋯ ≤ time n` and coefficients `coeff i`, bounded by `bound` and measurable with respect
to `F (time i)`, representing the process `∑ i, coeff i 1_{(time i, time (i + 1)]}`. Equal
consecutive times are allowed (the corresponding interval is empty).

articles.title: Polarized Itô isometry
articles.statement:
**Polarized Itô isometry** for elementary integrands: for a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted
to `F` whose increments `B t - B s` are independent of `F s`, and two elementary integrands
`H`, `K` (with possibly different partitions),
`E[(∫_0^t H dB) (∫_0^t K dB)] = E ∫_0^t H_u K_u du`.

articles.title: Itô isometry, discrete form
articles.statement:
For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` whose
increments `B t - B s` are independent of `F s`,
`E[(∫_0^t H dB)²] = ∑ i, E[ξ_i²] (t_{i+1} ∧ t - t_i ∧ t)`.

articles.title: Itô isometry
articles.statement:
**Itô isometry** for elementary integrands: for a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F`
whose increments `B t - B s` are independent of `F s`,
`E[(∫_0^t H dB)²] = E ∫_0^t H_u² du` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 3.2.A).

articles.title: Second moment of a Brownian increment
articles.statement: The second moment of a Brownian increment: `E[(B v - B r)²] = v - r` for `r ≤ v`.

articles.title: Time integral of a squared elementary integrand
articles.statement:
The time integral of the squared elementary integrand, path by path:
`∫_0^t H_u² du = ∑ i, ξ_i² (t_{i+1} ∧ t - t_i ∧ t)`.

articles.title: Itô isometry for Itô-approximable integrands
articles.statement:
The squared `L²(P ⊗ du)` distance between two Itô-approximable integrands is the squared
`L²(P)` distance between their Itô integrals.

articles.title: Itô isometry for elementary integrands
articles.statement:
`integrandDist` of two elementary integrands is the squared `L²(P)` distance of their Itô
integrals.

articles.title: Integrand distance as a squared $L^2$ seminorm
articles.statement:
The integrand distance on `(0, t]` is the square of the `L²` seminorm on
`Ω × (0, t]`.

articles.title: Quasi-triangle inequality for the integrand distance
articles.statement:
Pointwise `|x - y|² ≤ 2 |x - z|² + 2 |y - z|²`, integrated: a quasi-triangle inequality
for `integrandDist` between jointly measurable processes.

articles.title: Finite distance between elementary integrands
articles.statement: The `L²(P ⊗ du)` distance between two elementary integrands is finite.

articles.title: Integrand distance depends only on times in (0, t)
articles.statement: `integrandDist P X Y t` only depends on `X` and `Y` at times in `(0, t]`.

articles.title: Squared $L^2$ distance between integrands
articles.statement:
The squared `L²(P ⊗ du)` distance on `(0, t] × Ω` between two processes, in `ℝ≥0∞`:
`∫⁻ ω, ∫⁻ u in (0, t], |H u ω - K u ω|² du dP`.

articles.title: Density of elementary integrands
articles.statement:
A progressive integrand `H` with
`E ∫_0^t H_u² du < ∞` is the `L²(P ⊗ du)`-limit on `(0, t] × Ω` of elementary integrands
(Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Lemma 3.2.4 and Proposition 3.2.6).

articles.title: Elementary integrands are Itô-approximable
articles.statement: An elementary integrand is Itô-approximable on every `[0, t]` (by itself).

articles.title: Itô-approximable process
articles.statement:
A process `H` is **Itô-approximable on `[0, t]`** for the filtration `F` if it is jointly
measurable on `(0, t] × Ω` and is the `L²(P ⊗ du)`-limit on `(0, t] × Ω` of elementary
integrands. Neither condition involves the values of `H` at time `0` or after `t`.

articles.title: Itô integral process
articles.statement:
The **Itô integral** `t ↦ ∫_0^t H dB` as a real process: an `F t`-strongly measurable
version of `itoIntegralL2 P F B H t` when one exists (which is the case under the hypotheses of
the theorems below), and a representative of `itoIntegralL2 P F B H t` otherwise.

articles.title: Linearity (additivity)
articles.statement:
The Itô integral is additive in the integrand: for
`F`-progressive integrands `H₁, H₂` with `E ∫_0^t H_i² du < ∞`, the integral of the sum is almost
surely the sum of the integrals. Together with homogeneity and the difference isometry this pins
down the integral on the whole `L²` space of progressive integrands. Only the pre-Brownian
finite-dimensional laws are used; path continuity is not required.

articles.title: Linearity (additivity)
articles.statement:
The Itô integral is additive in the integrand: for
`F`-progressive integrands `H₁, H₂` with `E ∫_0^t H_i² du < ∞`, the integral of the sum is almost
surely the sum of the integrals. Together with homogeneity and the difference isometry this pins
down the integral on the whole `L²` space of progressive integrands.

articles.title: Itô integral process is a version of the $L^2$ integral
articles.statement: The Itô integral process is almost surely equal to `itoIntegralL2` at each time.

articles.title: Continuous modification
articles.statement:
The Itô integral admits a modification with continuous paths:
there is a process `J` with continuous paths such that `J t = ∫_0^t H dB` almost surely for each
`t` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 3.2). `ProbabilityTheory.itoIntegral` chooses its version
separately at each time, so it is only determined up to a null set that may depend on `t`; the
statement therefore asks for a modification rather than for a process indistinguishable from
this particular choice. Any two continuous modifications are indistinguishable.

articles.title: Wiener's integration by parts
articles.statement:
For a Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with
increments independent of the past and a deterministic `C¹` integrand `g`, the Itô integral is
`∫_0^t g dB = g t B t - g 0 B 0 - ∫_0^t g'(u) B u du` almost surely (Karatzas–Shreve 1991,
Section 3.3; the right side is a pathwise Riemann integral).

articles.title: Elementary integrands
articles.statement:
For `a ≤ b` and a bounded `F a`-measurable `ξ`, the Itô integral
of `ξ 1_{(a, b]}` against a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with increments independent
of the past is `ξ (B (b ∧ t) - B (a ∧ t))` almost surely (Karatzas–Shreve 1991,
Section 3.2.A).

articles.title: Difference isometry
articles.statement:
For two `F`-progressive integrands with `E ∫_0^t H_i² du < ∞`, the
difference of the integrals is square-integrable and
`E[(∫ H₁ dB - ∫ H₂ dB)²] = E ∫ (H₁ - H₂)² du`. With linearity this is the two-integrand isometry
that, together with the elementary-integrand formula, determines the construction on the whole
`L²` space. Only the pre-Brownian finite-dimensional laws are used; path continuity is not
required.

articles.title: Difference isometry
articles.statement:
For two `F`-progressive integrands with `E ∫_0^t H_i² du < ∞`, the
difference of the integrals is square-integrable and
`E[(∫ H₁ dB - ∫ H₂ dB)²] = E ∫ (H₁ - H₂)² du`. With linearity this is the two-integrand isometry
that, together with the elementary-integrand formula, determines the construction on the whole
`L²` space.

articles.title: Locality of the Itô integral
articles.statement:
The Itô integral at time `t` only depends on the integrand
at times in `(0, t]`.

articles.title: Itô integral as an element of $L^2$
articles.statement:
The **Itô integral** `∫_0^t H dB` as an element of `L²(P)`: the `L²` limit of the elementary
Itô integrals of an approximating sequence of elementary integrands when `H` is Itô-approximable
on `[0, t]`, and `0` otherwise.

articles.title: Itô integral of a Riemann step approximation
articles.statement:
The elementary Itô integral of `riemann F g t n` at time `t` is the Itô–Riemann sum
`∑_{k < n} g (t k / n) (B (t (k + 1) / n) - B (t k / n))`.

articles.title: Elementary integrands
articles.statement:
The Itô integral of `ξ 1_{(a, b]}` is
`ξ (B (b ∧ t) - B (a ∧ t))` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 3.2.A); this holds for every
process `B` and every `ω`, by definition.

articles.title: Linearity (homogeneity)
articles.statement:
The Itô integral is homogeneous in the integrand for a
pre-Brownian integrator; path continuity is not required.

articles.title: Linearity (homogeneity)
articles.statement: The Itô integral is homogeneous in the integrand.

articles.title: Itô integral agrees with the elementary integral on elementary integrands
articles.statement:
On an elementary integrand, the Itô integral agrees almost surely with the elementary Itô
integral.

articles.title: Elementary Itô integral vanishes at time zero
articles.statement: The elementary Itô integral vanishes at time `0`.

articles.title: Itô integral of an elementary integrand
articles.statement:
The **Itô integral** of an elementary integrand against a process `B`:
`t ↦ ∑ i, coeff i (B (time (i + 1) ∧ t) - B (time i ∧ t))`.

articles.title: The Ornstein–Uhlenbeck solution in Itô form
articles.statement:
For a Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F`
with increments independent of the past, any initial value `X₀` and any real `θ`, `σ`, the Itô
form `e^{-θt} X₀ + σ e^{-θt} ∫_0^t e^{θs} dB_s = e^{-θt} X₀ + σ ∫_0^t e^{-θ(t-s)} dB_s` of the
solution of `dX = -θ X dt + σ dB` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 5.6) agrees almost surely with
the pathwise solution `ouPathSolution`, which solves `X t = X₀ - θ ∫_0^t X + σ (B t - B 0)` path
by path (`ProbabilityTheory.ouPathSolution_integral_eq`).

articles.title: Itô isometry for progressive integrands
articles.statement:
For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F`
with increments independent of the past and an `F`-progressive integrand `H` with
`E ∫_0^t H_u² du < ∞`, `E[(∫_0^t H dB)²] = E ∫_0^t H_u² du` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991,
Section 3.2).

articles.title: Itô isometry
articles.statement:
**Itô isometry** for the `L²` Itô integral, in `ℝ≥0∞` form: for a pre-Brownian motion `B`
adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past and an integrand `H` that is
Itô-approximable on `[0, t]`, `E[(∫_0^t H dB)²] = E ∫_0^t H_u² du` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991,
Section 3.2).

articles.title: Martingale property of the Itô integral
articles.statement:
For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F`
with increments independent of the past and an integrand `H` that is Itô-approximable on every
`[0, t]`, the Itô integral `t ↦ ∫_0^t H dB` is an `F`-martingale (Karatzas–Shreve 1991,
Proposition 3.2.10).

articles.title: Martingale property for progressive integrands
articles.statement:
For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted
to `F` with increments independent of the past and an `F`-progressive integrand `H` with
`E ∫_0^t H_u² du < ∞` for every `t`, the Itô integral `t ↦ ∫_0^t H dB` is an `F`-martingale
(Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Proposition 3.2.10).

articles.title: Martingale property
articles.statement:
For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` whose increments
`B t - B s` are independent of `F s`, the elementary Itô integral `t ↦ ∫_0^t H dB` is an
`F`-martingale.

articles.title: Measurability of time averages of a progressive process
articles.statement:
For a progressive `H` and `b ≤ T`, the average of `u ↦ H u ω` over `[a, b]` is
`F T`-measurable in `ω`.

articles.title: Restriction to (0, t) preserves joint measurability
articles.statement:
Restricting a jointly measurable process to the times `(0, t]` keeps it jointly
measurable.

articles.title: Progressive processes are jointly measurable
articles.statement:
A progressive process is jointly measurable in `(u, ω)` (reading `u : ℝ` through
`Real.toNNReal`).

articles.title: Elementary integrands are jointly measurable
articles.statement:
An elementary integrand is jointly measurable in `(u, ω)` (reading `u : ℝ` through
`Real.toNNReal`).

articles.title: Square integrability of the elementary Itô integral
articles.statement: The elementary Itô integral against a pre-Brownian motion is square integrable.

articles.title: Square integrability of the Itô integral
articles.statement:
The Itô integral at each time is square integrable: it is a version of the element
`itoIntegralL2 P F B H t` of `L²(P)` (which is `0` when `H` is not Itô-approximable).

articles.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck path solution by integration by parts
articles.statement:
The pathwise Ornstein–Uhlenbeck solution in integration-by-parts form: with `g u = e^{θu}`,
`ouPathSolution θ σ x₀ w t = e^{-θt} x₀ + σ e^{-θt} (g t w t - g 0 w 0 - ∫_0^t g'(u) w u du)`,
for any path `w` and any real `θ`, `σ`, `x₀`, `t`.

articles.title: Restriction of a process to the time interval (0, t)
articles.statement:
The process `H` with its values at times outside `(0, t]` set to `0`. Only the values at
times in `(0, t]` enter the Itô integral at time `t`.

articles.title: Left-point step approximation of a deterministic integrand
articles.statement:
The left-point step approximation `∑_{k < n} g (t k / n) 1_{(t k / n, t (k + 1) / n]}` of a
deterministic `g` on the uniform partition of `[0, t]` into `n` cells, as an
elementary integrand for any filtration `F` (deterministic coefficients are measurable for every
σ-algebra).

articles.title: Single-step elementary integrand
articles.statement:
The elementary integrand `ξ 1_{(a, b]}` for `a ≤ b` and an `F a`-measurable `ξ` bounded by
`C`.

articles.title: Convergence of the delayed averages
articles.statement:
For a progressive `H` and a finite measure `P`, the
delayed-average approximations of the truncation of `H` at level `M` converge to it in
`L²(P ⊗ du)` on `(0, t] × Ω` as the mesh `t / (n + 1)` tends to `0` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, proof of
Lemma 3.2.4(b)).

articles.title: $L^2$ convergence of left-point approximations of a continuous function
articles.statement:
The left-point approximations of a continuous deterministic `g` converge to `g` in
`L²(P ⊗ du)` on `(0, t] × Ω`.

articles.title: Truncation
articles.statement:
For a jointly measurable `H` with `E ∫_0^t H_u² du < ∞`, the truncations of
`H` at levels `M → ∞` converge to `H` in `L²(P ⊗ du)` on `(0, t] × Ω`
(Karatzas–Shreve 1991, proof of Lemma 3.2.4(c)).

articles.title: Itô–Riemann sums of a deterministic `C¹` integrand
articles.statement:
Along every continuous path of `B`,
the elementary Itô integrals at time `t` of the left-point approximations of `g` converge to
Wiener's integration-by-parts expression `g t B t - g 0 B 0 - ∫_0^t g'(u) B u du`.

articles.title: Riemann–Stieltjes integration by parts, uniform partitions
articles.statement:
For a `C¹` function `g`, a
continuous path `w` and `t ≥ 0`, the left-point sums
`∑_{k < n} g (t k / n) (w (t (k + 1) / n) - w (t k / n))` converge, as `n → ∞`, to
`g t w t - g 0 w 0 - ∫_0^t g' w`.

articles.title: The Itô integral is well defined
articles.statement:
For a pre-Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with
increments independent of the past, an `H` jointly measurable on `(0, t] × Ω`, and *any*
sequence of elementary integrands `Kn` converging to `H` in `L²(P ⊗ du)` on `(0, t] × Ω`, the
elementary Itô integrals of `Kn` converge in `L²(P)` to `itoIntegralL2 P F B H t`.

articles.title: Function as an element of $L^2$
articles.statement: A function as an element of `L²(P)`, or `0` if it is not square integrable.

articles.title: Elementary integrand on a partition interval
articles.statement: On its `i`-th interval, an elementary integrand equals its `i`-th coefficient.

articles.title: Process of a single-step elementary integrand
articles.statement: The process of `single a b hab ξ hξ C hξC` is `u ↦ ξ 1_{(a, b]}(u)`.

articles.title: Elementary integrand as a process
articles.statement: The elementary integrand as a process: `u ↦ ∑ i, coeff i 1_{(time i, time (i + 1)]}(u)`.

articles.title: Truncation of a progressive process is progressive
articles.statement:
Truncating a progressive process at level `M` (Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.truncation`,
which keeps the values in `(-M, M]` and sets the others to `0`) gives a progressive process.

articles.title: Itô's formula
articles.statement:
**Itô's formula** for Brownian motion: for a Brownian motion `B` adapted to `F` with
increments independent of the past and jointly measurable in `(t, ω)`, and `f` of class `C²`
with `|f'| ≤ C` and `|f''| ≤ C`,
`f(B t) = f(B 0) + ∫_0^t f'(B u) dB u + (1/2) ∫_0^t f''(B u) du` almost surely, for every
`t ≥ 0` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Theorem 3.3.3). The last integral is a pathwise Riemann integral;
it is the integral of a continuous function on almost every path.

articles.title: Itô integral of the left-point integrand is the left-point sum
articles.statement:
The elementary Itô integral of `leftPoint` at time `t` is the left-point Itô sum
`∑_{k < n} g(B (t k / n)) (B (t (k + 1) / n) - B (t k / n))`.

articles.title: Left-point step process along a Brownian path
articles.statement:
The left-point step process `∑_{k < n} g(B (t k / n)) 1_{(t k / n, t (k + 1) / n]}` of
`u ↦ g (B u)` on the uniform partition of `[0, t]` into `n` cells.

articles.title: Left-point elementary integrand along a Brownian path
articles.statement:
The left-point elementary integrand `∑_{k < n} g(B (t k / n)) 1_{(t k / n, t (k + 1) / n]}`
of `u ↦ g (B u)` on the uniform partition of `[0, t]`, for a measurable `g` bounded by `C` and
an adapted `B`.

articles.title: Left-point approximation of a Lipschitz function of Brownian motion
articles.statement:
For a pre-Brownian
motion `B` that is jointly measurable in `(u, ω)` and an `L`-Lipschitz `g`, the left-point step
processes of `u ↦ g (B u)` converge to it in `L²(P ⊗ du)` on `(0, t] × Ω`:
`E ∫_0^t |leftPointProcess g B t n u - g (B u)|² du → 0`.

articles.title: Left-point Riemann sums of a continuous function
articles.statement:
**Left-point Riemann sums of a continuous function** on the uniform partition of `[0, t]`
converge to the integral: `∑_{k < n} g (t k / n) (t / n) → ∫_0^t g` (`t ≥ 0`).

articles.title: Second-order Taylor sums along a continuous path
articles.statement:
For `f` of class `C²`, a continuous
path `w`, `t ≥ 0`, and a sequence of mesh counts `ns j → ∞` along which the quadratic sums
`∑_{k < ns j} (w (t (k + 1) / ns j) - w (t k / ns j))²` stay bounded, the telescoped increment
`f (w t) - f (w 0)` minus the second-order Taylor sums
`∑_k (f'(w_k) Δw_k + (1/2) f''(w_k) Δw_k²)` tends to `0`.

articles.title: Process of the left-point integrand is the left-point step process
articles.statement: The process of `leftPoint` is `leftPointProcess`.

articles.title: Deterministic chaining
articles.statement:
If every adjacent dyadic increment at level
`m` is at most `D * 2^{-mγ}`, then `f` is `γ`-Hölder on the dyadic
rationals of `[0, 1]`, with an explicit constant.

articles.title: Dyadic rationals
articles.statement:
The set of **dyadic rationals**: real numbers of the form `k / 2 ^ n`
for some integer `k` and natural number `n`.

articles.title: Kolmogorov continuous-modification theorem for real-valued processes
articles.statement:
A real-valued Kolmogorov process on `NNReal` whose time exponent is greater
than one has one modification with measurable coordinates and continuous paths
on every sample. The same modification agrees exactly at time zero and
preserves every closed set containing an original sample path. Fixed-time
almost-everywhere equality is asserted separately at each time; no
indistinguishability claim is made for the raw process.

articles.title: Hölder bound on dyadics for a Kolmogorov process
articles.statement:
The canonical Kolmogorov-process condition implies a common a.e. Hölder
bound for `X` on the dyadics of `[0, 1]`. Its measurable-pair and finite
lintegral fields supply the Bochner hypotheses internally, including when
`M = 0`. No claim is made about the raw paths at every real time.

articles.title: Almost sure Hölder bound on the dyadic rationals
articles.statement:
A single full-measure set carries a Hölder bound for the original process
on the dyadic rationals of `[0, 1]`. The moment-integrability correction in
the module docstring is required for this Bochner formulation.

articles.title: Kolmogorov continuity theorem
articles.statement:
**Kolmogorov continuity theorem**, in the original modification formulation.
The direct dyadic bound permits choosing `Y = X`. See the module docstring for
the necessary moment-integrability correction to the archived v1 statement.

articles.title: Adapted real process
articles.statement:
A real-valued process $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ on $\Omega$, indexed by
$t \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, is adapted to a filtration $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ when $B_t$ is
$\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable for every $t \ge 0$.

articles.title: Cylinder events of the centered shifted path
articles.statement:
Let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real-valued
process on $\Omega$ and let $s \ge 0$. The centered cylinders at time $s$ are the events
$\bigcap_{t \in S} \{\omega \in \Omega : B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega) \in C_t\}$, where
$S \subset \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is a finite set and each $C_t \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a
Borel set.

articles.title: Telescoping the centered shifted path over a finite set
articles.statement:
Let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a
real-valued process on $\Omega$, let $s \ge 0$, and let $S \subset \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be a
finite set. For $u \ge 0$ let $u^-$ be the largest element of $S$ strictly below $u$, or $0$
if there is none. Then for every $t \in S$ and every $\omega \in \Omega$,
$B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega) =
\sum_{u \in S : u \le t} (B_{s+u}(\omega) - B_{s+u^-}(\omega))$.

articles.title: Law of the centered shifted path
articles.statement:
Let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real-valued process on a
measure space $(\Omega, \mu)$ and let $s \ge 0$. This is the pushforward of $\mu$ under the map
sending $\omega \in \Omega$ to the path $t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega)$, a measure on
the space of functions $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}$ with its product σ-algebra.

articles.title: Centered shifted path
articles.statement:
Let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real-valued process on $\Omega$ and
let $s \ge 0$. The centered shifted path at time $s$ sends $\omega \in \Omega$ to the function
$t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega)$ on $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$.

articles.title: Rectangles of a Borel set and a path cylinder
articles.statement:
Write $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}}$
for the space of functions $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}$. These are the subsets of
$\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}}$ of the form
$U \times \{f : f(t) \in V_t \text{ for all } t \in S\}$, where $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a
Borel set, $S \subset \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is a finite set, and each $V_t \subseteq \mathbb{R}$
is a Borel set.

articles.title: Increment rectangles
articles.statement:
Let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real-valued process on $\Omega$, let
$s \ge 0$, and let $S \subset \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be a finite set. For $t \ge 0$ let $t^-$ be the
largest element of $S$ strictly below $t$, or $0$ if there is none. The increment rectangles
are the events
$\bigcap_{t \in S} \{\omega \in \Omega : B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_{s+t^-}(\omega) \in C_t\}$, where each
$C_t \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a Borel set.

articles.title: σ-algebra of the increments over a finite set
articles.statement:
Let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real-valued
process on $\Omega$, let $s \ge 0$, and let $S \subset \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be a finite set. For
$t \ge 0$ let $t^-$ be the largest element of $S$ strictly below $t$, or $0$ if there is none.
This is the σ-algebra on $\Omega$ generated by the increment rectangles, the events
$\bigcap_{t \in S} \{\omega \in \Omega : B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_{s+t^-}(\omega) \in C_t\}$ with each
$C_t \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ a Borel set.

articles.title: Increment over the predecessor interval
articles.statement:
Let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real-valued process
on $\Omega$, let $s \ge 0$, and let $S \subset \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be a finite set. For $t \ge 0$
let $t^-$ be the largest element of $S$ strictly below $t$, or $0$ if there is none. The
increment at $t$ is the random variable $\omega \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_{s+t^-}(\omega)$.

articles.title: Independent increments with respect to a filtration
articles.statement:
A real-valued process
$(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ on $\Omega$ has independent increments with respect to a filtration
$(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ and a measure $\mu$ when, for all $0 \le s \le t$, the σ-algebra
generated by $B_t - B_s$ is independent of $\mathcal{F}_s$ under $\mu$.

articles.title: The process value paired with its centered future path
articles.statement:
For a real process
$(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ on $\Omega$ indexed by $t \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and a time $s \ge 0$, this is
the map $\Omega \to \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}}$ sending $\omega$ to the pair
consisting of $B_s(\omega)$ and the path $t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega)$.

articles.title: Cylinder sets of path space
articles.statement:
The collection of sets of paths
$f : \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}$ of the form $\bigcap_{t \in S} \{f : f(t) \in C_t\}$,
where $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is a finite set and each $C_t$ is a measurable subset of
$\mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Bound on the path expectation
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let
$(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real process on $\Omega$ indexed by $t \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, let
$s \ge 0$, and let $\nu_s$ be the law under $\mu$ of the path
$\omega \mapsto (t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega))$. If $Y$ is a measurable real function
on paths $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $|Y(p)| \le C$ for every path $p$, then for
every $x \in \mathbb{R}$ the path expectation $E_s Y(x) = \int Y(t \mapsto x + f(t))\, d\nu_s(f)$
satisfies $|E_s Y(x)| \le C$.

articles.title: Set integrals of the path expectation
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let
$(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a filtration of the σ-algebra of $\Omega$ indexed by
$\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, and let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real process such that each $B_t$ is
$\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable and, for all $u \le t$, the increment $B_t - B_u$ is independent of
$\mathcal{F}_u$ under $\mu$. Let $s \ge 0$, let $Y$ be a measurable real function on paths
$\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $|Y(p)| \le C$ for every path $p$, and let
$A \in \mathcal{F}_s$. Write $\nu_s$ for the law under $\mu$ of
$\omega \mapsto (t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega))$,
$E_s Y(x) = \int Y(t \mapsto x + f(t))\, d\nu_s(f)$ for $x \in \mathbb{R}$, and
$\theta_s \omega$ for the shifted path $t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega)$. Then

$$
\int_A E_s Y(B_s(\omega))\, d\mu(\omega)
  = \int_A Y^+(\theta_s \omega)\, d\mu(\omega) - \int_A Y^-(\theta_s \omega)\, d\mu(\omega),
$$

where $Y^+ = \max(Y, 0)$, $Y^- = \max(-Y, 0)$, and each integral on the right is the integral of
a nonnegative function, taken in $[0, \infty]$ and then converted to a real number.

articles.title: Time-dependent path expectation
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\Omega$, let
$(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real process on $\Omega$ indexed by $t \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, let
$s \ge 0$, and let $\nu_s$ be the law under $\mu$ (the pushforward of $\mu$) of the centered
shifted path $\omega \mapsto (t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega))$. For a real function $Y$
on paths $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the path expectation is the
Bochner integral $\int Y(t \mapsto x + f(t))\, d\nu_s(f)$, which is $0$ when the integrand is
not integrable.

This value can depend on $s$; it is the generic time-dependent expectation.

articles.title: Translating the centered future path recovers the shifted path
articles.statement:
For a real process
$(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ on $\Omega$ indexed by $t \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, a time $s \ge 0$ and
$\omega \in \Omega$, translating the centered shifted path
$t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega)$ by the constant $B_s(\omega)$ gives the shifted path
$t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega)$.

articles.title: Translating a path by a constant
articles.statement:
The map sending a pair $(x, f)$, with
$x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $f : \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}$, to the path $t \mapsto x + f(t)$.

articles.title: Inserting a larger element does not change the predecessor
articles.statement:
For a finite set
$T \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, call the largest element of $T$
strictly below $t$ (or $0$ if there is none) the predecessor of $t$ in $T$. Let
$S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be finite and let $t, a \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ with $t < a$.
Then the predecessor of $t$ in $S \cup \{a\}$ equals the predecessor of $t$ in $S$.

articles.title: Predecessor of a new maximum
articles.statement:
For a finite set $T \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and
$t \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, call the largest element of $T$ strictly below $t$ (or $0$ if there
is none) the predecessor of $t$ in $T$. Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be finite and let
$a \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ with $x < a$ for every $x \in S$. Then the predecessor of $a$ in
$S \cup \{a\}$ is the supremum of $S$ in $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, that is, its largest element, or $0$
if $S$ is empty.

articles.title: Predecessor of a time in a finite set
articles.statement:
For a finite set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and
$t \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, the predecessor of $t$ in $S$ is the largest element of $S$ strictly
below $t$, or $0$ if there is no such element.

articles.title: Shifted path of a process
articles.statement:
For a real-valued process $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ on $\Omega$
indexed by $t \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and a time $s \ge 0$, the shifted path is the map sending
$\omega \in \Omega$ to the path $t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega)$ in $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}}$.

articles.title: Independence of the centered future path from the present
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability
measure on $\Omega$, let $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a filtration indexed by
$\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, and let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real-valued process that is adapted (each
$B_t$ is $\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable) and has independent increments (for $u \le t$, the
increment $B_t - B_u$ is independent of $\mathcal{F}_u$ under $\mu$). Then for every $s \ge 0$,
$\mathcal{F}_s$ is independent under $\mu$ of the σ-algebra generated by the centered shifted
path $\omega \mapsto (t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega))$, where the path space
$\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}}$ carries the product σ-algebra.

articles.title: Independence of future increments from the present
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure
on $\Omega$, let $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a filtration indexed by $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, and
let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real-valued process that is adapted (each $B_t$ is
$\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable) and has independent increments (for $u \le t$, the increment
$B_t - B_u$ is independent of $\mathcal{F}_u$ under $\mu$). For a finite set
$S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and $t \in S$, let $t^-$ be the largest element of $S$ strictly
below $t$, or $0$ if there is none. Then for every $s \ge 0$ and every finite
$S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, $\mathcal{F}_s$ is independent under $\mu$ of the σ-algebra
generated by the events $\bigcap_{t \in S} \{B_{s+t} - B_{s+t^-} \in C_t\}$, where every
$C_t \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is Borel.

articles.title: Conditional expectation of a future path functional
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure
on $\Omega$, let $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a filtration indexed by $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, and
let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real-valued process that is adapted (each $B_t$ is
$\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable) and has independent increments (for $u \le t$, the increment
$B_t - B_u$ is independent of $\mathcal{F}_u$ under $\mu$). Fix $s \ge 0$ and let $\nu_s$ be the
law under $\mu$ of the centered shifted path $\omega \mapsto (t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) -
B_s(\omega))$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}}$ with the product σ-algebra. Let
$Y : \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}} \to \mathbb{R}$ be measurable with $|Y(p)| \le C$ for every
path $p$, for some real $C$, and for $x \in \mathbb{R}$ put
$\Phi_s(x) = \int Y(t \mapsto x + f(t)) \, d\nu_s(f)$. Then, $\mu$-almost everywhere,

$$\mathbb{E}_\mu\big[\, Y\big((B_{s+t})_{t \ge 0}\big) \bigm| \mathcal{F}_s \big] = \Phi_s(B_s).$$

The function $\Phi_s$ is computed from the law of the increments after time $s$, so it may
depend on $s$.

articles.title: Nonnegative integrals of future path functionals over present events
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a
probability measure on $\Omega$, let $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a filtration indexed by
$\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, and let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real-valued process that is adapted (each
$B_t$ is $\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable) and has independent increments (for $u \le t$, the
increment $B_t - B_u$ is independent of $\mathcal{F}_u$ under $\mu$). Fix $s \ge 0$ and let
$\nu_s$ be the law under $\mu$ of the centered shifted path
$\omega \mapsto (t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega))$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}}$
with the product σ-algebra. Then for every measurable
$Y : \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}} \to [0, \infty]$ and every $A \in \mathcal{F}_s$,

$$\int_A Y\big((B_{s+t}(\omega))_{t \ge 0}\big) \, d\mu(\omega)
= \int_A \int Y\big(t \mapsto B_s(\omega) + g(t)\big) \, d\nu_s(g) \, d\mu(\omega),$$

where all integrals are Lebesgue integrals of $[0, \infty]$-valued functions.

articles.title: Bounded integrals of future path functionals over present events
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a
probability measure on $\Omega$, let $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a filtration indexed by
$\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, and let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real-valued process that is adapted (each
$B_t$ is $\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable) and has independent increments (for $u \le t$, the
increment $B_t - B_u$ is independent of $\mathcal{F}_u$ under $\mu$). Fix $s \ge 0$ and let
$\nu_s$ be the law under $\mu$ of the centered shifted path
$\omega \mapsto (t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega))$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}}$
with the product σ-algebra. Let $Y : \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}} \to \mathbb{R}$ be
measurable with $|Y(p)| \le C$ for every path $p$, for some real $C$, and for $x \in \mathbb{R}$
put $\Phi_s(x) = \int Y(t \mapsto x + f(t)) \, d\nu_s(f)$. Then for every $A \in \mathcal{F}_s$,

$$\int_A Y\big((B_{s+t}(\omega))_{t \ge 0}\big) \, d\mu(\omega)
= \int_A \Phi_s(B_s(\omega)) \, d\mu(\omega).$$

articles.title: Rectangles of a Borel set and a path cylinder form a π-system
articles.statement:
Consider the subsets of
$\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}}$ of the form
$U \times \bigcap_{t \in S} \{f \in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}} : f(t) \in V_t\}$, where
$U \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is Borel, $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is finite and every
$V_t \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is Borel. They form a π-system: whenever two of them have nonempty
intersection, the intersection is again of this form.

articles.title: Path cylinders form a π-system
articles.statement:
Consider the subsets of $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}}$
of the form $\bigcap_{t \in S} \{f : f(t) \in C_t\}$, where $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is
finite and every $C_t \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is Borel. They form a π-system: whenever two of them
have nonempty intersection, the intersection is again of this form.

articles.title: Measurability of the centered shifted path
articles.statement:
Let $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a
filtration on a measurable space $\Omega$ indexed by $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, and let
$(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real-valued process adapted to it (each $B_t$ is
$\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable). Then for every $s \ge 0$ the map
$\omega \mapsto (t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega))$ from $\Omega$ to
$\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}}$, with the product σ-algebra, is measurable.

articles.title: Measurability of an increment in the increment σ-algebra
articles.statement:
Let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a
real-valued process on $\Omega$, let $s \ge 0$, and let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be
finite; for $t \in S$ let $t^-$ be the largest element of $S$ strictly below $t$, or $0$ if there
is none. Then for every $t \in S$, the increment $\omega \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) -
B_{s+t^-}(\omega)$ is measurable with respect to the σ-algebra generated by the events
$\bigcap_{u \in S} \{B_{s+u} - B_{s+u^-} \in C_u\}$, where every $C_u \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is
Borel.

articles.title: Measurability of an increment before a given time
articles.statement:
Let $B = (B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real
process on a measurable space $\Omega$, adapted to a filtration $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ of its
σ-algebra, let $S$ be a finite set of nonnegative reals and let $s, t, u \ge 0$. Write $p_S(t)$
for the largest element of $S$ strictly below $t$, or $0$ if there is none. If $s + t \le s + u$
and $s + p_S(t) \le s + u$, then the increment $B_{s+t} - B_{s+p_S(t)}$ is
$\mathcal{F}_{s+u}$-measurable.

articles.title: Measurability of the increments
articles.statement:
Let $B = (B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real process on a
measurable space $\Omega$, adapted to a filtration $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ of its σ-algebra.
For every finite set $S$ of nonnegative reals and all $s, t \ge 0$, the increment
$B_{s+t} - B_{s+p_S(t)}$ is measurable, where $p_S(t)$ is the largest element of $S$ strictly
below $t$, or $0$ if there is none.

articles.title: Measurability of the pair map
articles.statement:
Let $B = (B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real process on a
measurable space $\Omega$, adapted to a filtration $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ of its σ-algebra,
and give the space $\mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)}$ of real paths indexed by $t \ge 0$ the product
σ-algebra. For every $s \ge 0$, the map from $\Omega$ to
$\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)}$ sending $\omega$ to the pair of $B_s(\omega)$ and the
centered shifted path $t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega)$ is measurable.

articles.title: The path expectation is measurable in the starting point
articles.statement:
Let $B = (B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a
real process on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, let $s \ge 0$, and let $\nu_s$ be the law of
the centered shifted path $t \mapsto B_{s+t} - B_s$ on the space $\mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)}$ of
real paths indexed by $t \ge 0$, with its product σ-algebra. For every measurable
$Y : \mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)} \to \mathbb{R}$, the function $x \mapsto \int Y(x + f) \, d\nu_s(f)$
on $\mathbb{R}$ is measurable, where $x + f$ is the path $t \mapsto x + f(t)$.

articles.title: Translation of paths is measurable
articles.statement:
Give the space $\mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)}$ of real paths
indexed by $t \ge 0$ the product σ-algebra. The map from
$\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)}$ to $\mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)}$ sending $(x, f)$ to the
path $t \mapsto x + f(t)$ is measurable.

articles.title: Measurability of the shifted path
articles.statement:
Let $B = (B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real process on a
measurable space $\Omega$, adapted to a filtration $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ of its σ-algebra,
and give the space $\mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)}$ of real paths indexed by $t \ge 0$ the product
σ-algebra. For every $s \ge 0$, the map from $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)}$ sending
$\omega$ to the path $t \mapsto B_{s+t}(\omega)$ is measurable.

Each coordinate $B_{s+t}$ is $\mathcal{F}_{s+t}$-measurable, hence measurable.

articles.title: Nonnegative translated integrals against the centered law are measurable
articles.statement:
Let
$B = (B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real process on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, let $s \ge 0$,
and let $\nu_s$ be the law of the centered shifted path $t \mapsto B_{s+t} - B_s$ on the space
$\mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)}$ of real paths indexed by $t \ge 0$, with its product σ-algebra. For
every measurable $Y : \mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)} \to [0, \infty]$, the function
$x \mapsto \int Y(x + g) \, d\nu_s(g)$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is measurable, where $x + g$ is the path
$t \mapsto x + g(t)$.

articles.title: Section measures of the centered law are measurable
articles.statement:
Let $B = (B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real
process on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$, let $s \ge 0$, and let $\nu_s$ be the law of the
centered shifted path $t \mapsto B_{s+t} - B_s$ on the space $\mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)}$ of real
paths indexed by $t \ge 0$, with its product σ-algebra. For every measurable set
$T \subseteq \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^{[0, \infty)}$, the function
$x \mapsto \nu_s(\{f : (x, f) \in T\})$ from $\mathbb{R}$ to $[0, \infty]$ is measurable.

articles.title: Centered cylinders lie in the increment σ-algebra
articles.statement:
Let $B = (B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real
process on a measurable space $\Omega$, let $s \ge 0$ and let $S$ be a finite set of nonnegative
reals. For $u \ge 0$ let $p_S(u)$ be the largest element of $S$ strictly below $u$, or $0$ if
there is none, and let $\Delta_u = B_{s+u} - B_{s+p_S(u)}$. Let $\mathcal{G}_S$ be the σ-algebra
on $\Omega$ generated by the sets $\bigcap_{u \in S} \{\omega : \Delta_u(\omega) \in E_u\}$ for
families $(E_u)_{u \ge 0}$ of measurable subsets of $\mathbb{R}$. Then for every family
$(C_t)_{t \ge 0}$ of measurable subsets of $\mathbb{R}$, the set
$\bigcap_{t \in S} \{\omega : B_{s+t}(\omega) - B_s(\omega) \in C_t\}$ belongs to
$\mathcal{G}_S$.

articles.title: Events of a single increment lie in the increment σ-algebra
articles.statement:
Let $B = (B_t)_{t \ge 0}$
be a real process on a measurable space $\Omega$, let $s \ge 0$ and let $S$ be a finite set of
nonnegative reals. For $u \ge 0$ let $p_S(u)$ be the largest element of $S$ strictly below $u$,
or $0$ if there is none, and let $\Delta_u = B_{s+u} - B_{s+p_S(u)}$. Let $\mathcal{G}_S$ be the
σ-algebra on $\Omega$ generated by the sets
$\bigcap_{u \in S} \{\omega : \Delta_u(\omega) \in E_u\}$ for families $(E_u)_{u \ge 0}$ of
