measurable subsets of $\mathbb{R}$. Then for every $t \in S$ and every measurable
$D \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, the event $\{\omega : \Delta_t(\omega) \in D\}$ belongs to
$\mathcal{G}_S$.

articles.title: Evaluation events are measurable
articles.statement:
For every $t \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and every Borel set
$D \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, the set of paths $f : \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f(t) \in D$
is measurable for the product σ-algebra on the space of all such paths.

articles.title: Past events factor against grid increments
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure and let
$(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real process adapted to a filtration $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ such that
$B_t - B_s$ is independent of $\mathcal{F}_s$ under $\mu$ whenever $s \le t$. Let
$s \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be finite. For $t \in S$ let
$\Delta_t = B_{s+t} - B_{s+t^-}$, where $t^-$ is the largest element of $S$ strictly below $t$, or
$0$ if there is none. Then for every family $(C_t)_{t \ge 0}$ of Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ and
every $A \in \mathcal{F}_s$,

$$\mu\Big(A \cap \bigcap_{t \in S} \{\Delta_t \in C_t\}\Big)
= \mu(A)\,\mu\Big(\bigcap_{t \in S} \{\Delta_t \in C_t\}\Big).$$

The proof is induction on $S$ by its maximum element $a$: the increment $\Delta_a$ is independent
of $\mathcal{F}_{s + a^-}$, which contains both $A$ and the earlier increments.

articles.title: Measurable rectangles lie in the σ-algebra of cylinder rectangles
articles.statement:
Let
$U \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a Borel set and let $V$ be a set of paths
$f : \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}$ that is measurable for the product σ-algebra. Then
$U \times V$ belongs to the σ-algebra on $\mathbb{R} \times (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R})$
generated by the cylinder rectangles, the sets $U' \times \{f : f(t) \in C_t \text{ for all }
t \in S\}$ with $U'$ Borel, $S$ a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and $(C_t)_{t \ge 0}$ a
family of Borel sets.

This is Dynkin's theorem applied to the cylinder π-system on path space.

articles.title: The pair-section identity for measurable sets
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure and
let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real process adapted to a filtration $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ such
that $B_t - B_s$ is independent of $\mathcal{F}_s$ under $\mu$ whenever $s \le t$. Fix
$s \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, let $W^s$ be the centered shifted path $t \mapsto B_{s+t} - B_s$ and
let $\nu_s$ be its law under $\mu$. Then for every set
$T \subseteq \mathbb{R} \times (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R})$ that is measurable for the
product σ-algebra and every $A \in \mathcal{F}_s$,

$$\mu\big(A \cap \{(B_s, W^s) \in T\}\big)
= \int_A \nu_s\big(\{f : (B_s(\omega), f) \in T\}\big)\,d\mu(\omega).$$

The proof is Dynkin's theorem over cylinder rectangles.

articles.title: The pair identity on cylinder rectangles
articles.statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure and let
$(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a real process adapted to a filtration $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t \ge 0}$ such that
$B_t - B_s$ is independent of $\mathcal{F}_s$ under $\mu$ whenever $s \le t$. Fix
$s \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, let $W^s$ be the centered shifted path $t \mapsto B_{s+t} - B_s$ and
let $\nu_s$ be its law under $\mu$. Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be Borel, let
$S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be finite, let $(V_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}$,
and let $R = U \times \{f : f(t) \in V_t \text{ for all } t \in S\}$. Then for every
$A \in \mathcal{F}_s$,

$$\mu\big(A \cap \{(B_s, W^s) \in R\}\big)
= \int_A \nu_s\big(\{f : (B_s(\omega), f) \in R\}\big)\,d\mu(\omega).$$

The left side factors by the independence of $W^s$ from $\mathcal{F}_s$, and the section on the
right is empty unless $B_s(\omega) \in U$.

articles.title: Cylinders generate the product σ-algebra on path space
articles.statement:
The product σ-algebra on the space
of paths $f : \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}$ equals the σ-algebra generated by the cylinders,
the sets $\{f : f(t) \in C_t \text{ for all } t \in S\}$ with $S$ a finite subset of
$\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and $(C_t)_{t \ge 0}$ a family of Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Cylinder rectangles generate the product σ-algebra
articles.statement:
The product σ-algebra on
$\mathbb{R} \times (\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R})$, where the path space carries its product
σ-algebra, equals the σ-algebra generated by the cylinder rectangles, the sets
$U \times \{f : f(t) \in V_t \text{ for all } t \in S\}$ with $U$ Borel, $S$ a finite subset of
$\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and $(V_t)_{t \ge 0}$ a family of Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}$.

articles.title: Telescoping sum of grid increments
articles.statement:
Let $(B_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a family of real functions
on $\Omega$, let $s \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ be a nonempty
finite set. For $u \in S$ let $\Delta_u = B_{s+u} - B_{s+u^-}$, where $u^-$ is the largest element
of $S$ strictly below $u$, or $0$ if there is none. Then for every $\omega \in \Omega$,
$\sum_{u \in S} \Delta_u(\omega) = B_{s + \max S}(\omega) - B_s(\omega)$.

articles.title: Transition law
articles.statement:
For the stationary OU process and `s ≤ t`, the conditional law of
`X t` given `X s = x` is `N(e^{-θ(t-s)} x, (σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θ(t-s)}))` for almost every
`x`.

articles.title: Conditional law of a Gaussian process at one time given another
articles.statement:
For a centered Gaussian process with `cov(X s, X t) = c Var(X s)`, the conditional law of
`X t` given `X s = x` is `N(c x, Var(X t) - c² Var(X s))` for almost every `x`.

articles.title: Transition law
articles.statement:
For the OU process started at `0` and `s ≤ t`, the conditional law of
`X t` given `X s = x` is `N(e^{-θ(t-s)} x, (σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θ(t-s)}))` for almost every
`x`.

articles.title: Mean reversion
articles.statement:
For the stationary OU process and `s ≤ t`,
`E[X t | F s] = e^{-θ(t-s)} X s`, where `F` is the natural filtration of `X`.

articles.title: Conditional expectation of a Gaussian process given its past
articles.statement:
For a centered Gaussian process with `cov(X u, X t) = c cov(X u, X s)` for all `u ≤ s`,
the conditional expectation of `X t` given the natural filtration at `s` is `c X s`.

articles.title: Mean reversion
articles.statement:
For the OU process started at `0` and `s ≤ t`,
`E[X t | F s] = e^{-θ(t-s)} X s`, where `F` is the natural filtration of `X`.

articles.title: Continuity of the pathwise Langevin solution
articles.statement: The pathwise solution is continuous when the driving path is.

articles.title: Uniqueness
articles.statement:
A continuous solution of `x t = x₀ - θ ∫_0^t x + σ (w t - w 0)` on
`t ≥ 0` equals `ouPathSolution θ σ x₀ w` there.

articles.title: The Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process from zero starts at zero
articles.statement: The OU process of `IsOrnsteinUhlenbeckFromZero` starts at `0` almost surely.

articles.title: Existence of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at zero
articles.statement: An Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0` exists for every `θ > 0` and `σ`.

articles.title: Existence of a pre-Brownian motion on path space
articles.statement:
There is a probability measure on paths `ℝ≥0 → ℝ` under which the coordinate process is a
pre-Brownian motion (Kolmogorov extension of the Brownian finite-dimensional laws).

articles.title: Existence of the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
articles.statement: A stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process exists for every `θ > 0` and `σ`.

articles.title: Stationary law
articles.statement: Each `X t` of a stationary OU process is `N(0, σ² / (2θ))`.

articles.title: One-time law of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process from zero
articles.statement:
The one-time law of the OU process started at `0`:
`X t ~ N(0, (σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θt}))`.

articles.title: Covariance of the Wiener integrals
articles.statement:
**Covariance of the Wiener integrals** `I_t = ∫_0^t e^{θu} dB_u`: for a pre-Brownian motion
`B` adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past and `θ ≠ 0`,
`E[I_s I_t] = (e^{2θ (s ∧ t)} - 1) / (2θ)`, by the martingale property and the Itô isometry.

articles.title: The pathwise Langevin solution driven by Brownian motion is Gaussian
articles.statement:
For a Brownian
motion `B`, `θ ≠ 0`, any real `σ`, and a start `X₀ ~ N(0, v)` independent of `B`, the process
`X t = ouPathSolution θ σ X₀ B t` (`t ≥ 0`) is a Gaussian process with `E[X t] = 0` and
`cov[X s, X t] = e^{-θ(s+t)} (v + σ² (e^{2θ (s ∧ t)} - 1) / (2θ))` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991,
Section 5.6).

articles.title: Construction (Doob 1942)
articles.statement:
The time change `σ e^{-θt} B((e^{2θt} - 1)/(2θ))` of a
pre-Brownian motion is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0`.

articles.title: The pathwise Langevin solution is an OU process
articles.statement:
Driven by a Brownian motion and started
at `0`, `ouPathSolution` is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991,
Section 5.6). No filtration and no measurability of the coordinates of `B` is assumed.

articles.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at zero
articles.statement:
`X` is an **Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0`** with rate `θ > 0` and noise
amplitude `σ` under `P`: a centered Gaussian process with covariance `ouCovariance θ σ`.
Only the finite-dimensional laws are fixed (no path regularity).

articles.title: Stationary start
articles.statement:
Driven by a Brownian motion `B` and started from `X₀ ~ N(0, σ²/(2θ))`
independent of `B`, `ouPathSolution` is a stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
(Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 5.6).

articles.title: Construction (Doob 1942)
articles.statement:
The time change `σ e^{-θt} B(e^{2θt}/(2θ))` of a
pre-Brownian motion is a stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process.

articles.title: Stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
articles.statement:
`X` is a **stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process** with rate `θ > 0` and noise
amplitude `σ` under `P`: a centered Gaussian process with covariance
`ouStationaryCovariance θ σ`. Only the finite-dimensional laws are fixed.

articles.title: Elementary Itô integrals agree for modifications
articles.statement:
Elementary Itô integrals against two modifications of the same process agree almost
surely.

articles.title: Gaussian process laws are determined by mean and covariance
articles.statement:
The finite-dimensional laws of a real Gaussian process are determined by its mean and
covariance functions: two Gaussian processes with the same means and covariances (possibly on
different probability spaces) have the same finite-dimensional laws.

articles.title: Strict stationarity
articles.statement:
Every finite-dimensional law of a stationary OU process is
invariant under time shifts.

articles.title: Adjoining an independent Gaussian variable
articles.statement:
If `X₀` is a real Gaussian random variable
independent of the real Gaussian process `B`, the process indexed by `Option T` that is `X₀` at
`none` and `B t` at `some t` is a Gaussian process.

articles.title: Doob's clock for the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process from zero
articles.statement:
Doob's clock `τ t = (e^{2θt} - 1)/(2θ)` for the process started at `0`. The value is
nonnegative for every real `θ`, so `Real.toNNReal` only changes its type.

articles.title: Symmetry of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck covariance
articles.statement: The OU covariance is symmetric.

articles.title: Variance of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at zero
articles.statement: The variance of the OU process started at `0`: `(σ² / (2θ)) (1 - e^{-2θt})`.

articles.title: Covariance of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at zero
articles.statement:
The covariance function of the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process started at `0`:
`(σ² / (2θ)) (e^{-θ|t-s|} - e^{-θ(t+s)})` (Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Section 5.6). It is meant
for `θ > 0` and times `s, t ≥ 0`; at `θ = 0` the division by zero makes it `0`.

articles.title: Doob's time change of Brownian motion
articles.statement: Doob's time change `t ↦ σ e^{-θt} B(τ t)` of a process `B`, with `τ = ouClock θ`.

articles.title: Pathwise Langevin equation
articles.statement:
For a continuous path `w` and every real `t`,
`ouPathSolution θ σ x₀ w` satisfies `x t = x₀ - θ ∫_0^t x + σ (w t - w 0)` (any real `θ`,
`σ`, `x₀`).

articles.title: Pathwise solution of the Langevin equation
articles.statement:
The explicit solution of the pathwise Langevin equation driven by a path `w`:
`e^{-θt} x₀ + σ (w t - e^{-θt} w 0 - θ ∫_0^t e^{-θ(t-u)} w u du)`. This is
`e^{-θt} x₀ + σ ∫_0^t e^{-θ(t-u)} dw(u)` after integration by parts (the Itô-integral form for a
Brownian path is a wanted statement).

articles.title: Doob's clock for the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
articles.statement: Doob's clock `t ↦ e^{2θt}/(2θ)` for the stationary process (positive for `θ > 0`).

articles.title: Variance of the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
articles.statement: The stationary variance `σ² / (2θ)`.

articles.title: Covariance of the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
articles.statement:
The covariance function of the stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process:
`(σ² / (2θ)) e^{-θ|t-s|}` (Uhlenbeck–Ornstein 1930). It is meant for `θ > 0`.

articles.title: Doob's stationary time change of Brownian motion
articles.statement: Doob's stationary time change `t ↦ σ e^{-θt} B(e^{2θt}/(2θ))` of a process `B`.

articles.title: Time shifts of a stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process
articles.statement: A time shift of a stationary OU process is a stationary OU process.

articles.title: Relaxation to stationarity
articles.statement:
For the process started at `0`,
`cov(X (s + h), X (t + h)) → (σ² / (2θ)) e^{-θ|t-s|}` as `h → ∞`.

articles.title: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck covariance converges to the stationary one
articles.statement: Shifting both times by `h → ∞` turns `ouCovariance` into `ouStationaryCovariance`.

articles.title: Processes with measurable coordinates are adapted to their natural filtration
articles.statement: A process with measurable coordinates is adapted to its natural filtration.

articles.title: Increments are independent of the past
articles.statement:
For a pre-Brownian motion with measurable
coordinates, each increment `B t - B s` (`s ≤ t`) is independent of the natural filtration at
time `s` (a consequence of `IsPreBrownianReal.indepFun_shift`, the weak Markov property).

articles.title: Second moment of the weighted quadratic-variation error
articles.statement:
For a pre-Brownian motion `B`
adapted to `F` with increments independent of the past, and a measurable weight `φ` bounded by
`C`, `E[(∑_{k < n} φ(B_{t_k}) ((ΔB_k)² - Δt))²] ≤ 2 C² t² / n` on the uniform partition
`t_k = t k / n` (`n ≥ 1`).

articles.title: Quadratic variation of Brownian motion
articles.statement:
**Quadratic variation of Brownian motion**, `[B]_t = t`: along the uniform partitions of
`[0, t]`, `∑_{k < n} (B (t (k + 1) / n) - B (t k / n))² → t` in `L²(P)`, for every pre-Brownian
motion `B` (no filtration and no measurability of the coordinates is assumed; Øksendal 2003,
Exercise 2.17; Karatzas–Shreve 1991, Theorem 1.5.8 treats continuous square-integrable
martingales in probability).

articles.title: Weighted quadratic variation of Brownian motion
articles.statement:
Under the hypotheses of
`integral_weightedQVError_sq_le`, `∑_{k < n} φ(B_{t_k}) ((ΔB_k)² - Δt) → 0` in `L²(P)`.

articles.title: Quadratic variation of Brownian motion in probability
articles.statement:
Along the uniform partitions of
`[0, t]`, `∑_{k < n} (B (t (k + 1) / n) - B (t k / n))² → t` in probability.

articles.title: Weighted quadratic-variation error of Brownian motion
articles.statement:
The weighted quadratic-variation error along the uniform partition of `[0, t]` into `n`
cells: `∑_{k < n} φ(B (t k / n)) ((B (t (k + 1) / n) - B (t k / n))² - t / n)`.
